events.description: The succession discussion confronts Lovelace with threatened continuity, diminishing bodily capacity and unanswered requests. Fear and sadness coexist with anticipation expressed in a concrete plan and trust visible in her reliance on William, Neale's work and the collaboration that Babbage can still offer. The depicted drawing exchange includes laughter and brief shared pleasure before breath restores the bodily constraint; low joy in this coarse succession-focused appraisal does not assert that those moments are joyless. Frustration at deferral is possible without making anger the whole episode, and no conspicuous new disgust or surprise governs it. The FEELS Cut is one authored composition of emotional attention with an unresolved remainder, distinct from wants and anticipated fulfillment. This is an attributed authored reading of Lovelace within the succession episode E20, not a measured psychological state or a claim of uniform attention throughout August. The August interval locates the episode at the existing date precision; it supplies neither duration weights nor a moment-by-moment emotional trajectory. It does not give Lovelace knowledge of the particular March lesson interruption or of later outcomes.

All twelve cases then agree with the independent results on two complete runs. The second run is opened card by card: Babbage briefly stops explaining and allows a clerk to find the relation in the recorded operation; Lovelace follows the trace; the foreman follows bearing heat and load; Halden follows time; and Davies withholds the independent answer until the apparatus value has been read. Most of each run's time goes to people rather than to the apparatus: each value is read aloud and entered by hand, and each result is transcribed and read back before the next case begins. The apparatus turns for less than an hour of the first morning.

Neale's hours have a cause outside the office. He keeps his post at an assurance office, which carries a pension, and will not leave it for an office a month old; his employer spares him ten hours a week, about 130 a quarter on paper, from which late sources, corrected preparations, customer questions and absence leave the 80 Halden will promise. Two men answer Halden's advertisement for a second checker; neither can yet challenge a prepared deck without Neale's supervision. Four packets at 40 hours need 160, and Lovelace says the number aloud when she asks Neale whether he can check them by the final dates.

events.boundary: The duplicate check is omitted. Halden authorizes Friday delivery after a single check, intending the independent comparison to follow on Monday, 10 April. The decision is attributable and was not mad
events.description:
The duplicate check is omitted. Halden authorizes Friday delivery after a single check, intending the independent comparison to follow on Monday, 10 April. The decision is attributable and was not made by the machine. [Source window: 7 Apr 1854; no finer instant asserted.]

Friday 7 April 1854. The Guardian deck is ready a little after nine with one mark in the checking column, Wills's own. Neale is behind the glass on the Lothbury comparison, due the same day, with perhaps six of his week's hours left; moving him would make Lothbury late. The wage envelopes lie filled on Halden's desk; Guardian's £180 deposit has paid for part of them and becomes returnable if the date passes. Lovelace's qualification lies on the shelf above the desk beside the test packet. Halden writes the exception in the ledger margin, 'Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date.', initials it, and tells Wills to release the cards: Mr Neale will compare the copy on Monday. The cards run from ten; by four the table has gone to Guardian in Lombard Street, and Neale has finished Lothbury, which leaves with both signatures. On Monday the third return arrives with a query and Neale's hours go to it; on Tuesday the fourth arrives. The Guardian line carries its one mark forward week by week, as other exceptions have, until the table is returned on 3 May.

Within the returned-table inquiry, Halden recognizes that he too felt relief when he found the configuration seal unbroken. Seeing Babbage attend only to the correct operation trace, he refuses to let that shared relief discharge the office's responsibility. This is newly authored interior detail within the existing inquiry, not an independent historical finding or a reassessment of any numerical Cut.

Guardian's acceptance practice is its own: Davies still has the ages from forty-seven onward recomputed by hand in every table Guardian buys, where the reserves are largest. The office sold a table and its two signatures, not relief from that practice; the returned figures disagree exactly where Davies's computers look.

Davies returns the packet cut along its far edge, its end with the office's green tape and seal left unopened, so that the table comes back exactly as it was delivered: evidence under clause eleven. The hand recomputation of the upper ages is Davies's standing check on every table Guardian buys.

Davies's covering letter keeps his dry register: he does not doubt the mechanism; Guardian did not purchase it. Chapter XII's 'But they bought the table' concedes his point.

events.boundary: The error is disclosed and corrected. Halden records the full trace and his own authorization; the office refunds £180 and spends £100 on recomputation and printing. Neale deliberately places Wills in
events.description:
The error is disclosed and corrected. Halden records the full trace and his own authorization; the office refunds £180 and spends £100 on recomputation and printing. Neale deliberately places Wills in the active reading role during correction and later puts his own name beneath that work. Babbage initially describes the failure as external to the Engine. [Source window: May--Dec 1854; no finer instant asserted.]

Within the already recorded four-day paired correction, Wills initially responds to Neale's interruption by rushing the line. Neale returns him to the position marked by the checking strip. After they exchange reading and copying roles, Wills asks again, audibly, for a figure he did not hear; Neale repeats it, and Wills enters it only after hearing it. This specific corrective conduct supports the existing reference evidence. It creates no additional transposition, delivery, independent qualification, or alteration to the mechanism.

When Babbage wants the response to say the mechanism made no error, Halden asks what Guardian purchased and answers it himself: the office was paid to stop that table leaving. In 1871 Charles names this as Halden's question.

events.description: Authored: the bounded apparatus as it works. events.description: In 1821, checking tables computed by hand with John Herschel and finding error after error, Babbage exclaims: 'I wish to God these calculations had been executed by steam.' Printed tables of the period carry errors of calculation, of transcription and of typesetting, and his engines are designed both to calculate and to print (automatic typesetting and stereotyped plates) so that no hand copies a figure between the machine and the page. The bounded apparatus of 1843 excludes printing, and people copy figures by hand at both ends (III, VIII). The returned table's error enters by a hand copying a figure (E23), the kind of error the engines were first designed to end, before the machine rather than after it. [Source window: 1821 to 1843; no finer instant asserted.]

events.description: On two occasions before the book's cutoff, a member of the House of Lords and a member of the House of Commons ask Babbage whether, if wrong figures are put into the machine, the right answers will come out. events.description: Authored: the office's four customers and what became of their tables. The fourth office (invented; large table; its return arrives Tuesday 11 April; delivered with both signatures in February 1855). So at the closure the customers have their money or their work (XI), and the ledger holds one refund.

events.boundary: Authored: the office's route from a customer's figures to a delivered table, with the check at each stage. (1) The customer's signed source sheet. (2) A preparer's copy reduced to the form the cards c
events.description: Authored: the office's route from a customer's figures to a delivered table, with the check at each stage. (1) The customer's signed source sheet. (2) A preparer's copy reduced to the form the cards carry; check: an independent comparison of the copy against the source by the checker, whose mark is the second signature. (3) The card order; check: the run trace against the declared sequence. (4) The run; check: the trace and the sealed configuration. (5) The results read from the register faces and transcribed by a clerk; check: read back against the faces before the next case. (6) Printing; check: the proof read against the transcription by the preparer. (7) Two signatures, preparer's and checker's, and delivery. Only stage 2's check compares the office's work with the customer's own figures, and it is the one the checker's hours limit. On 7 April 1854 it is the one waived; the transposition at stage 2 passes every later check because each later check compares the work with itself.

events.boundary: One supervised checking lesson is interrupted for accepted preparation work during March 1852.
events.description: During the four-contract preparations in March 1852, Halden finds Wills beside Neale with specimen sheets. A fresh copy of a card order Wills began that morning waits at the preparation desk; handing it to another preparer would require that person to learn its arrangement. Asked how much longer the lesson will take, Neale says they have not compared Wills’s copy yet. Halden directs Wills to finish the cards first and then return. Wills takes his pencil and ruler, leaving the specimen with Neale. By the time the cards are finished, Neale’s paid hours for that day are over. Halden places the unfinished lesson with the next day’s work and enters completed production in the week’s account. He regards this as postponement, not cancellation. This single authored allocation makes one mechanism of the training problem inspectable; it does not prove that every later lesson was interrupted or that qualification was impossible. These are specimen/provisional preparations, not final signed customer returns or independent checker capacity.

events.boundary: Wills answers factual questions about his self-comparison but falls silent when Halden asks who authorized release.
events.description: During the May 3 returned-table inquiry, Wills brings his ruler and pencil although asked only to attend, and keeps their ends aligned. He acknowledges reading to himself while Neale handled Lothbury, accepts Halden’s correction that this was not a comparison, but does not answer who instructed release. Halden dismisses him rather than completing the question, then opens his own ledger. This is the limit of what the scene establishes about Wills’s speech: the unanswered question and bodily gesture do not establish whether he forgot, feared accusation, protected the employer, or judged the answer pointless. The lesson’s ability to ask a source question therefore cannot be generalized to challenging an employer. The later reference request will make a meaningful comparison, not prove that this earlier silence had one settled cause.

events.boundary: In paired correction Wills shifts from rushing after an interruption to making a repetition request that Neale hears and answers.
events.description: Within the accepted four-day correction, Neale and Wills exchange reading and copying roles. When stopped, Wills first starts the line again faster: an earlier tendency to repair difficulty by smooth performance remains available. Neale locates the restart with the checking strip. Later Wills does not hear a figure; his first request is too soft and Neale continues. Wills places his pencil across the copy and asks audibly for the previous figure. Neale returns to it, and only then does Wills enter it. The development is relational and material: a recoverable place on the page, role exchange, a clear interruption and a responsive partner jointly let uncertainty alter the work. It remains supervised reciprocal correction, not independent-checker qualification. events.boundary: Wills learns, in supervised specimen checking, to leave a figure unresolved instead of supplying the expected answer.
events.description: Within Neale’s existing January 1852 lesson, Wills initially answers from the clear prepared copy while claiming to read the specimen source. Neale keeps the checking strip at the unresolved line and points to the different evidence. Wills puts his pencil down and admits that the source cannot be read. His brief wish that he had given the expected figure returns while Neale examines it: admitting uncertainty is socially difficult, not an effortless new disposition. Neale also cannot read it and explicitly permits the check to remain open. Wills asks for the original and marks the unresolved place before moving the strip. The teacher’s response makes this particular interruption workable. Whether the original is obtained remains unknown. This supervised lesson supplies no independently qualified checker or additional protected hours.

events.boundary: Actuarial checking in the life offices, 1821 to 1854: tables were recomputed by a second hand before a board relied on them, and an office's actuary answered for them. Griffith Davies (1788 to 1855),
events.description: Actuarial checking in the life offices, 1821 to 1854: tables were recomputed by a second hand before a board relied on them, and an office's actuary answered for them. Griffith Davies (1788 to 1855), who rose from a slate quarry to teaching mathematics in London, was the Guardian Assurance Company's first actuary and held the post until his death on 25 March 1855; the Institute of Actuaries was founded in London on 8 July 1848, with examinations and classes. Documented (MacTutor, Griffith Davies; Dictionary of Welsh Biography; Wikipedia, Institute of Actuaries). Davies's own practice in the Book, a hand recomputation of the ages from forty-seven on every table he buys, is authored within that documented practice.

At the existing reference encounter he can ask Halden for a fuller account while keeping his own copying error in it. These context-dependent changes do not define a monotone competence score or establish permanent confidence. His earlier learning, the unresolved specimen original, gaps between these episodes and later independent qualification remain unspecified.

concepts.boundary: A result complete of the object it declared and not of any larger design; stating the edge keeps its truth, and the pleasure of having made it, when the larger promise fails.
differentia: the claim names what it does not establish
the success and the failure of the same object are recorded together
the pleasure in the made thing does not wait for the larger design
direction_families: state the object a result is complete of, and what it is not complete of
concepts.label: completion of a bounded object

concepts.boundary: An exception recorded honestly as temporary and then carried forward by routine until its temporariness becomes permanent.
differentia: the exception is visible in the record, not hidden
what keeps it is a routine (the next date, the week's account), not concealment
direction_families: follow each recorded exception to the day it is closed, or to the day it is found
concepts.label: carried exception

direction_families: trace each witness to its source; count independent routes, not witnesses

concepts.boundary: A function that one person alone can perform or authorize, so that it stops when that person is absent; its singleness can be protected as authority or created as economy.
differentia: the function has no second holder who is competent, paid and authorized
the singleness may be guarded by the carrier or produced by others who do not pay for a second
direction_families: name who can perform the function, whose hours are paid for it, and who may refuse
concepts.label: sole carrier

concepts.boundary: A declared power to stop, refuse or reduce an undertaking, held by a named person or rule before the result is known and usable against the one who proposes; where the proposer is also the only one who may refuse, the right is nominal.
differentia: the stop is declared before anyone knows whether it will be wanted
someone other than the proposer can use it, or the proposer binds himself to it at a cost to himself
using it ends a stage or a claim, not necessarily the undertaking
direction_families: for each commitment, name who may stop it, whether they can, and what stopping costs them
concepts.label: a right to stop

events.boundary: What Lovelace's signature is in the compact. Under coverture a married woman could not make a contract in her own name before the Married Women's Property Acts (from 1870); documented (Wikipedia, Cove
events.description: What Lovelace's signature is in the compact. Under coverture a married woman could not make a contract in her own name before the Married Women's Property Acts (from 1870); documented (Wikipedia, Coverture; Britannica, Married Women's Property Acts). So her signature in the compact is not a party's: it is the compact's own rule, which the parties agree to be bound by, that no test result and no public claim may be made without it, an evidentiary authority inside the undertaking. Contracts and money are signed by Halden, Babbage and the subscriber trust's solicitor; her time and travel are negotiated inside a household whose legal powers are not hers (V).

events.boundary: The bounded trial passes. When a register first fails to clear, Davies's curiosity yields to the prospective stop he helped require; the incomplete run is voided and the protocol survives contact with
events.description:
The bounded trial passes. When a register first fails to clear, Davies's curiosity yields to the prospective stop he helped require; the incomplete run is voided and the protocol survives contact with desire. All twelve cases then agree with the independent results on two complete runs. The second run is opened card by card: Babbage briefly stops explaining and allows a clerk to find the relation in the recorded operation; Lovelace follows the trace; the foreman follows bearing heat and load; Halden follows time; and Davies withholds the independent answer until the apparatus value has been read. The final card, slowing shaft, held register values, sealed comparison case, and three unnecessary empty cycles make the success perceptible through the apparatus rather than through a declared emotion alone. Before any inquiry arrives, Babbage, Lovelace, and Halden briefly share the pleasure of seeing directed operations persist in matter. The event is a large positive shock because the principals had organized themselves around containing failure. [Source window: May 1851; no finer instant asserted.]

Most of each run's time goes to people rather than to the apparatus: each value is read aloud and entered by hand, and each result is transcribed and read back before the next case begins. The apparatus turns for less than an hour of the first morning.

events.boundary: Capacity is calculated. Halden's own ledger shows two independently checked jobs per quarter: 80 protected hours, at 40 per final packet. The prospective contracts use specimens while customers close
events.description:
Capacity is calculated. Halden's own ledger shows two independently checked jobs per quarter: 80 protected hours, at 40 per final packet. The prospective contracts use specimens while customers close their accounts at the end of 1853 and reconcile them through March 1854. Final signed returns become available no earlier than 1 April, with deliveries due in April--June 1854. Neale is already teaching Wills, but supervised practice consumes rather than adds independent hours. Lovelace accepts two jobs in that delivery quarter as the current service boundary. [Source window: Jan 1852; no finer instant asserted.]

During the already recorded supervised practice, Wills begins from the expected figure in a legible prepared copy. Neale redirects him to the specimen source. Wills admits that he cannot independently read one figure there; Neale also cannot read it and tells him to leave the check open. Wills asks whether to obtain the original and marks the unresolved place. This is a practice or specimen source during the existing training period, not a final signed April 1854 return. Obtaining and resolving the original remains unopened. The episode is evidence of supervised learning and source verification work; it supplies no independent checker-hours and does not establish that Wills is independently qualified.

Neale's hours have a cause outside the office. He keeps his post at an assurance office, which carries a pension, and will not leave it for an office a month old; his employer spares him ten hours a week, about 130 a quarter on paper, from which late sources, corrected preparations, customer questions and absence leave the 80 Halden will promise. Two men answer Halden's advertisement for a second checker; neither can yet challenge a prepared deck without Neale's supervision. Four packets at 40 hours need 160, and Lovelace says the number aloud when she asks Neale whether he can check them by the final dates.

The qualification begins in her usual close hand with two sentences: the 1851 trial established one frozen operation under prospective comparison, not the rate at which customer work could be prepared and independently checked, and the four obligations depended upon capacity not present when they were accepted. Below them the lines stand farther apart and each direction begins at the margin: accept no fifth; pay for Wills's instruction in hours of its own; before the first return arrives, name who checks when Mr Neale cannot. The first is kept. The second becomes her August plan and is deferred. The third is never answered: no second checker exists when the returns arrive on 1 April 1854.

The third direction is worded as a deputy: 'Before the first return arrives, name Mr Neale's deputy.' It asks for the provision she struck out for herself in 1844 (E06), which X lets her see.

events.description:
Succession is deferred. Lovelace confronts the parallel between her sole claim signature and Neale's sole checking authority. Looking at the deleted deputy provision, she asks William whether he would have signed, then admits she would not have let him. He declines competence for her work and offers no judgment on her refusal; recognition leaves her attachment to that authority unsettled. She makes the cost and function of checking succession explicit. While examining Babbage's proposed mechanical self-comparison, she distinguishes an Engine's power to carry supplied relations beyond one person's survey from judgment about the question, source, or purpose supplied to it. Their old collaborative speed briefly returns and consumes the bodily time William had asked her to protect; breath then restores the constraint. The design is narrowed from verification to internal comparison. Babbage supports delay and Halden, holding office expenditure authority, defers protected time and outside instruction intended to develop a second procedural checker. This omission, not her later death alone, creates the delivery vulnerability. [Source window: Aug 1852; no finer instant asserted.]

Wills has been receiving supervised lessons between preparations; the deferred proposal is to protect paid time away from preparation, with part of each week under Neale and part with an outside assurance clerk. Paying for that absence as well as instruction would lower immediate output. The stated approximate first-year cost remains £120. Halden’s deferral is not a claim that no instruction ever began, and no independent qualification or added checker hours are asserted.

events.description:
The office compresses work. Preparers overlap methods, specimen calculations, and corrections for four contracts while customers reconcile their closed accounts through March. Guardian's final signed return arrives on 1 April 1854 and replaces its provisional source. None of the four final signed returns is released before April; the other three dates remain unresolved within that month. Earlier checking marks cannot certify the final inputs. Neale starts the final comparisons in delivery order without the funded successor. The office has done real preparatory work while leaving the known final-check bottleneck unresolved. [Source window: Jan 1853--Apr 1854; no finer instant asserted.]

The Lothbury office's signed return also arrives on 1 April 1854, and its copy is ready first, so Neale begins the final comparisons with Lothbury. Guardian's and Lothbury's delivery dates both fall on Friday 7 April: the collision the four acceptances made possible. The third and fourth returns arrive on 10 and 11 April.

Guardian's and Lothbury's are the two small packets, each about a week of Neale's hours; the two large packets fall later in the quarter. That is why the two dates could be set for the first Friday, and why they could not both be kept.

Forty hours is the office's average verified packet. The two small packets need about a week of Neale's hours each at their final comparison; the two large ones need the rest of the quarter and more, so the four together still ask for about a hundred and sixty.

Friday 7 April 1854. The Guardian deck is ready a little after nine with one mark in the checking column, Wills's own. Neale is behind the glass on the Lothbury comparison, due the same day, with perhaps six of his week's hours left; moving him would make Lothbury late. The wage envelopes lie filled on Halden's desk; Guardian's £180 deposit has paid for part of them and becomes returnable if the date passes. Lovelace's qualification lies on the shelf above the desk beside the test packet. Halden writes the exception in the ledger margin, 'Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date.', initials it, and tells Wills to release the cards: Mr Neale will compare the copy on Monday. The cards run from ten; by four the table has gone to Guardian in Lombard Street, and Neale has finished Lothbury, which leaves with both signatures. On Monday the third return arrives with a query and Neale's hours go to it; on Tuesday the fourth arrives. The Guardian line carries its one mark forward week by week, as other exceptions have, until the table is returned on 3 May.

Within the returned-table inquiry, Halden recognizes that he too felt relief when he found the configuration seal unbroken. Seeing Babbage attend only to the correct operation trace, he refuses to let that shared relief discharge the office's responsibility. This is newly authored interior detail within the existing inquiry, not an independent historical finding or a reassessment of any numerical Cut.

Guardian's acceptance practice is its own: Davies still has the ages from forty-seven onward recomputed by hand in every table Guardian buys, where the reserves are largest. The office sold a table and its two signatures, not relief from that practice; the returned figures disagree exactly where Davies's computers look.

Davies returns the packet cut along its far edge, its end with the office's green tape and seal left unopened, so that the table comes back exactly as it was delivered: evidence under clause eleven. The hand recomputation of the upper ages is Davies's standing check on every table Guardian buys.

Davies's covering letter keeps his dry register: he does not doubt the mechanism; Guardian did not purchase it. Chapter XII's 'But they bought the table' concedes his point.

events.description: Authored: the bounded apparatus as it works. Limits: thirty card steps to a sequence, no conditional branch, no printing, values entered by hand and results transcribed by a clerk, and one frozen configuration in the sealed configuration register (parts, order, exclusions and the signed page), which may not be altered without a recorded decision. events.description: In 1821, checking tables computed by hand with John Herschel and finding error after error, Babbage exclaims: 'I wish to God these calculations had been executed by steam.' Printed tables of the period carry errors of calculation, of transcription and of typesetting, and his engines are designed both to calculate and to print (automatic typesetting and stereotyped plates) so that no hand copies a figure between the machine and the page. The bounded apparatus of 1843 excludes printing, and people copy figures by hand at both ends (III, VIII). The returned table's error enters by a hand copying a figure (E23), the kind of error the engines were first designed to end, before the machine rather than after it. [Source window: 1821 to 1843; no finer instant asserted.]

events.description:
Authored: in January 1852, before the articles are signed, Edward proposes putting £150, most of what the household has saved since the first venture, into the calculation office. He shows Margaret the articles, the stopping clauses and the first inquiries; he does not show her his capacity sheet, which that month allows two tables of the four the office means to accept. She keeps the household's accounts and asks what the office owes if it fails; he says the stopping clauses protect them. She agrees. It is his authorization, given with her consent to a risk she was not shown whole; he does not name it among his authorizations at the closure, and she does.

The later discovery distinguishes her financial assent to the stated articles from assent informed by the withheld capacity condition. His expectation of recruiting another checker is his contemporaneous hope, not achieved capacity or consent on her behalf.

events.boundary: At the closure Margaret finds the capacity sheet of January 1852 and names the authorization he never listed.
events.description:
Authored: the night before Halden writes the closure resolution, Margaret sorts the office's figures at the kitchen table into sums already owed, money still in hand and money a new circular only hoped to attract. Among the papers she finds his capacity sheet of January 1852, with Lady Lovelace's line marked twice, and names the authorization he never listed: 'You showed me the articles in January. Not this.' He had not. It is the household decision of January 1852 (event.book.halden.household-decision-1852-01) said aloud, by the one who carried its cost.

The disclosure and immediate incomplete response open into event.book.063.margaret.retains-condition and event.book.063.halden.domestic-participation. Margaret keeps the sheet beside her household book; Edward finally reads actual owed payments with her. This night precedes the closure resolution in1854, while the remaining obligations continue until the final dismantling of E27 inMarch1855. The retained envelope does not name an exact night.

events.description: Authored: Neale's hours from 1 to 11 April 1854. Saturday 1 April, Guardian's and Lothbury's signed returns arrive; Lothbury's copy is ready first. Monday 3 to Thursday 6, four of his ten released hours go to Lothbury's final comparison around his assurance post's own quarter-day accounts. Friday 7, a little after nine, he has about six hours left and needs them all to finish Lothbury by four; Guardian's final comparison, another ten, cannot also be done that week. Monday 10, his new week's hours go to the third office's query; Tuesday 11, the fourth return arrives. From then on he works to the nearest promised date, and a delivered table has none.

events.description: Authored: how ten hours a week become eighty a quarter. Released ten hours a week, a hundred and thirty in a thirteen-week quarter; late sources and corrected preparations take about twenty, customer questions about fifteen, ordinary absence about fifteen, leaving eighty protected hours, from which any teaching of Wills is also taken (IX). A packet's forty hours is Halden's planning average: a small table needs about twenty (ten of method checks with specimen figures before its return, ten of final comparison after it), a large one about sixty (twenty before, forty after). After 1 April 1854 the four final comparisons need a hundred hours against a quarter's eighty, and the two small ones, twenty hours, fall due in one week of ten.

events.description: Authored: the office's cash in hand by date, from the whole-account ledger (event.book.07r2.ledger.office; receipts £1,620, uses £1,620). In hand in February 1852 after the capital (£900) and the four deposits (£720): £1,620. End of 1852: £1,200 (wages £200, rent heat and light £70, preparation and cards £70, maintenance £50, administration £30). End of 1853: £735. On 31 March 1854: £631, and on Friday 7 April about £620 with the week's wage envelopes filled. After the return, the refund (£180) and the correction and reprinting (£100) leave £252 at the end of June 1854; £177 at the end of September; £105 at the end of December; nothing on 31 March 1855 after the last wages and closure and storage (£50). The refund does not stop the four tables being finished; it leaves nothing for a second checker or a continuing office without new capital.

events.boundary: Authored: the office's four customers and what became of their tables. Guardian Assurance (small table; due Friday 7 April 1854; delivered on one signature; returned 3 May; deposit refunded, the corre
events.description: Authored: the office's four customers and what became of their tables. Guardian Assurance (small table; due Friday 7 April 1854; delivered on one signature; returned 3 May; deposit refunded, the corrected table received as evidence). The Lothbury office (invented; small table; due the same Friday; delivered with both signatures at a quarter to four). The third office (invented; large table; its signed return arrives Monday 10 April with a query; delivered with both signatures in September 1854). The fourth office (invented; large table; its return arrives Tuesday 11 April; delivered with both signatures in February 1855). So at the closure the customers have their money or their work (XI), and the ledger holds one refund.

events.boundary: Authored: the office's route from a customer's figures to a delivered table, with the check at each stage. (1) The customer's signed source sheet. (2) A preparer's copy reduced to the form the cards c
events.description: Authored: the office's route from a customer's figures to a delivered table, with the check at each stage. (1) The customer's signed source sheet. (2) A preparer's copy reduced to the form the cards carry; check: an independent comparison of the copy against the source by the checker, whose mark is the second signature. (3) The card order; check: the run trace against the declared sequence. (4) The run; check: the trace and the sealed configuration. (5) The results read from the register faces and transcribed by a clerk; check: read back against the faces before the next case. (6) Printing; check: the proof read against the transcription by the preparer. (7) Two signatures, preparer's and checker's, and delivery. Only stage 2's check compares the office's work with the customer's own figures, and it is the one the checker's hours limit. On 7 April 1854 it is the one waived; the transposition at stage 2 passes every later check because each later check compares the work with itself.
provenance: Authored Book-branch revision 2026-09-29 (Claude Opus 5.5, private branch of canonical head e940f0fe); not historical evidence.

events.boundary: One supervised checking lesson is interrupted for accepted preparation work during March 1852.
events.description: During the four-contract preparations in March 1852, Halden finds Wills beside Neale with specimen sheets. A fresh copy of a card order Wills began that morning waits at the preparation desk; handing it to another preparer would require that person to learn its arrangement. Asked how much longer the lesson will take, Neale says they have not compared Wills’s copy yet. Halden directs Wills to finish the cards first and then return. Wills takes his pencil and ruler, leaving the specimen with Neale. By the time the cards are finished, Neale’s paid hours for that day are over. Halden places the unfinished lesson with the next day’s work and enters completed production in the week’s account. He regards this as postponement, not cancellation. This single authored allocation makes one mechanism of the training problem inspectable; it does not prove that every later lesson was interrupted or that qualification was impossible. These are specimen/provisional preparations, not final signed customer returns or independent checker capacity.

events.boundary: Wills answers factual questions about his self-comparison but falls silent when Halden asks who authorized release.
events.description: During the May 3 returned-table inquiry, Wills brings his ruler and pencil although asked only to attend, and keeps their ends aligned. He acknowledges reading to himself while Neale handled Lothbury, accepts Halden’s correction that this was not a comparison, but does not answer who instructed release. Halden dismisses him rather than completing the question, then opens his own ledger. This is the limit of what the scene establishes about Wills’s speech: the unanswered question and bodily gesture do not establish whether he forgot, feared accusation, protected the employer, or judged the answer pointless. The lesson’s ability to ask a source question therefore cannot be generalized to challenging an employer. The later reference request will make a meaningful comparison, not prove that this earlier silence had one settled cause.

events.boundary: In paired correction Wills shifts from rushing after an interruption to making a repetition request that Neale hears and answers.
events.description: Within the accepted four-day correction, Neale and Wills exchange reading and copying roles. When stopped, Wills first starts the line again faster: an earlier tendency to repair difficulty by smooth performance remains available. Neale locates the restart with the checking strip. Later Wills does not hear a figure; his first request is too soft and Neale continues. Wills places his pencil across the copy and asks audibly for the previous figure. Neale returns to it, and only then does Wills enter it. The development is relational and material: a recoverable place on the page, role exchange, a clear interruption and a responsive partner jointly let uncertainty alter the work. It remains supervised reciprocal correction, not independent-checker qualification. The reference encounter is already declared to follow that correction; no exact completion date is invented.

events.boundary: Wills learns, in supervised specimen checking, to leave a figure unresolved instead of supplying the expected answer.
events.description: Within Neale’s existing January 1852 lesson, Wills initially answers from the clear prepared copy while claiming to read the specimen source. events.description: Actuarial checking in the life offices, 1821 to 1854: tables were recomputed by a second hand before a board relied on them, and an office's actuary answered for them. Griffith Davies (1788 to 1855), who rose from a slate quarry to teaching mathematics in London, was the Guardian Assurance Company's first actuary and held the post until his death on 25 March 1855; the Institute of Actuaries was founded in London on 8 July 1848, with examinations and classes. Documented (MacTutor, Griffith Davies; Dictionary of Welsh Biography; Wikipedia, Institute of Actuaries). Davies's own practice in the Book, a hand recomputation of the ages from forty-seven on every table he buys, is authored within that documented practice.

the pleasure in the made thing does not wait for the larger design

concepts.boundary: A declared power to stop, refuse or reduce an undertaking, held by a named person or rule before the result is known and usable against the one who proposes; where the proposer is also the only one who may refuse, the right is nominal.

events.boundary: What Lovelace's signature is in the compact. Under coverture a married woman could not make a contract in her own name before the Married Women's Property Acts (from 1870); documented (Wikipedia, Cove
events.description: What Lovelace's signature is in the compact. Under coverture a married woman could not make a contract in her own name before the Married Women's Property Acts (from 1870); documented (Wikipedia, Coverture; Britannica, Married Women's Property Acts). So her signature in the compact is not a party's: it is the compact's own rule, which the parties agree to be bound by, that no test result and no public claim may be made without it, an evidentiary authority inside the undertaking. Contracts and money are signed by Halden, Babbage and the subscriber trust's solicitor; her time and travel are negotiated inside a household whose legal powers are not hers (V).

Within the household discussion of the unpaid call, Margaret asks Edward to let her finish the current line of her stationer's account before he spreads the venture ledger across it. He lifts the ledger and waits while she checks and marks her own entry. She then takes his ledger and examines the existing unpaid calls and wage obligation. The interaction opens Margaret's own working time and Edward's reliance upon it; it changes neither the earned-wages payment nor the suspension of new manufacture.

That evening Margaret puts the accounts aside and asks Edward to stay while she reads from an unnamed novel. They compare their recollection of two men in the book and laugh at the complication; Edward settles back in his chair while she begins a paragraph earlier. Their shared pleasure does not resolve the financial difficulty. The next morning Edward pays the earned wages and suspends the next stage as already recorded.

events.boundary: The bounded trial passes. When a register first fails to clear, Davies's curiosity yields to the prospective stop he helped require; the incomplete run is voided and the protocol survives contact with
events.description:
The bounded trial passes. When a register first fails to clear, Davies's curiosity yields to the prospective stop he helped require; the incomplete run is voided and the protocol survives contact with desire. All twelve cases then agree with the independent results on two complete runs. The second run is opened card by card: Babbage briefly stops explaining and allows a clerk to find the relation in the recorded operation; Lovelace follows the trace; the foreman follows bearing heat and load; Halden follows time; and Davies withholds the independent answer until the apparatus value has been read. The final card, slowing shaft, held register values, sealed comparison case, and three unnecessary empty cycles make the success perceptible through the apparatus rather than through a declared emotion alone. Before any inquiry arrives, Babbage, Lovelace, and Halden briefly share the pleasure of seeing directed operations persist in matter. The event is a large positive shock because the principals had organized themselves around containing failure. [Source window: May 1851; no finer instant asserted.]

Most of each run's time goes to people rather than to the apparatus: each value is read aloud and entered by hand, and each result is transcribed and read back before the next case begins. The apparatus turns for less than an hour of the first morning.

events.description: Authored: the trial's fault. The trace enters it as a timing fault in the reset, not in the arithmetic; because resetting is a declared operation and nothing in the configuration changes, the configuration stays frozen, and the claim is made only for the two complete runs (event.book.07r2.E14a).

events.description: The calculation office is constituted. In January 1852, in the solicitor's room where the compact was signed, Babbage puts in £650 and Halden £150, most of what the Halden household has saved since the first venture; the £100 left unspent from the construction account makes £900 of contributed capital. The apparatus comes to the office in its frozen configuration. The fourth article gives the acceptance of customer work to the manager. Lovelace reads the articles at Ockham and pencils beside the fourth: 'And who may refuse the manager?' Halden writes beneath it 'The account' and returns the page. She signs the article governing published claims and leaves the fourth without her name. events.boundary: Capacity is calculated. Halden's own ledger promises 80 protected independent checker-hours in the April--June delivery quarter and keeps two jobs as the current service boundary. Forty hour
events.description:
Capacity is calculated. Halden's own ledger promises 80 protected independent checker-hours in the April--June delivery quarter and keeps two jobs as the current service boundary. Forty hours is his planning average for all method checks and final comparison associated with a completed packet, not the final-comparison requirement of every packet. The prospective contracts use specimens while customers close their accounts at the end of 1853 and reconcile them through March 1854. Final signed returns become available no earlier than 1 April, with deliveries due in April--June 1854. Neale is already teaching Wills, but supervised practice consumes rather than adds independent hours. Lovelace accepts two jobs in that delivery quarter as the current service boundary. [Source window: Jan 1852; no finer instant asserted.]

During the already recorded supervised practice, Wills begins from the expected figure in a legible prepared copy. Neale redirects him to the specimen source. Wills admits that he cannot independently read one figure there; Neale also cannot read it and tells him to leave the check open. Wills asks whether to obtain the original and marks the unresolved place. This is a practice or specimen source during the existing training period, not a final signed April 1854 return. Obtaining and resolving the original remains unopened. The episode is evidence of supervised learning and source verification work; it supplies no independent checker-hours and does not establish that Wills is independently qualified.

Neale's hours have a cause outside the office. He keeps his post at an assurance office, which carries a pension, and will not leave it for an office a month old; his employer spares him ten hours a week, about 130 a quarter on paper, from which late sources, corrected preparations, customer questions and absence leave the 80 Halden will promise. Two men answer Halden's advertisement for a second checker; neither can yet challenge a prepared deck without Neale's supervision. Four packets at the planning average of 40 hours need 160 hours in total across method checks and final comparison, and Lovelace says that total aloud when she asks Neale whether he can check them by the final dates. The planning total alone does not state how many hours remain after the signed returns arrive.

events.description:
Lovelace files the capacity qualification. She states that demonstrated arithmetic is not demonstrated preparation, checking, correction, or recurring capacity. [Source window: Apr 1852; no finer instant asserted.]

The qualification begins in her usual close hand with two sentences: the 1851 trial established one frozen operation under prospective comparison, not the rate at which customer work could be prepared and independently checked, and the four obligations depended upon capacity not present when they were accepted. Below them the lines stand farther apart and each direction begins at the margin: accept no fifth; pay for Wills's instruction in hours of its own; before the first return arrives, name who checks when Mr Neale cannot. The first is kept. The second becomes her August plan and is deferred. The third is never answered: no second checker exists when the returns arrive on 1 April 1854.

The third direction is worded as a deputy: 'Before the first return arrives, name Mr Neale's deputy.' It asks for the provision she struck out for herself in 1844 (E06), which X lets her see.

events.boundary: Succession is deferred. Lovelace confronts the parallel between her sole claim signature and Neale's sole checking authority. Looking at the deleted deputy provision, she asks William whether he would
events.description:
Succession is deferred. Lovelace confronts the parallel between her sole claim signature and Neale's sole checking authority. Looking at the deleted deputy provision, she asks William whether he would have signed, then admits she would not have let him. He declines competence for her work and offers no judgment on her refusal; recognition leaves her attachment to that authority unsettled. She makes the cost and function of checking succession explicit. While examining Babbage's proposed mechanical self-comparison, she distinguishes an Engine's power to carry supplied relations beyond one person's survey from judgment about the question, source, or purpose supplied to it. Their old collaborative speed briefly returns and consumes the bodily time William had asked her to protect; breath then restores the constraint. The design is narrowed from verification to internal comparison. Babbage supports delay and Halden, holding office expenditure authority, defers protected time and outside instruction intended to develop a second procedural checker. This omission, not her later death alone, creates the delivery vulnerability. [Source window: Aug 1852; no finer instant asserted.]

Wills has been receiving supervised lessons between preparations; the deferred proposal is to protect paid time away from preparation, with part of each week under Neale and part with an outside assurance clerk. Paying for that absence as well as instruction would lower immediate output. The stated approximate first-year cost remains £120. Halden’s deferral is not a claim that no instruction ever began, and no independent qualification or added checker hours are asserted.

events.description:
The office compresses work. Preparers overlap methods, specimen calculations, and corrections for four contracts while customers reconcile their closed accounts through March. Guardian's final signed return arrives on 1 April 1854 and replaces its provisional source. None of the four final signed returns is released before April; the other three dates remain unresolved within that month. Earlier checking marks cannot certify the final inputs. Neale starts the final comparisons in delivery order without the funded successor. The office has done real preparatory work while leaving the known final-check bottleneck unresolved. [Source window: Jan 1853--Apr 1854; no finer instant asserted.]

The Lothbury office's signed return also arrives on 1 April 1854, and its copy is ready first, so Neale begins the final comparisons with Lothbury. Guardian's and Lothbury's delivery dates both fall on Friday 7 April: the collision the four acceptances made possible. The third and fourth returns arrive on 10 and 11 April.

Guardian's and Lothbury's are the two small packets, each about a week of Neale's hours; the two large packets fall later in the quarter. That is why the two dates could be set for the first Friday, and why they could not both be kept.

Forty hours is Halden's planning average for all checking work on a completed packet. Each small packet needs about twenty hours in total: ten of method checks with specimen figures before its signed return and ten of final comparison after it. Each large packet needs about sixty: twenty before its return and forty after. The four therefore need about a hundred and sixty checking hours in total, sixty before the final returns and a hundred after. The final comparisons require a hundred hours against eighty protected hours in the April--June delivery quarter; the two small packets require twenty of those final hours in the first week, against ten available. This is the static authored workload already specified in event.book.neale.hours.quarter; it asserts no simulated capacity trajectory.

events.description:
The duplicate check is omitted. Halden authorizes Friday delivery after a single check, intending the independent comparison to follow on Monday, 10 April. The decision is attributable and was not made by the machine. [Source window: 7 Apr 1854; no finer instant asserted.]

Friday 7 April 1854. The Guardian deck is ready a little after nine with one mark in the checking column, Wills's own. Neale is behind the glass on the Lothbury comparison, due the same day, with perhaps six of his week's hours left; moving him would make Lothbury late. The wage envelopes lie filled on Halden's desk; Guardian's £180 deposit has paid for part of them and becomes returnable if the date passes. Lovelace's qualification lies on the shelf above the desk beside the test packet. Halden writes the exception in the ledger margin, 'Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date.', initials it, and tells Wills to release the cards: Mr Neale will compare the copy on Monday. The cards run from ten; by four the table has gone to Guardian in Lombard Street, and Neale has finished Lothbury, which leaves with both signatures. On Monday the third return arrives with a query and Neale's hours go to it; on Tuesday the fourth arrives. The Guardian line carries its one mark forward week by week, as other exceptions have, until the table is returned on 3 May.

Within the returned-table inquiry, Halden recognizes that he too felt relief when he found the configuration seal unbroken. Seeing Babbage attend only to the correct operation trace, he refuses to let that shared relief discharge the office's responsibility. This is newly authored interior detail within the existing inquiry, not an independent historical finding or a reassessment of any numerical Cut.

Guardian's acceptance practice is its own: Davies still has the ages from forty-seven onward recomputed by hand in every table Guardian buys, where the reserves are largest. The office sold a table and its two signatures, not relief from that practice; the returned figures disagree exactly where Davies's computers look.

Davies returns the packet cut along its far edge, its end with the office's green tape and seal left unopened, so that the table comes back exactly as it was delivered: evidence under clause eleven. The hand recomputation of the upper ages is Davies's standing check on every table Guardian buys.

Davies's covering letter keeps his dry register: he does not doubt the mechanism; Guardian did not purchase it. Chapter XII's 'But they bought the table' concedes his point.

Within the already recorded four-day paired correction, Wills initially responds to Neale's interruption by rushing the line. Neale returns him to the position marked by the checking strip. When Babbage wants the response to say the mechanism made no error, Halden asks what Guardian purchased and answers it himself: the office was paid to stop that table leaving. In 1871 Charles names this as Halden's question.

events.description: Authored: the bounded apparatus as it works. Six registers of six decimal digits behind glass; a card reader taking operation and variable cards in a declared order; a mill that adds and subtracts only; a clearing lever to each register; a shared drive from the shaft beneath the floor. Limits: thirty card steps to a sequence, no conditional branch, no printing, values entered by hand and results transcribed by a clerk, and one frozen configuration in the sealed configuration register (parts, order, exclusions and the signed page), which may not be altered without a recorded decision. Nothing in it compares a supplied value with its source.

events.description: In 1821, checking tables computed by hand with John Herschel and finding error after error, Babbage exclaims: 'I wish to God these calculations had been executed by steam.' Printed tables of the period carry errors of calculation, of transcription and of typesetting, and his engines are designed both to calculate and to print (automatic typesetting and stereotyped plates) so that no hand copies a figure between the machine and the page. The bounded apparatus of 1843 excludes printing, and people copy figures by hand at both ends (III, VIII). The returned table's error enters by a hand copying a figure (E23), the kind of error the engines were first designed to end, before the machine rather than after it. [Source window: 1821 to 1843; no finer instant asserted.]

Authored: in January 1852, before the articles are signed, Edward proposes putting £150, most of what the household has saved since the first venture, into the calculation office. He shows Margaret the articles, the stopping clauses and the first inquiries; he does not show her his capacity sheet, which that month allows two tables of the four the office means to accept. It is his authorization, given with her consent to a risk she was not shown whole; he does not name it among his authorizations at the closure, and she does.

events.description: Authored: Neale's hours from 1 to 11 April 1854. Saturday 1 April, Guardian's and Lothbury's signed returns arrive; Lothbury's copy is ready first. Monday 3 to Thursday 6, four of his ten released hours go to Lothbury's final comparison around his assurance post's own quarter-day accounts. Friday 7, a little after nine, he has about six hours left and needs them all to finish Lothbury by four; Guardian's final comparison, another ten, cannot also be done that week. Monday 10, his new week's hours go to the third office's query; Tuesday 11, the fourth return arrives. From then on he works to the nearest promised date, and a delivered table has none.

events.description: Authored: how ten hours a week become eighty a quarter. Released ten hours a week, a hundred and thirty in a thirteen-week quarter; late sources and corrected preparations take about twenty, customer questions about fifteen, ordinary absence about fifteen, leaving eighty protected hours, from which any teaching of Wills is also taken (IX). A packet's forty hours is Halden's planning average: a small table needs about twenty (ten of method checks with specimen figures before its return, ten of final comparison after it), a large one about sixty (twenty before, forty after). After 1 April 1854 the four final comparisons need a hundred hours against a quarter's eighty, and the two small ones, twenty hours, fall due in one week of ten.

events.description: Authored: the office's cash in hand by date, from the whole-account ledger (event.book.07r2.ledger.office; receipts £1,620, uses £1,620). In hand in February 1852 after the capital (£900) and the four deposits (£720): £1,620. End of 1852: £1,200 (wages £200, rent heat and light £70, preparation and cards £70, maintenance £50, administration £30). End of 1853: £735. On 31 March 1854: £631, and on Friday 7 April about £620 with the week's wage envelopes filled. After the return, the refund (£180) and the correction and reprinting (£100) leave £252 at the end of June 1854; £177 at the end of September; £105 at the end of December; nothing on 31 March 1855 after the last wages and closure and storage (£50). The refund does not stop the four tables being finished; it leaves nothing for a second checker or a continuing office without new capital.

events.boundary: Authored: the office's four customers and what became of their tables. Guardian Assurance (small table; due Friday 7 April 1854; delivered on one signature; returned 3 May; deposit refunded, the corre
events.description: Authored: the office's four customers and what became of their tables. Guardian Assurance (small table; due Friday 7 April 1854; delivered on one signature; returned 3 May; deposit refunded, the corrected table received as evidence). The Lothbury office (invented; small table; due the same Friday; delivered with both signatures at a quarter to four). The third office (invented; large table; its signed return arrives Monday 10 April with a query; delivered with both signatures in September 1854). The fourth office (invented; large table; its return arrives Tuesday 11 April; delivered with both signatures in February 1855). So at the closure the customers have their money or their work (XI), and the ledger holds one refund.

events.boundary: Authored: the office's route from a customer's figures to a delivered table, with the check at each stage. (1) The customer's signed source sheet. (2) A preparer's copy reduced to the form the cards c
events.description: Authored: the office's route from a customer's figures to a delivered table, with the check at each stage. (1) The customer's signed source sheet. (2) A preparer's copy reduced to the form the cards carry; check: an independent comparison of the copy against the source by the checker, whose mark is the second signature. (3) The card order; check: the run trace against the declared sequence. (4) The run; check: the trace and the sealed configuration. (5) The results read from the register faces and transcribed by a clerk; check: read back against the faces before the next case. (6) Printing; check: the proof read against the transcription by the preparer. (7) Two signatures, preparer's and checker's, and delivery. Only stage 2's check compares the office's work with the customer's own figures, and it is the one the checker's hours limit. On 7 April 1854 it is the one waived; the transposition at stage 2 passes every later check because each later check compares the work with itself.
provenance: Authored Book-branch revision 2026-09-29 (Claude Opus 5.5, private branch of canonical head e940f0fe); not historical evidence.

source-quote:News reached Halden at the office before noon. He closed the preparation room
for the day and left the apparatus uncovered, because nobody could agree who
possessed the authority to alter the schedule. Neale stood beside four waiting
packets, his blank strip arrested beneath the first line. Babbage came late and
went first to the machine. He pressed his palm against the frame and left it

events.boundary: One supervised checking lesson is interrupted for accepted preparation work during March 1852.
events.description: During the four-contract preparations in March 1852, Halden finds Wills beside Neale with specimen sheets. A fresh copy of a card order Wills began that morning waits at the preparation desk; handing it to another preparer would require that person to learn its arrangement. Asked how much longer the lesson will take, Neale says they have not compared Wills’s copy yet. Halden directs Wills to finish the cards first and then return. Wills takes his pencil and ruler, leaving the specimen with Neale. By the time the cards are finished, Neale’s paid hours for that day are over. Halden places the unfinished lesson with the next day’s work and enters completed production in the week’s account. He regards this as postponement, not cancellation. This single authored allocation makes one mechanism of the training problem inspectable; it does not prove that every later lesson was interrupted or that qualification was impossible. These are specimen/provisional preparations, not final signed customer returns or independent checker capacity.

events.boundary: Wills answers factual questions about his self-comparison but falls silent when Halden asks who authorized release.
events.description: During the May 3 returned-table inquiry, Wills brings his ruler and pencil although asked only to attend, and keeps their ends aligned. He acknowledges reading to himself while Neale handled Lothbury, accepts Halden’s correction that this was not a comparison, but does not answer who instructed release. Halden dismisses him rather than completing the question, then opens his own ledger. This is the limit of what the scene establishes about Wills’s speech: the unanswered question and bodily gesture do not establish whether he forgot, feared accusation, protected the employer, or judged the answer pointless. The lesson’s ability to ask a source question therefore cannot be generalized to challenging an employer. The later reference request will make a meaningful comparison, not prove that this earlier silence had one settled cause.

events.boundary: In paired correction Wills shifts from rushing after an interruption to making a repetition request that Neale hears and answers.
events.description: Within the accepted four-day correction, Neale and Wills exchange reading and copying roles. When stopped, Wills first starts the line again faster: an earlier tendency to repair difficulty by smooth performance remains available. Neale locates the restart with the checking strip. Later Wills does not hear a figure; his first request is too soft and Neale continues. Wills places his pencil across the copy and asks audibly for the previous figure. Neale returns to it, and only then does Wills enter it. The development is relational and material: a recoverable place on the page, role exchange, a clear interruption and a responsive partner jointly let uncertainty alter the work. It remains supervised reciprocal correction, not independent-checker qualification. The reference encounter is already declared to follow that correction; no exact completion date is invented.

events.boundary: Wills learns, in supervised specimen checking, to leave a figure unresolved instead of supplying the expected answer.
events.description: Within Neale’s existing January 1852 lesson, Wills initially answers from the clear prepared copy while claiming to read the specimen source. Neale keeps the checking strip at the unresolved line and points to the different evidence. Wills puts his pencil down and admits that the source cannot be read. His brief wish that he had given the expected figure returns while Neale examines it: admitting uncertainty is socially difficult, not an effortless new disposition. Neale also cannot read it and explicitly permits the check to remain open. Wills asks for the original and marks the unresolved place before moving the strip. The teacher’s response makes this particular interruption workable. Whether the original is obtained remains unknown. This supervised lesson supplies no independently qualified checker or additional protected hours.

events.boundary: Wills helps another preparer use a familiar card arrangement; the colleague can continue alone while Wills’s own specimen source-comparison lesson remains unfinished.
events.description: On one unspecified afternoon during1853, another existing unnamed preparer asks Wills whether a card arrangement can be reused. Wills distinguishes the familiar arrangement from its old figures, uses a provisional table to show how its rows follow the form, and gives the colleague his ruler to try the next row. After Wills nods, the colleague moves his own pencil to the following row without asking. Wills smiles and draws his stool nearer. Neale remains occupied with sheets at his own desk. When his paid afternoon ends, he closes his book and tells Wills his specimen copy will be next time. Wills answers respectfully. The colleague continues alone; Wills brings back his ruler and leaves his own uncompleted specimen comparison open. This accepts observed preparation competence, useful assistance and one displaced learning opportunity, not hidden motives, permanent confidence, completed independent training, a qualified second checker or idle paid time. The provisional material is not an April1854 final signed customer return. The episode need not cause the later transposition and does not make helping wrong.

events.boundary: Actuarial checking in the life offices, 1821 to 1854: tables were recomputed by a second hand before a board relied on them, and an office's actuary answered for them. Griffith Davies (1788 to 1855),
events.description: Actuarial checking in the life offices, 1821 to 1854: tables were recomputed by a second hand before a board relied on them, and an office's actuary answered for them. Griffith Davies (1788 to 1855), who rose from a slate quarry to teaching mathematics in London, was the Guardian Assurance Company's first actuary and held the post until his death on 25 March 1855; the Institute of Actuaries was founded in London on 8 July 1848, with examinations and classes. Documented (MacTutor, Griffith Davies; Dictionary of Welsh Biography; Wikipedia, Institute of Actuaries). Davies's own practice in the Book, a hand recomputation of the ages from forty-seven on every table he buys, is authored within that documented practice.

events.description: Who could check a prepared table independently in these years. The life offices' senior clerks and actuaries, whose profession organized itself only in 1848 (the Institute of Actuaries, with its examinations and classes; documented, Wikipedia, Institute of Actuaries), held pensioned posts they did not leave for a month-old office; that Neale will not leave his is authored. The two men who answer Halden's advertisement cannot yet challenge a prepared set of cards without Neale's supervision (IX), and training them uses the hours it is meant to add. Money cannot buy a second Neale quickly: that is the market idea 2 rests on.

In this history it is the wider contraction behind the unpaid third call: in October 1847 the call brings six letters and no money, one from a subscriber who has failed (VII). events.description: The precision-engineering trade from the 1820s to 1851: the maker's custom that the tools he builds for a customer's work are his (Clement keeps the tools in 1833), the slow move from a master's hand towards gauges and stated tolerances, and the men trained in Clement's shop who carry it on. It is the custom Babbage learns from (event.book.babbage.clement-tools-1833) and the practice Whitworth's review applies to the reduced interfaces in 1844 (event.book.07r2.E05).

events.description: The English quarter days, Lady Day (25 March), Midsummer (24 June), Michaelmas (29 September) and Christmas (25 December), on which rents, wages and accounts were settled. Credit pressure slows the build. A wider contraction delays the next subscription call. Existing wages are paid, new work slows, and scope is not enlarged to attract money. [Source window: Oct 1847--Jun 1848; no finer instant asserted.]

Within the household discussion of the unpaid call, Margaret asks Edward to let her finish the current line of her stationer's account before he spreads the venture ledger across it. He lifts the ledger and waits while she checks and marks her own entry. She then takes his ledger and examines the existing unpaid calls and wage obligation. The interaction opens Margaret's own working time and Edward's reliance upon it; it changes neither the earned-wages payment nor the suspension of new manufacture.

That evening Margaret puts the accounts aside and asks Edward to stay while she reads from an unnamed novel. They compare their recollection of two men in the book and laugh at the complication; Edward settles back in his chair while she begins a paragraph earlier. Their shared pleasure does not resolve the financial difficulty. The next morning Edward pays the earned wages and suspends the next stage as already recorded.

events.boundary: The bounded trial passes. When a register first fails to clear, Davies's curiosity yields to the prospective stop he helped require; the incomplete run is voided and the protocol survives contact with
events.description:
The bounded trial passes. When a register first fails to clear, Davies's curiosity yields to the prospective stop he helped require; the incomplete run is voided and the protocol survives contact with desire. All twelve cases then agree with the independent results on two complete runs. The second run is opened card by card: Babbage briefly stops explaining and allows a clerk to find the relation in the recorded operation; Lovelace follows the trace; the foreman follows bearing heat and load; Halden follows time; and Davies withholds the independent answer until the apparatus value has been read. The final card, slowing shaft, held register values, sealed comparison case, and three unnecessary empty cycles make the success perceptible through the apparatus rather than through a declared emotion alone. Before any inquiry arrives, Babbage, Lovelace, and Halden briefly share the pleasure of seeing directed operations persist in matter. The event is a large positive shock because the principals had organized themselves around containing failure. [Source window: May 1851; no finer instant asserted.]

Most of each run's time goes to people rather than to the apparatus: each value is read aloud and entered by hand, and each result is transcribed and read back before the next case begins. The apparatus turns for less than an hour of the first morning.

events.boundary: The calculation office is constituted: £900 of capital, two signatures promised beneath each table, and acceptance of customer work given to the manager.
events.description: The calculation office is constituted. In January 1852, in the solicitor's room where the compact was signed, Babbage puts in £650 and Halden £150, most of what the Halden household has saved since the first venture; the £100 left unspent from the construction account makes £900 of contributed capital. The apparatus comes to the office in its frozen configuration. The articles copy the compact's stopping clauses and promise every customer two signatures beneath each table: the preparer's and an independent checker's. The fourth article gives the acceptance of customer work to the manager. Lovelace reads the articles at Ockham and pencils beside the fourth: 'And who may refuse the manager?' Halden writes beneath it 'The account' and returns the page. She signs the article governing published claims and leaves the fourth without her name. [Source window: Jan 1852; no finer instant asserted.]

events.boundary: Capacity is calculated. Halden's own ledger promises 80 protected independent checker-hours in the April--June delivery quarter and keeps two jobs as the current service boundary. Forty hour
events.description:
Capacity is calculated. Halden's own ledger promises 80 protected independent checker-hours in the April--June delivery quarter and keeps two jobs as the current service boundary. Forty hours is his planning average for all method checks and final comparison associated with a completed packet, not the final-comparison requirement of every packet. The prospective contracts use specimens while customers close their accounts at the end of 1853 and reconcile them through March 1854. Final signed returns become available no earlier than 1 April, with deliveries due in April--June 1854. Neale is already teaching Wills, but supervised practice consumes rather than adds independent hours. Lovelace accepts two jobs in that delivery quarter as the current service boundary. [Source window: Jan 1852; no finer instant asserted.]

During the already recorded supervised practice, Wills begins from the expected figure in a legible prepared copy. Neale redirects him to the specimen source. Wills admits that he cannot independently read one figure there; Neale also cannot read it and tells him to leave the check open. Wills asks whether to obtain the original and marks the unresolved place. This is a practice or specimen source during the existing training period, not a final signed April 1854 return. Obtaining and resolving the original remains unopened. The episode is evidence of supervised learning and source verification work; it supplies no independent checker-hours and does not establish that Wills is independently qualified.

Neale's hours have a cause outside the office. He keeps his post at an assurance office, which carries a pension, and will not leave it for an office a month old; his employer spares him ten hours a week, about 130 a quarter on paper, from which late sources, corrected preparations, customer questions and absence leave the 80 Halden will promise. Two men answer Halden's advertisement for a second checker; neither can yet challenge a prepared deck without Neale's supervision. Four packets at the planning average of 40 hours need 160 hours in total across method checks and final comparison, and Lovelace says that total aloud when she asks Neale whether he can check them by the final dates. The planning total alone does not state how many hours remain after the signed returns arrive.

He recalls being addressed as inventor in a customer's letter. Although he corrected the word in his reply, he had read the salutation twice. This is authored detail within the existing argument. No choice, authority, capacity, or estimate changes.

The reciprocal endorsement opens into event.book.063.halden.receives-endorsement and event.book.063.babbage.receives-corroboration. Different competencies make reassurance appear independent although both judgments still rest on the same trial. Capacity quantities, contracting authority, four commitments and final outcomes are unchanged.

events.description:
Lovelace files the capacity qualification. She states that demonstrated arithmetic is not demonstrated preparation, checking, correction, or recurring capacity. [Source window: Apr 1852; no finer instant asserted.]

The qualification begins in her usual close hand with two sentences: the 1851 trial established one frozen operation under prospective comparison, not the rate at which customer work could be prepared and independently checked, and the four obligations depended upon capacity not present when they were accepted. Below them the lines stand farther apart and each direction begins at the margin: accept no fifth; pay for Wills's instruction in hours of its own; before the first return arrives, name who checks when Mr Neale cannot. The first is kept. The second becomes her August plan and is deferred. The third is never answered: no second checker exists when the returns arrive on 1 April 1854.

The third direction is worded as a deputy: 'Before the first return arrives, name Mr Neale's deputy.' It asks for the provision she struck out for herself in 1844 (E06), which X lets her see.
