nodes.text:
During March the four preparations began to overlap. Wills's lessons continued
among them.

One afternoon Halden found him beside Neale with the specimen sheets. At the
preparation desk a card order waited for a fresh copy. Wills had begun it that
morning; another preparer would have to learn the arrangement before finishing
it.

“How much longer here?” Halden asked.

Neale kept the strip on the line. “We have not compared his copy yet.”

“The cards first, Wills. Then come back.”

Wills gathered his pencil and ruler. Neale left the specimen where it was.

By the time the cards were ready, Neale's paid hours for that day were over.
Halden put the unfinished lesson beside the next day's work. The card order
was complete. It could be entered in the week's account; the lesson could wait
for another afternoon. He did not cancel it.

In April Lovelace returned to the office decision. She had not resigned. Both
men had feared it, and both would have found it convenient: her absence could
have been treated as consent obtained by exhaustion. Instead she took a sheet
of the venture's paper and wrote a qualification beneath the February decision.
It began in her usual close hand.

*The 1851 trial established one frozen operation under comparison fixed
beforehand, not the rate at which customer work could be prepared and independently
checked. The four obligations depended upon capacity not present when they were
accepted.*

Below that the lines stood farther apart, and each direction began at the
margin.

*Accept no fifth.*

*Pay for Mr Wills's instruction in hours of its own.*

*Before the first return arrives, name Mr Neale's deputy.*

She signed and dated it.

## X. The Unfunded Successor

By August, Lovelace could work for an hour and lose the afternoon to it.

The arithmetic of her illness was more exact than its cause. A journey to
London spent several days. A long letter spent one. Visitors spent whatever
strength courtesy concealed from them. At Ockham, papers from the Calculation
Office arrived in packets whose urgency was visible before she broke their
seals.

William found her with the capacity qualification, Neale's checking sheets, and
three letters spread over the bed.

“You promised me one hour,” he said.

“I said I would not travel.”

“You promised both.”

He removed none of the papers. He set the water within her reach and drew the
curtains against the light.

“They have made checking depend upon a single man,” she said.

“Then it does not depend upon you.”

“It depends upon my continuing to insist that he is single.”

Her signature stood alone beside the claim clauses in the copy before her.
Beneath it, *deputy, if required* was still legible through the line she had
drawn. She set one finger on it.

“Would you have signed it?” she asked.

“What?”

“If they had put your name there.”

“I could not have done your work.”

“No.”

She drew the copy back onto her lap. A moment later she straightened it so he
could read the line.

“I would not have let you,” she said.

William sat down beside the bed. She waited for him to say that she had been
right. He asked whether the water was still cool.

She had proposed that Samuel Wills spend part of each week under Neale and part
with an assurance clerk outside the office. During training, output would fall
further. The additional wages and external review would cost approximately one
hundred and twenty pounds in the first year. Halden's answer praised the plan
and asked whether it might begin after the four current packets were delivered.
Babbage's answer proposed that recurrent portions of comparison might later be
mechanized.

She read Halden's answer again, looking for a date she could put beside the
cost. Babbage offered a route through machinery that did not yet exist. Neither paper gave her a day on which Wills would begin.

Lovelace began another page with three headings: competence, paid time,
authority to refuse. She entered Wills, Neale, Halden, Babbage, Davies, and
herself. No row was complete. She sent the unfinished table to both men and
asked them to accept no work beyond Neale's demonstrated reach until one was.

Babbage came to Ockham near the end of the month. He brought drawings rather
than the office account. She recognized the peace offering and the evasion in
the same roll of paper.

He opened the roll across her unanswered table. She drew one edge of it back
into view.

He showed her a proposed means by which a later apparatus might verify parts of
its own operation sequence.

She followed his pencil through two transfers and made him return to the carry.
At the next comparison she stopped him again: both checking paths inherited the
same earlier value. He stared at the lines, rubbed one away with his thumb, and
sent the second path through another register. She moved the delayed sign one
operation farther. He saw why before she explained it.

She left one finger where the two paths had inherited the same value. “If a
later apparatus compared enough of its own operations, would you call that
judgment?”

“Judgment is often the name we give an operation whose conditions have not yet
been exposed,” he said. “If the apparatus compares its own proceedings and
changes what follows, at what exact line would you deny it the word?”

“I wrote that an Engine might compose music if the relations of harmony could
be given to its operations. It might carry them to a passage no composer had
set down note by note.”

“Would it not have invented the passage?”

“The consequence might be new to us. The relations and purpose would still
have entered from us. Our surprise would not be its intention.”

He crossed out *verification* and wrote *comparison of internal operations*.

For several minutes the mechanism occupied the whole table. He began a mark and
she completed it; she crossed out his correction and he laughed. Their old
speed returned so suddenly that neither acknowledged it. For those minutes
William's hour ceased to exist for both of them. Then she reached for the
pencil and had to wait for her breath. When she shifted in the chair, the edge
of Guardian's source sheet slipped from beneath the roll.

“It is good,” she said.

He waited for the rest.

“It does not read Guardian's source sheet.”

She drew the successor register from beneath the roll and closed it over his
letter.

He did not consent or refuse. He recommended that the office wait. Halden
adopted the recommendation, deferring training until the present contracts
produced their next payments.

After he left, Lovelace attached his answer and Halden's to her question. She
left the page unclosed, so the unanswered place remained visible.

By November she was in Marylebone, at Great Cumberland Place, and the papers
that had once replaced her presence now had difficulty reaching her at all. She
died there on the twenty-seventh.

News reached Halden at the office before noon. He closed the preparation room
for the day and left the apparatus uncovered, because nobody could agree who
possessed the authority to alter the schedule. Neale stood beside four waiting
packets, his blank strip arrested beneath the first line. Babbage came late and
went first to the machine. He pressed his palm against the frame and left it
there. No motion returned through the metal. It was cold and still.

During 1853 the four packets passed through the office in overlapping stages.
On most days this looked like growth. Preparers borrowed desks and reused card
forms; Neale moved to whichever promised date was nearest; corrections that
once had opened a margin now consumed it. Wills's ruler and pencil moved from
packet to packet. The edge of Neale's blank strip darkened with use. No single
day announced failure; each exception was carried forward until one could leave
the room.

On 1 April 1854 Guardian's signed return arrived. Wills laid it beside the
specimen sheets. Much of the card order could be kept. Neale put the old
checking sheets aside; their ticks belonged to different figures. He drew the
first new source beneath his strip.

On most days this looked like growth. Preparers borrowed desks and reused card
forms; Neale moved to whichever promised date was nearest; corrections that

the room.

with it. Wills laid Guardian's beside the specimen sheets. Much of the card
order could be kept. Neale put the old checking sheets aside; their ticks
belonged to different figures. The Lothbury copy was ready first, and he drew
its first line beneath his strip. Lothbury's and Guardian's were the two small
packets, a week of Neale's hours apiece; the two large ones would need the rest
of the quarter and more.

On Friday the seventh both dates fell due, the first the office had ever had
to keep.

The Guardian cards were ready a little after nine. Wills brought the cards and
his copy to Halden's desk. There was one mark in the checking column, his own.

“Mr Neale?” Halden asked.

“The Lothbury comparison, sir. He hopes to finish it by four.”

Through the glass Neale sat with his strip beneath a line of another office's
figures. He had perhaps six of his week's hours left. Halden could walk twenty
feet and put the Guardian copy on top of the Lothbury sheets, and one of the
two offices would receive its table late.

The wage envelopes lay filled in their box on the corner of the desk.
Guardian's deposit had paid for some of them; if the date passed, the deposit
became returnable. On the shelf above, beside the test packet, lay Lady
Lovelace's qualification.

He opened the delivery ledger at the Guardian line. No line in it had yet been
marked delivered. He wrote in the margin reserved for an exception.

*Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date.*

*E. H.*

“Release them,” he said. “Mr Neale will compare the copy on Monday.”

Wills looked at the single mark and then at the margin. He squared the cards
against his palm and carried them to the reader.

The cards began to fall at ten. By four the table had gone to Guardian in
Lombard Street, and Lothbury's had followed it with both signatures and a
quarter of an hour to spare.

On Monday, with the papers full of the war, the third office's signed return
arrived with a query in its covering letter, and Neale's hours went to the
query. Halden had meant to tell him about Guardian's copy once the query was
answered. On Tuesday the fourth arrived. Neale worked, as he had all year, to
the nearest promised date, and a delivered table had none. The Guardian line in
the ledger carried its single mark forward from week to week, as the year's exceptions had, until
the packet came back tied with the office's own green tape.

## XI. The Seller's Conditions

Halden's reply to Guardian contained the source sheet, the preparation copy,
the cards, both run traces, the delivery ledger, and the sentence with which he
had begun: there was no second signature.

Davies accepted the trace and rejected the table.

Clause eleven required correction at the seller's expense. The following
clause permitted cancellation if the error had passed a promised independent
check or if no such check had occurred. Guardian invoked both. Its deposit of
one hundred and eighty pounds was to be returned. The corrected table would be
received as evidence of performance under the clause, not as completion of a
continuing contract.

The office recomputed the deck. Wills copied the source under Neale's voice,
then Neale copied it again under Wills's. The apparatus produced the corrected
values. The work took four days. By the third evening Neale's voice had
roughened, and Wills read while Neale followed with the grey-edged strip.

When Neale stopped him, Wills began the whole line again, faster.

“From where the strip is.”

Wills found the place. He read the figure once. Neale moved the strip, and they
went on.

When they exchanged sheets, Wills asked for a repetition. The request came out
too softly; Neale had already begun the next figure. Wills put his pencil across the copy.

“The one before, Mr Neale.”

Neale returned to it. Wills entered the figure only after he had heard it again.
Neither man looked towards the office door. There was still the rest of the
column to read.

The correction had required no alteration to the mechanism. Babbage wanted
the response to say so.

He slid the two exact run traces away from the delivery ledger. Halden returned
them to the same packet before answering.

“Put this before the refund,” Babbage said. “The difference enters before the
first card.”

“The trace makes it clear,” Halden said.

“A trace in a cancelled office will not govern what people say. They will say
the Engine made a wrong table.”

“Guardian paid us to stop that table leaving,” Halden said. “The clerk has his
line in the trace. Mine is in the ledger. I won't answer cancellation with a
paragraph about the Engine.”

Halden opened the office account.

There had been nine hundred pounds in contributed capital and seven hundred and
twenty in customer deposits. Wages, rent, heat, cards, maintenance, and delivery
had consumed most of it. Guardian's refund, the correction, reprinting, closure,
and storage consumed the rest. Even if another customer agreed to wait, the
office could not support the staff required to complete and independently check
the remaining work without new capital.

“Then raise new capital on the investigation,” Babbage said.

“Upon what statement?”

“That the calculating mechanism executed every operation supplied to it;
preparation and checking failed outside it.”

“And the office?”

“Those functions can be constituted anew under stricter conditions.”

Halden imagined the circular. A correct machine, a corrected human process,
subscriptions sought for renewed operation under improved safeguards. Every
sentence could be defended. Together they would invite a new subscriber to
finance obligations the present account could not meet.

Margaret had sorted the figures the night before into sums already owed, money
still in hand, and money a new circular only hoped to attract. When Halden began
to call the third rescue, she put one finger beneath the first.

“Before you send another circular,” she had said, “show me what leaves this
house before the first new subscription comes in.”

New money might preserve Halden's standing and keep Wills and Neale employed.
It might also convert Guardian's disclosed error into evidence that the system
had already corrected itself. He had spent twelve years teaching other men that
a future capacity could not pay a present debt merely because it was described
well.

He wrote the closure resolution.

The remaining customer obligations would be completed only where existing
funds and independent checking sufficed; otherwise they would be cancelled
before another stage became due. Guardian would receive its refund and corrected
table. Wills and Neale would be paid through the closure month. The apparatus
would be dismantled into stored assemblies. The complete ledger would name the
February 1852 four-job authorization and the April 1854 delivery exception.
Under *cause of exception*, Halden first wrote *pressure of business*. He read
the words, struck them through, and copied both of his authorizations in full.

Wills asked to see him after the staff were told.

“Will the record carry my name?” the young man asked.

“On the preparation copy.”

“And on my reference?”

“The reference will state both the error and what you did afterward.”

Wills looked toward the preparation room. “A new master may stop at the error.”

Neale had waited at the door with his wooden case. “Put my name beneath the
correction, sir. He read the second copy. I followed.”

Halden added the sentence. Neale initialled it, then Halden turned the reference
around and placed it beside Wills's ruler. “Read it before I sign.”

On the last day of March 1855, the shaft beneath the calculating room stopped.
Farrow's men removed the card reader first, then the registers. Neale carried
his checking books away in a wooden case. Wills left with a reference that
described both the error and his conduct during correction.

Halden locked the account and gave one key to the subscriber trust's solicitor
and one to Babbage.

“You have used the stopping clauses as though dissolution were a completed
stage,” Babbage said.

“The wages are paid. The customers have their money or their work. One key goes
to the trust and one to you.”

“That preserves the account by surrendering the work.”

Halden waited. Babbage closed his hand around the key.

“It does,” Halden said.

received as evidence of performance under the clause, not as completion of a
continuing contract.

Neale had come in at two on the day the packet returned. He read the margin of
the delivery ledger before he took off his coat, and Wills told him what had
been said at the desk that Friday.

“You promised my Monday, sir.”

“I did.”

Neale hung the coat on its peg and asked for the source sheet.

The office recomputed the table. Wills copied the source under Neale's voice,
then Neale copied it again under Wills's. The apparatus produced the corrected
values. The work took four days. By the third evening Neale's voice had
roughened, and Wills read while Neale followed with the grey-edged strip.

When Neale stopped him, Wills began the whole line again, faster.

“From where the strip is.”

Wills found the place. He read the figure once. Neale moved the strip, and they
went on.

When they exchanged sheets, Wills asked for a repetition. The request came out
too softly; Neale had already begun the next figure. Wills put his pencil
across the copy.

“The one before, Mr Neale.”

Neale returned to it. Wills entered the figure only after he had heard it again.
Neither man looked towards the office door. There was still the rest of the
column to read.

The correction had required no alteration to the mechanism. Babbage wanted
the response to say so.

He slid the two exact run traces away from the delivery ledger. Halden returned
them to the same packet before answering.

“Put this before the refund,” Babbage said. “The difference enters before the
first card.”

“The trace makes it clear,” Halden said.

“A trace in a cancelled office will not govern what people say. They will say
the Engine made a wrong table. I began the first engine because tables
computed and copied by hand were wrong, Mr Halden. I gave it a printer so that
no hand need copy a figure between the machine and the page, and you struck the
printer from your first report.”

“The figure went in by hand. A printer would have printed it.”

“I know it,” Babbage said. “I have twice been asked, by members of both
Houses, whether the machine gives right answers when it is given wrong figures.
They will not need to ask again. They will think this table has answered them.”

“What did Guardian purchase?” Halden said. “It paid us to stop that table
leaving. The clerk has his line in the trace. Mine is in the ledger. I won't
answer cancellation with a paragraph about the Engine.”

nodes.text:
Halden opened the office account.

There had been nine hundred pounds in contributed capital and seven hundred and
twenty in customer deposits. Wages, rent, heat, cards, maintenance, and delivery
had consumed most of it. Guardian's refund, the correction, reprinting, closure,
and storage consumed the rest. Even if another customer agreed to wait, the
office could not support the staff required to complete and independently check
the remaining work without new capital.

“Then raise new capital on the investigation,” Babbage said.

“On what statement?”

“That the calculating mechanism executed every operation supplied to it;
preparation and checking failed outside it.”

“And the office?”

“Those functions can be constituted anew under stricter conditions.”

Halden imagined the circular. A correct machine, a corrected human process,
subscriptions sought for renewed operation under improved safeguards. Every
sentence could be defended. Together they would invite a new subscriber to
finance obligations the present account could not meet.

Margaret had sorted the figures the night before into sums already owed, money
still in hand, and money a new circular only hoped to attract. When Halden
began to call the third column a rescue, she had put one finger beneath the first.

“Before you send any circular,” she had said, “show me what leaves this
house before the first new subscription comes in.”

She had found his capacity sheet among the office papers, the line marked twice.
“You showed me the articles in January, when you asked for the savings,” she
had said. “Not this.”

He had not.

New money might preserve Halden's standing and keep Wills and Neale employed.
He looked again at the sums already owed.

He wrote the closure resolution.

The remaining customer obligations would be completed only where existing
funds and independent checking sufficed; otherwise they would be cancelled
before another stage became due. Guardian would receive its refund and corrected
table. Wills and Neale would be paid through the closure month. The apparatus
would be dismantled into stored assemblies. The complete ledger would name the
February 1852 four-job authorization and the April 1854 delivery exception.
Under *cause of exception*, Halden first wrote *pressure of business*. He read
the words, struck them through, and copied both of his authorizations in full.

Wills asked to see him after the staff were told.

“Will the record carry my name?” the young man asked.

“On the preparation copy.”

“And on my reference?”

“The reference will state both the error and what you did afterward.”

Wills looked towards the preparation room. “A new master may stop at the error.”

Neale had waited at the door with his wooden case. “Put my name beneath the
correction, sir. He read the second copy. I followed.”

Halden added the sentence. Neale initialled it, then Halden turned the reference
around and placed it beside Wills's ruler. “Read it before I sign.”

Wills put the ruler beneath the first line. He read down to Neale's initials,
moved it back to the top, and began again.

Neale lowered his wooden case to the floor.

“Is there something wrong?” Halden asked.

“Could you put the order in, sir?” Wills asked.

“The order?”

“To send the table before the second comparison.”

Halden brought the pen towards the first paragraph.

“Not the copying,” Wills said. “I did that.”

“I wasn't going to take it out.”

Wills looked at the ruler. “Only the other part as well.”

There was room beneath Neale's initials if Halden wrote small. He drew a fresh
sheet from the drawer instead.

He copied the account of the transposition, then wrote: *I authorized delivery
before the independent comparison was complete.* Below it he put the account
of the correction.

Neale bent over the new sheet. His case stood between his feet while he
initialled his sentence again.

Wills put the ruler beneath the first line. When he came to the new sentence
he read it twice. Then he moved the ruler down.

nodes.text:
The remaining obligations took until the spring to close. On the last day of
March 1855, the shaft beneath the calculating room stopped. Farrow's men
removed the card reader first, then the registers. Neale carried his checking
books away in a wooden case. Wills left with a reference that described both
the error and his conduct during correction.

Halden locked the account and gave one key to the subscriber trust's solicitor
and one to Babbage.

“You have used the stopping clauses as though dissolution were a completed
stage,” Babbage said.

“The wages are paid. The customers have their money or their work. One key goes
to the trust and one to you.”

“That preserves the account by surrendering the work.”

Halden waited. Babbage closed his hand around the key.

“It does,” Halden said.

## XII. The Complete Record

In 1871, Henry Babbage found the returned table among his father's successful
papers.

It had remained there for sixteen years. At first Charles pencilled *mechanism
trace exact* upon the wrapper. Later he asked Halden for the reconciled account
and tied it beneath the same green tape. The tape had been opened often enough
to soften at the knot. Each time, proof and failure returned beneath one
fastening.

Charles had asked him to inventory what would pass into his custody. The work
occupied several autumn afternoons. Drawings had multiplied beyond cabinets.
Mechanisms stood beneath covers. Notes on improvements continued into the
present year, written in the same hand that had marked changes before Henry was
born.

The packet from the old undertaking was different. It had been assembled as if
for a dispute whose parties might all be dead. The frozen configuration came
first, then the successor register, inspection corrections, sealed cases, run
traces, and the signed statement of 1851. After them lay Lady Lovelace's
capacity qualification, her unanswered succession question, the source sheet,
the transposed copy, the delivery exception, Davies's cancellation, the
corrected table, and Halden's closure account.

Her qualification began in the close hand Henry knew from the Notes. Its final
directions stood farther apart, each beginning at the margin.

Henry lifted the returned table. “This is filed with the Engine papers.”

His father was seated near the fire, wrapped in a coat although the day was not
cold. Age had reduced the distance he could cross without effort but not the
distance his thought attempted in a sentence.

“It was not an error of the Engine,” Charles said.

Henry set it beside the office accounts.

“Not there,” Charles said.

Henry left the sheet between the two piles. “Then the inventory needs a heading
that takes both.”

For several seconds, only the fire answered.

“That was Halden's question,” Charles said at last. “What had the customer
purchased?”

“The apparatus performed the operation supplied to it. Precisely. Yet the
office had undertaken to supply a table. Lady Lovelace insisted upon that
distinction before the office existed.”

Henry kept his pencil above the blank line.

“I distinguished the general machine from a temporary arrangement of persons.”
Charles looked toward the covered mechanisms. “The distinction was true.” His
voice lost its earlier force. “It did not answer the account. The office had
undertaken to deliver a correct table.”

Henry had grown up among unfinished objects defended by future completion.
Even now the covered mechanisms drew his eye away from the account. There was
work he could imagine doing with them, and he had to bring himself back to the
blank inventory line. The returned table still lay between the two piles.
Whatever happened to the drawings, it would need a place.

Military service had taken Henry far from these rooms. Now he had returned,
with questions of his own about the machinery, and his father tired before they
could finish an argument.

Charles noticed him looking towards the drawings.

“Not that sheet. The alteration is on the next.”

Henry lifted it. Underneath lay a drawing crowded with pencilled corrections.

“Here?”

“One farther.”

Henry carried the drawing to him. They followed a line together until it passed
beneath another sheet. His father was still tracing its continuation when Henry
moved the paper aside.

“Yes,” Charles said. “You see.”

Henry returned the drawing to its place and took up the pencil beside the
inventory.

“What name shall I put upon the inventory?” Henry asked.

Charles answered too quickly. “Analytical Engine—experimental working papers.”

Henry wrote the phrase, then left space beneath it.

His father noticed. “You disapprove?”

“It does not explain why the accounts are present.”

Charles asked for the inventory. His hand was unsteady, and Henry expected him
to strike out the first line. Instead he added another.

Bounded apparatus and calculation office: configuration, proof, qualification,
error, correction, and closure, complete.

“Complete,” Henry read.

“Of that object,” Charles said. “Not of the Engine.”

“I understand.”

“Do you?”

The old impatience sharpened the words, but it could not sustain itself. Charles
rested the pen.

“No matter. Keep the sentence.”

The packet passed into Henry's custody with the drawings and workshop material
after his father's death. He copied both headings into the inventory and placed
the packet beside the drawings.

In 1900, Henry opened the packet again.

The green tape had faded. Guardian's seal remained broken along the cut Halden
made in 1854. The wrong table and the corrected one lay side by side, equally
preserved. Between them was Lovelace's qualification, its final lines still
widening toward the end.

Henry returned her sheet between the two tables and tied the faded tape around
all three.

The complete record holds the success and the failure together, and is complete only of its object. Strategy. Where the reader meets it: III (The reader meets the idea as pleasure: the night the list grows shorter and Halden smiles at empty columns.). Where the story tests it: VI (The accepted repair works and the better route stays recorded; the machine does not judge between them.); VIII (The signed sentence claims exactly what was shown; the joy is real; for three strokes nobody watches the registers.); X (Even at the end the shared work gives pleasure that does not answer Lovelace's table.). Where it lands: XII (The inventory's second heading, and the three papers tied together in 1900.). The telling process story.process.book.idea.made-stays-made.20260929 follows the strategy through the chapters with exact passages; the model records it rests on are linked below."}
nodes.title: Idea and strategy: What was made stays made

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"plan","text":"Idea: An undertaking can be trusted only as far as someone named can stop it. Refusal is a founding act, not a failure, and it is weakest where the one who proposes is also the only one who may refuse. The book does not settle that refusing a promise is always right: the stop that saves the test also closes the office. Strategy. Where the reader meets it: II (The reader meets the idea as the empty office in Lovelace's proposal and as a term of thirty days whose refusal must carry its reason.); III (Halden's fee buys the possibility of refusal.); V (The compact begins with who can stop it.). Where the story tests it: VII (Stopping costs the stopper: Halden follows Lovelace's three directions against every private pressure and loses his fee.); VIII (The stop is used against everyone's wish to go on.); IX (The counter-instance: acceptance given to the manager, whom only the account may refuse.); X (Lovelace's succession table asks who may refuse beside who is competent and who is paid; no row is complete.). Where it lands: XI (The stopping clauses close the office; Babbage names the cost and Halden agrees.). The telling process story.process.book.idea.someone-can-say-no.20260929 follows the strategy through the chapters with exact passages; the model records it rests on are linked below."}
nodes.title: Idea and strategy: Someone must be able to say no

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"lens","text":"An optional lens, used where it illuminates; no shares. Babbage's refusal to sign an arrangement into permanence (II) is fear, taught by Clement keeping the tools: fear of losing what he made to whoever holds the paper. Lovelace striking the deputy line (V) is both: fear of being substituted and erased, and care for a claim that must not be widened by whoever stands in. At Ockham she names the fear herself ('I would not have let you'). Halden's Friday order (X) is mostly fear: of the returnable deposit, of the wage envelopes, of Lothbury's lateness, of the office's name; what he cares for inside it is the household's savings in the office and the recognition he has begun to live on. It is the act the book is built around, and neither reading excuses it. Neale asking for his name beneath Wills's correction (XI) is care, the more so after 'You promised my Monday, sir'. Charles's second heading in 1871 (XII) is care for a true record over fear of a curated triumph; age has worn the fear down. Other reasons stand beside these (duty, habit, the money, the hours), and the prose shows the acts rather than naming the motives, which this reading does not change."}
nodes.title: Fear or love behind five acts (qualitative reading)

nodes.text:
{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"plan","text":"Reading, 2026-09-29, after the tool update. I read the tool's guidance in full: life_modeling_context (creative_story, continuation), the storytelling add-on resource (sha256 5351b557...), and the interestCatalog that the opening stage returns (31 elements; it comes back at the opening stage, so I recorded a retrospective opening, world.book.opening.retrospective.20260929). Then the construction replay from r0 at outline level (165 revisions) and the model outline at graph revision 164, model revision 22 (ceaa78db).

What the reading shows. The Book's causes, money, capacity, disclosures and voices are modeled deeply. What is thin, measured against the catalog and the model's own 83 questions: the three principals' flaws are labels in developments, not processes over their lives; all three have only the shared vocabulary of wants (wants-generic), and Halden and Lovelace have no change arc of their own (shocks-few); the model holds 434 Events and one concept, and no laws; the relationship processes have no phases; ten secondary people have no periods, wants or shocks; Lovelace's life has no period from 1847 to May 1851; the objects that return (the checking strip, the qualification, the thin book, Wills's ruler, the compact copy) are Things without uses; the 1847 crisis is only 'a wider contraction'.

Plan for this pass (model first, then prose, then follow-through):
1. Flaws as processes over lives, with deep wants and proxies. Babbage turns threatened dependence into control (Clement kept the tools in 1833): brilliant in design, harmful when judgment must be shared. Lovelace guards sole authority over the claim (the struck deputy line), until she sees at Ockham that she too is a sole carrier. Halden's usefulness has been invisible all his life; recognition, when it comes after the trial, becomes the proxy that displaces the durable work he wanted, and the office's fourth article rewards it. For each: the teaching event, the situations it takes over, strength and harm, cost, who sees it, whether it changes.
2. Concepts and laws the Events instantiate: common-source dependence (Babbage's and Halden's confidence moved by one trial in E18; two checking paths inheriting one value in E20a; Wills reading his own copy on 6 April); the sole carrier (Lovelace's signature, Neale's ten hours, the manager whom nobody may refuse); recognition as a proxy. One law to state and test: a shared success moves together the judgments it rewards.
3. The secret's social life: who knew from 7 April to 3 May 1854 that Guardian's table had gone out on one mark, and whether each one's silence is plausible.
4. Relationship tone for the three principal pairs, as processes with phases: what each relies on the other for, and what they refuse to.
5. Objects that return, with their changing uses.
6. Macro: the 1847 crisis as a sourced world Event; the errors in printed tables that Babbage's engines were built to end; Lovelace's 1847 to 1851 period after the documentary cutoff, including whether her documented betting of 1851 belongs to this history.
7. Secondary lives for Neale, Wills and Margaret: a deep want, a proxy and a shock of their own.
Then re-read the prose against each opening, the crisis chapters (VIII to XI) first, carrying the modeled voices; revise where the deeper model disagrees, or record why a passage stands; renew facts, disclosures and telling processes; run the revision check. Before and after: a blind voice-attribution check (names and tags removed) and one controlled read-back with a control reader, all Sonnet 5.5. The work remained on a separate draft branch pending acceptance."}

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"plan","text":"Reading and plan for the Book branch after the tool update of 14:45 (model revision 26 onward), recorded before any change. I re-read the tool list (81 tools; changed: life_understanding_record, life_revision_check, life_story_author_record), life_modeling_context for a continuation, the storytelling add-on resource in full (93,211 characters, sha256 a75311ea...), the Meaning Model theory, which changed (cbb2336e; read as a diff against 8fd20a32, which I had read in full: a new paragraph on compressing the story and on ideas with strategies, and telling phases checked separately in the revision check), and the stage and director schemas. What is new: a book is a way of communicating specific ideas. Write each idea down with its strategy (where the reader meets it, where the story tests it, where it lands); compress the story into a sentence, a paragraph and a page; if the sentence does not make it interesting, go back to the model; check that the book still fits its sentence. The director has two new principles, one for each: the ideas are written down with their strategies, and each reaches the reader. A blind read-back shows which ideas reached a reader. The revision check lists telling phases whose passages changed until they are renewed. The active author record (world.book.nora-author-reader.calendar-20260927) says only that Nora wants a reader to feel the cost and pleasure of work shared across unequal kinds of knowledge; it names no ideas or strategies. {"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"# The Book of Conditions — first continuation candidate

Status: private, unaccepted editorial candidate, 27 September 2026. Nothing in the accepted source, model, paper, compiled examples, or releases has been replaced. `manuscript-v1.md` is a complete book, not a set of excerpts. This pass is local fiction editing; it introduces no claim of historical evidence.

## What the book already achieves

The manuscript has a strong causal structure: one bounded proof becomes a temptation to expand, scarce independent checking remains scarce, and the institution fails while the mechanism performs its supplied operations correctly. The return of the same physical objects — drawings, checking strip, signature, account, green tape — gives the changing interpretation a material continuity. The successful trial is allowed genuine shared joy. That matters: later division costs the characters something they actually had.

The existing refinements already resist an easy saint-and-villains reading. Lovelace protects her rare authority in a way that also makes it fragile. Halden understands the limit he exceeds. Babbage's architectural distinction is true and inadequate to the purchased obligation. These should survive expansion.

The current risk is more local than a missing plot: the narrator and principals sometimes finish the interpretation before the scene has had time to produce it. Secondary people can become bearers of the founders' lesson. Wills makes the error and receives a reference, but has little room to practice the uncertain competence that management prematurely treats as future capacity. Margaret's labor is recognized in narration, then she immediately serves the useful function of correcting Edward. More explanation would intensify those problems.

## The chosen first pass

Nine bounded changes develop existing material. The candidate adds about four hundred words overall; seven of the twelve sections change. It does not add a thirteenth section, another catastrophe, a new customer, a new failure, an improved apparatus, or a new historical assertion. Sections II, III, IV, VI and VIII remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

The largest additions occur inside the existing E17 training and E26 correction. Wills learns to stop when he cannot independently read a source; after the failure he makes himself ask Neale to repeat a figure. These are modest actions, not proof that he is now an independent checker. Neale does not become an infallible rescuer. He admits unreadability, directs the work, and accepts being interrupted. Their language stays close to the sheet.

Margaret gets one brief working boundary: Edward must wait for her to finish an entry before spreading his venture across her book. The final custody scene loses one explanatory paragraph in favor of Henry's eye returning from the tempting mechanisms to the inventory line. Lovelace's unanswered question is allowed an extra beat of searching for an actionable date.

The accepted model currently supports the parent actions and broad character interpretations. Three newly specified interactions are proposals requiring event/evidence refinement before adoption as model-grounded prose. They are not already present in the model merely because they are plausible. The other edits render established actions or substitute local scene detail for explanatory prose; they require fresh document/span identities if adopted, but not changed world causality or numerical profiles.

## Adoption map

Each `BC-` identifier is local to this editorial pass, not a native Meaning Model ID. Exact before/after text, line anchors, and SHA-256 hashes are in `scene-anchor-map.json`. Existing E-numbers below are the accepted authored event aliases; any native IDs must be resolved from the import receipt.

| Edit | Section / event | Classification | Intended effect | Required action before adopting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BC-01 | I / E25 | Prose-only elaboration | Allow Wills's silence and Halden's impulse to repeat the accusation to take time; Halden still finds his own authorization. | Rebind changed passage evidence; no new cause, accusation, or profile weight. |
| BC-02 | V / E06 | Prose-only elaboration | Replace Lovelace's universal institutional maxim with her attention to stopping clauses. | Rebind passage; retain authority and deputy decisions. |
| BC-03 | VII / E11 | **Event/evidence refinement** | Margaret finishes her own account entry before taking the venture ledger. | Extend E11 / household-work interpretation with this proposed interaction; retain the same payment and pause decision. |
| BC-04 | VII / E11, Halden's later interpretation | Prose-only elaboration | Bring the existing household exchange back into Halden's remembered proof of discipline instead of announcing a general lesson. | Rebind passage; read as attributed retrospective interpretation, not additional documentary history. |
| BC-05 | IX / E17 | **Event/evidence refinement** | Open training: unreadable source, comparison to expectation, Wills's request for the original, Neale's permission to leave a check unresolved. | Extend E17 with a coarse child opening or description; source is a practice/specimen copy, not one of the final April 1854 returns. Do not invent duration, Cut shares, independent qualification, or a completed source resolution. |
| BC-06 | IX / E18 | Prose-only elaboration | Show the scope of Halden's checking narrowing to correct customer particulars while he accepts the known capacity gamble. | Preserve all four acceptances, his sole contracting authority, and the unchanged profile/decision Cuts. |
| BC-07 | X / E20 | Prose-only elaboration | Lovelace searches the existing answers for a usable training date. | No new promise or deadline; preserve deferred expenditure and existing letter-before-visit order. |
| BC-08 | XI / E26 | **Event/evidence refinement** | Wills stops a reading he did not hear; Neale accepts the interruption during their already recorded paired correction. | Extend E26 and the corrective-conduct evidence. Do not treat the episode as independent certification or a new copying error. |
| BC-09 | XII / E29 | Prose-only elaboration | Henry has to turn from imaginable future work to an actual inventory place for the returned table. | Preserve complete custody, both headings, the unresolved general Engine and the 1900 survival-only coda. |

## Minimal proposed model refinements

These statements are proposed authored content, **not changes already applied**:

**E11 — household labor within the credit decision:** Before reading the venture ledger, Margaret asks Edward to let her finish the line in her own stationer's account. He lifts the venture ledger and waits. She then reviews the same unpaid calls and wage obligation already described. The episode opens her work and control of working time without adding income, cost, a new causal shock, or a different decision.

**E17 — supervised source comparison:** During the already recorded practice with Neale, Wills begins from an expected figure made legible in a prepared copy. He then admits he cannot independently read its source. Neale also cannot read it and leaves the check open. Wills asks for the original and marks the unresolved place. This is a practice/specimen source in the existing training period; its later resolution remains unopened. The episode supplies evidence of supervised learning and the ordinary labor of obtaining a trustworthy source. It supplies no independent checker-hours.

**E26 — correction and the permission to interrupt:** In the already recorded four-day paired correction, Wills at first responds to an interruption by rushing the line. Neale returns him to the strip. When their reading and copying roles exchange, Wills makes a second, audible request for a figure he did not hear, and Neale repeats it. The corrected operation remains unchanged. The episode supplies specific evidence for the corrective conduct already carried into his reference.

These descriptions can remain refinements inside the current parent events. Creating separate subsidiary nodes is useful only if the tool or author needs to inspect these episodes independently. No new numerical Cut is needed to justify the prose. If future exploration gives Wills or Margaret richer motives, those should be authored as their attributed understanding and tested against the scene, not inferred from the founders' profiles.

## What should be opened next

The next useful candidate is the ordinary aftermath already accepted in Halden's life: return to salaried estimating after closure. The current manuscript jumps from 1855 to custody in 1871. A small scene could let the reader experience continued work without public redemption, while Margaret and Halden renegotiate household means after his two stakes are lost. This would give the claimed later adaptation evidence beyond the closure decision itself.

That extension is deliberately not written into this candidate. First choose an ordinary job consistent with the existing broad municipal/instrument work, who is present, and what small decision demonstrates changed judgment without simply repeating the wages conversation. Salary, employer, exact year, client and family circumstances remain unestablished. Those choices would require a new or refined post-1855 event before prose. There is no need to invent a famous downstream influence, an Engine Age, or a reconciliation that makes the ending easier.

## Review limits and checks

- Complete accepted manuscript and relevant world/person/scene/health/route/understanding documents were read.
- Source SHA-256, candidate SHA-256 and exact changed block hashes are recorded in the anchor map.
- All twelve headings and the complete ordered sequence of numeric literals match the source. These mechanical checks protect against accidental omission; they do not prove semantic fidelity.
- Manual review checked the main risks introduced by the new prose: the practice source is not a final 1854 return; no completed independent training is claimed; reader/copier role exchanges are explicit; Babbage's drawing does not arrive before his visit; the apparatus configuration, cost, and four-day correction remain fixed.
- Source and model files remain untouched. No native narrative revision, director review, evidence rebind, fresh import, paper rendering or publication has been performed for this candidate. It should not be described as model-validated or final.

{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"# Blind read: The Book of Conditions

Read in full, in order, from the single manuscript file. Nothing else consulted. Real-world facts are judged from memory; confidence is stated where it matters.

## 1. Verdict

*The Book of Conditions* is a twelve-chapter novella of about 11,700 words built on one real hinge. In August 1843 Ada Lovelace proposed to Charles Babbage that she take charge of the practical side of the Analytical Engine; historically he refused every condition within a day. Here he grants her thirty days instead. An estimator, Edward Halden, is found; he refuses to price "the Engine" and prices instead a deliberately crippled fragment of it (six registers, six digits, thirty card steps, addition and subtraction, nothing else). With the actuary Griffith Davies of Guardian Assurance and a Lambeth works, the three build it under a compact that says who may stop what; it binds, is repaired within its own terms, survives the 1847 credit crisis, and in 1851 reproduces twelve sealed actuarial cases on two witnessed runs. A calculation office is founded on the proof, sells four tables against checking capacity for two, loses Lovelace in November 1852, ships a wrong table in April 1854 with one signature where two were promised, and closes honestly in March 1855. Two codas (1871, 1900) let Babbage and then his son Henry decide what heading the record deserves. Underneath, the book is about the gap between a mechanism being correct and an undertaking being trustworthy: who may say no, what a signature promises, what capacity is actually for sale, and what the customer bought ("But they bought the table"). Without once winking, it reads as a parable for present-day machine evaluation and deployment: frozen configuration, sealed cases, a change register, two-person checking, a trace that is exact while the answer is wrong.

It works. The prose is disciplined, the procedures are the drama, and the physical chapters (the assemblies that bind, the two-day test, the reference on the desk) carry real weight; the real history underneath is handled accurately and the invented history is, with two exceptions noted below, easy to follow. Its limits are those of its method. The three principals speak in one epigrammatic voice; the commercial second half is founded in the white space between Chapters VIII and IX; and the book's decisive act, Halden's waiver of the second comparison, is the one act it never puts in scene. It is remembered in a paragraph of Chapter I. The single change that would most improve the book is to dramatize Halden's fall: the founding of the office and, above all, the Friday morning of the waiver, so that the failure the whole book turns on is felt as a man's choice under pressure rather than read back from a ledger.

## 2. What works

- The opening puzzle and the sentence that names its danger: "An absurd answer accused itself. A reasonable wrong answer recruited the reader." The transposition (3,742 for 3,472) is the right size of error for this book: small, plausible, propagating.
- The thesis is stated once, early, in concrete terms, and not repeated: "For every hour of its operation, people spent several hours deciding what it should be given, and more deciding whether its answer could leave the room."
- The book is best when metal and wages are in the room. Chapter VI: "The mechanism's resistance entered Farrow's life first as Friday." Chapter VIII: "There was no line in the account for a load that remained ordinary."
- The test is a genuine set piece, opened by the best first line in the book, "The test began with everyone forbidden to improve it," and given its sharpest moment in four words: "Let him hear the card."
- Motifs are planted and paid: the foreman's two fingers on the bearing cap (VI, VIII), Wills's ruler and pencil (I, IX, XI), Neale's strip cut from a rejected card ("The edge of Neale's blank strip darkened with use"), the green tape (I, XII), the struck line *deputy, if required* (V, X).
- Babbage is drawn fairly and without softening: "He was overtaken by a joy so close to relief that for several seconds he could not distinguish them," and, in the works, "The machine offered no judgment on the route not taken." His late concession, "But they bought the table," is earned by everything before it.
- Lovelace and William at Ockham is the most human scene in the book: "She waited for him to say that she had been right. He asked whether the water was still cool."
- Dialogue economy at its best: "Then we have written sixteen pages to arrive at your memory." "Judgment is often the name we give an operation whose conditions have not yet been exposed." "It does not read Guardian's source sheet."
- Margaret, in two sentences: "Edward had sometimes described her work as help with his books. She had stopped correcting the phrase."
- The reference scene in Chapter XI is the moral climax and is done by indirection: the clerk asks that his employer's fault be written on his own reference and gets it, "Only the other part as well." Halden striking out *pressure of business* and copying both authorizations in full is exactly the right ending for him.
- Real-world grounding is accurate where I can check it: Dorset Street; Ockham; Great Cumberland Place in Marylebone and 27 November 1852; Menabrea's Sketch and the Turin account; the Treasury's refusal; Clement; Whitworth in Manchester; Griffith Davies as Guardian's actuary; Babbage's earlier work on assurance (1826); the October 1847 credit crisis; the mid-August 1843 date of the proposal itself, which is the real date of Lovelace's letter and Babbage's refusal. Confidence high on all of these.

## 3. Findings, most serious first

### Errors

**1. Error, continuity.** Ch. XII against VII and IX. "Its final directions stood farther apart, each beginning at the margin," and at the very end, "its final lines still widening toward the end," both describe Lovelace's capacity qualification. But that physical form belongs to a different document: her October 1847 letter in Chapter VII, where "the three directions—pay, stop, publish nothing—each began a line." The qualification as written in Chapter IX is two sentences ("The 1851 trial established one frozen operation ... not present when they were accepted.") with no directions at all. The book's closing image rests on a detail it never gave the document. Fix in either direction: give the qualification directions in IX (accept no fifth; reserve Neale's hours; name a second checker), which would also strengthen IX; or in XII describe the qualification as it was written. The first is better.

**2. Error, logic.** Ch. I. Davies's letter says the figures "did not agree with Guardian's independent calculation from age forty-seven onward." Babbage then finds the fault at "The first supplied value. After that, every transfer is true," and Halden "found the first divergence" at a single transposed input. If the first supplied value of the table is wrong, the table is wrong from its first line, not from age forty-seven. The reconciliation exists in the book's own rules (thirty card steps per sequence, so a long table runs as several sequences, each with its own supplied start), but the reader is never told the transposed figure opened the sequence that began at forty-seven. One clause fixes it: "the first supplied value of the sequence that began at forty-seven." Without it a careful reader stops.

**3. Error, chronology.** Ch. XII. "In 1871, Henry Babbage found the returned table ... It had remained there for sixteen years. At first Charles pencilled *mechanism trace exact* upon the wrapper." That pencil note is the argument Babbage makes in 1854 (Chapters I and XI), so the table was among his papers from 1854: seventeen years, not sixteen. Sixteen is right only if counted from the closure of March 1855, which the sentence does not say. Low stakes, easy fix: "seventeen," or "since the office closed."

### Majors

**4. Major, dropped structure.** Ch. II sets the book's first finite obligation and its title: "Thirty days," "To find your missing man. Or to establish that he ought to remain missing," "Nothing is built. Nothing is subscribed. Nothing is announced," and a refusal that, if it comes, "is written with its reason." Chapter III has Halden ask for "four weeks," and the thirty days are never mentioned again. The reader is never told whether the bound held, whether the report arrived inside it, or that no refusal was written. For a book whose whole argument is that obligations must be closed on their own terms, leaving its first one open is a real fault. One sentence at the end of III or the start of IV ("On the twenty-ninth day Babbage wrote no refusal; he wrote to Davies") would close it.

**5. Major, turn summarized where it should be shown.** Between VIII and IX the venture becomes a business. "By December the first inquiry had become four." Then in IX we are in "Halden's new office, two rooms adjoining the calculating room," with Neale retained, Wills employed, rent to carry, and, in XI, "nine hundred pounds in contributed capital" that is never raised, subscribed, or explained anywhere (the original compact was three thousand; whether any of it survived, and who put up the nine hundred, is not said). Chapters III–V train the reader to expect every obligation to be priced, divided, and signed, and then the obligation the second half depends on, selling calculations at all, happens between chapters. Suggest a short scene: the first inquiry answered, the office's own compact (who holds the nine hundred, who may stop it), and Lovelace's signature or its absence on it.

**6. Major, the decisive act is never in scene.** The waiver is the book's hinge, and it exists only as a remembered paragraph in Chapter I: "He remembered the morning. The wages had been due on Friday ... Monday had filled itself before it arrived." Chapter X ends on 1 April 1854 with Neale drawing "the first new source beneath his strip"; Chapter XI opens with Halden's reply to Guardian. The whole Guardian job, the Friday, the single signature, the delivery, and the return happen offstage, pre-told. The remembered paragraph is good, but a man's ruin by "pressure of business" needs to be watched, not recalled: Halden at the ledger, Neale on the Lothbury packet, the messenger waiting, the margin. Put that morning at the end of X or the start of XI (Chapter I can keep its discovery; the two would rhyme).

**7. Major, voice.** Halden, Babbage, and Lovelace share one register: compressed, aphoristic, every line an epigram. "Division makes no one competent. It tells me whose hours enter the price and whose refusal stops the wages." (Halden). "A machine being paid for must be governed as if somebody can say what is being paid for." (Lovelace). "To charge the mechanism with the table is to confuse obedience to an operation with judgment upon its premise." (Babbage). The minor characters are more distinct than the leads: Farrow ("I won't have him condemn a sound shaft to make this week's account easier"), Neale ("Watch the one you expect"), Margaret ("Is this sum in the bank on Friday?"). The practical cost is that the long unattributed exchanges in II, III, and V require the reader to count lines to know who is speaking. Give each principal a habit of speech the others lack: Babbage's sentences could run long and subordinate; Halden's could stay in quantities; Lovelace's could keep the conditional mood she uses in her letters.

**8. Major, borderline, premise.** What Guardian is buying is never made plain. Davies says "Guardian purchases calculations," but the returned table "did not agree with Guardian's independent calculation," so Guardian computed the table itself anyway; and in XI Halden says "Guardian paid us to stop that table leaving," which is a third thing (a checking service). A reader who is asked to care about "What had the customer purchased?" for twelve chapters may reasonably not know. One line would settle it (Davies bought the machine table to release his own computers, and recomputed the ages above forty-six as his check; or Guardian bought a second, independent computation and compared the whole). I mark it borderline because the book's ambiguity may be intentional; if so, the last chapter should let Charles or Henry name it.

### Minors

**9. Minor, chronology.** Ch. II. "Eleven years earlier" and "He read it on the fifteenth of August" are the only anchors, and no year is given for the opening or for II. The first absolute date in the book is "October 1847" in VII. A reader can back the year out of "the test packet from 1851" and "three years before" in I, but should not have to. Say "August 1843" once; it also announces the point of departure to readers who know the real date.

**10. Minor, unexplained term.** Ch. I. "Mr Neale had the Lothbury packet." Nothing tells the reader this is another customer's job (it is named again as "the Lothbury packet" three paragraphs later). "Another office's packet" or the customer's name would do.

**11. Minor, logic.** Ch. XI. "Halden's reply to Guardian contained the source sheet, the preparation copy, the cards, both run traces, the delivery ledger ..." An office would not post its whole delivery ledger, with other customers' entries, to one customer. "An extract from the delivery ledger" or "the ledger page."

**12. Minor, typography of embedded documents.** Halden's marginal authorization ("Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date." / "E. H."), the public sentence in VIII, the qualification in IX, and both inventory headings in XII run as ordinary body paragraphs, while *deputy, if required*, *mechanism trace exact*, *pressure of business*, and *I authorized delivery before the independent comparison was complete* are italic. Choose one treatment for quoted documents (block or italic) and apply it throughout. In the same pass: the paragraph in VIII ends "could all be named." and "Only then did Davies permit the prospective packet to close." begins on a new line without a paragraph break, and several sentences in IX, X, and XI run far past the file's wrap width ("He held the office pen ...", "In April Lovelace returned ...", "The additional wages ...", "She read Halden's answer again ...", "too softly; Neale had already begun ..."), which suggests later edits pasted in.

**13. Minor, clarity.** Ch. II. "Any later proposal must answer it before anyone is asked to build a metaphor." The line is the chapter's best joke and the reader cannot be sure what the metaphor is (the Engine as it exists "most completely in his mind"?). One more beat earlier in the exchange would earn it.

**14. Minor, redundancy.** Ch. III tells the discovery of the reversal three times: "For the first week Halden tried to bound the Engine ... That failed."; "He discovered the reversal after covering the largest drawing with unpaid accounts ... began with the answer instead."; "The Notes supplied the route." The second is the scene; the first and third can be folded into it.

**15. Minor, unexplained term.** Ch. III. "Halden crossed out an automatic return that required machinery he could not price." "Automatic return" (the cards backing to repeat a sequence) is not explained, and it is the one exclusion that matters most to what the apparatus cannot do. Half a sentence.

**16. Minor, clarity.** Ch. III. "It was more than Babbage expected and less than Halden could afford to waste." Why a wealthy man would expect less than twenty-five pounds for four weeks is not clear; if the point is that Babbage expected the possibility of refusal to be cheap, say so.

**17. Minor, clarity.** Ch. IV. "Davies closed the Notes upon his finger." then, next paragraph, "Davies turned the pages. He paused at the exclusions". Two consecutive paragraphs open with "Davies"; the second does not say which document's pages (the proposal, evidently, since he then "closed the proposal"). "Davies turned the pages of the proposal."

**18. Minor, clarity.** Ch. IV. "The second refusal arrived from Manchester in a wooden box." Nothing before it has been called a refusal; Davies's scene ended on "the first condition on which they agreed." If Davies's refusal to hold an opinion is the first refusal, say it once, because the pairing is a good one.

**19. Minor, accounting.** Ch. V. "The capital page named three thousand pounds. Babbage supplied half. Outside subscribers supplied one thousand through the trust. Guardian's feasibility and test payments supplied four hundred. Halden supplied one hundred." The sums add (1,500 + 1,000 + 400 + 100), but Guardian's payments are receipts for services, not capital, and a book this exact about accounts should not let Halden call them capital. "The page of funds" or "sources of money" instead of "capital page."

**20. Minor, antecedent.** Ch. VI. "Then leave the finding so. I won't have him condemn a sound shaft to make this week's account easier." "Him" is Babbage, who has not yet entered; on first reading it attaches to Halden, who has just spoken. Name him.

**21. Minor, plausibility.** Ch. I: "Every few seconds the card reader lifted, admitted a stiff rectangle, and let it fall." Ch. VIII: "The first attempt consumed the morning" for five and a fraction cases of thirty cards each, and twelve cases take an afternoon. At a card every few seconds, 360 cards is under an hour; the hours must be going to reading back, manual entry, and transcription between cases, which is exactly the book's point, but VIII never says so. One sentence in VIII crediting the day to the human steps would turn a wobble into a theme.

**22. Minor, chronology.** Ch. VIII. "That prohibition had taken nearly seven years to earn." From August 1843 to a test in spring 1851 is closer to eight; from the compact (unstated, presumably early 1844) it is a little over seven. "Seven years" or "more than seven years."

**23. Minor, ambiguity.** Ch. VIII. "Neale signed both preparation checks." In a book that turns on two hands for two signatures, this reads on first pass as one man signing both checks, which is the failure of Chapter I. If it means the preparation check for each of the two runs, say "the preparation check for each run."

**24. Minor, phrasing.** Ch. IX. "Thomas Neale was retained for ten hours a week, which made the theoretical quarter larger." The clause is doing arithmetic the sentence does not show (130 hours against the 80 promised). Give the number or cut the clause.

**25. Minor, clarity.** Ch. IX. "Halden had advertised for another checker. None could yet challenge a prepared deck without Neale's supervision". "None" implies applicants who came and failed; if no one came, say so; if some came, one clause on them would show the market for the skill.

**26. Minor, abstraction.** Ch. IX. "For a moment, the old alliance between conditions and limits reappeared." The narrator naming his own theme. Cut; the exchange it follows ("Is in no contract and no account.") already shows it.

**27. Minor, arithmetic left to the reader.** Ch. IX. "At forty hours per verified packet, the office could deliver two." Neale's "I have eighty hours, sir" is close; let Lovelace or Neale say the other number once.

**28. Minor, continuity (soft).** Ch. IX has Neale "retained for ten hours a week" and "Neale's paid hours for that day were over"; Ch. Two years have passed and his retention may have grown, but the book does not say so, and it is the book that taught the reader to count his hours. One phrase in X or XI.

**29. Minor, terminology drift.** Ch. X. "the edge of Guardian's source sheet slipped from beneath the roll." **31. Minor, clarity.** Ch. X. "He did not consent or refuse. He recommended that the office wait. Halden adopted the recommendation". **33. Minor, clarity.** Ch. XI. "Before you send another circular," implies an earlier circular; none has been sent (Babbage's improvement notice in VII was not circulated). "Before you send a circular."

**35. Minor, phrasing.** Ch. XII. "found the returned table among his father's successful papers." "Successful papers" is either a slip for "successor papers" (the successor register is in the packet) or an irony the sentence cannot carry. If irony, "among the papers of his father's successes"; if slip, fix.

**36. Minor, plausibility.** Ch. XII. "the close hand Henry knew from the Notes." The Notes were printed; a hand is known from manuscript. "from her letters among his father's papers" or "from the manuscript of the Notes."

The reader cannot tell what drawing they are following or why the line passing "beneath another sheet" matters (an improvement never finished, presumably). **39. Minor, spelling consistency.** The manuscript mixes American and British forms: "labor" (II), "honor" (IV), "favored" (V), "recognized" against "theatre" (III), "initialled," "pencilled," "grey-edged," and both "toward" and "towards" throughout. **40. Minor, tic.** Negation as narration is used often enough to become a mannerism: "He did not call for Babbage. Each is fine alone; together they announce the author's hand. Keep the best three.

**41. Minor, tic.** The finger on the line is the book's governing gesture, and it is used past the point of return: "She put one fingernail beneath the wages due."; "She set one finger on it."; "She left one finger where the two paths had inherited the same value."; "she put one finger beneath the first."; "Lovelace's finger reached the final operation and stayed there"; "He touched the prepared copy."; "his blank strip arrested beneath the first line." **42. Minor, slack passages.** The back half of IV (the Whitworth box and Lovelace's two columns, all in summary) and the first page of IX (capacity arithmetic in the narrator's voice) are the two places a reader will skim. Both would take a line of speech or an object.

### Notes

**43. Note.** The title phrase never appears in the text, and its referent is open: Lovelace's ruled volume, the sixteen-page compact with its stopping clauses, or the whole packet. That may be intended; if not, one use in V or XII would fix it.

**44. Note, real world.** Guardian Assurance's own office was in Lothbury (11 Lothbury, I am fairly but not fully sure). Calling another customer's job "the Lothbury packet" will trip readers who know that.

**45. Note, real world.** "The paper had arrived after the Notes." Lovelace's proposal was written on 14 August 1843 while the Notes were in final proof; publication in Taylor's Scientific Memoirs was, I believe, September 1843 (fairly sure). "After the Notes were finished" is exact; "after the Notes" is arguable. Not an error for an alternate history, but this is the sentence that sits on the point of departure.

**46. Note, real world.** The historical Lovelace was in London and gravely ill through August 1852; the Ockham pencil scene in X near the end of that month is a softening of her condition. The book's rule ("could work for an hour and lose the afternoon to it") makes it internally consistent, and the departure is allowed; I record it because a reader who knows will feel it.

**47. Note, real world.** Chapter XII's "several autumn afternoons" of 1871 sit inside a short window: Babbage died on 18 October 1871 (confident). The scene works as an inventory made because he is dying, and the text half says so ("his father tired before they could finish an argument"), but a phrase acknowledging how little time is left would stop the reader checking. I believe Henry was in England that autumn; not certain.

**48. Note, character.** Babbage does not change inside the 1843–1855 story; his last line to Halden is "That preserves the account by surrendering the work." The concession arrives sixteen years later, in the coda. This is a defensible design (the tragedy of a fixed man), and XII earns it; but the reader should know it is chosen. If the author wants any movement earlier, VI already has the seed ("Enter both").

**49. Note, character.** Lovelace is right in every dispute in the book. Her one flaw, refusing her own deputy and so making the venture's judgment depend on one person, is present and well placed ("It depends upon my continuing to insist that he is single"; "I would not have let you"), but it is left for the reader to connect to her accusation against Halden. One more beat, from William or from her, would make her a person rather than a conscience.

**50. Note.** "In 1900, Henry opened the packet again." Nothing motivates the year. A reason (an inquiry, a move, his own work on the mill) would cost a sentence and make the coda feel less like an author choosing a round number.

**51. Note.** Chapter I is dense with terms the reader cannot yet decode (clause eleven, configuration register, successor register, run trace, "sold four dates with hands for two," the 1851 packet, the qualification on capacity). On reread it is the best chapter; on first read the last page is cryptic. That is a fair trade, but the author should know the first-time reader finishes I on faith.

**52. Note.** Halden forgetting his own waiver until he opens the ledger ("He remembered the morning") is psychologically framed by the book ("The third course had felt least like a decision"), and it is the point. Some readers will still not believe that the man of accounts forgot the largest job's exception within weeks. Dramatizing the Friday (finding 6) would remove the need for him to forget.

**53. Note.** "Babbage answered too quickly." (VIII) and "Charles answered too quickly." (XII) are an echo, and a good one. Keep it; make sure nothing else in the book uses the phrase.

**54. Note.** The aphoristic paragraph-closer is the book's signature ("Monday had filled itself before it arrived."; "A reasonable wrong answer recruited the reader."; "Since the government's withdrawal, no one had offered him a refusal that did not also end the undertaking."). Most earn their place; the density in II, III, and V means some land as manner rather than meaning. Consider cutting a fifth of them.

**55. Note.** "Lovelace came to his rooms in Dorset Street." Babbage owned the house at 1 Dorset Street; "rooms" suggests lodgings. "His house" is plainer and true.

**56. Note.** "For several seconds, only the fire answered." is the one stock sentence in an otherwise unstock book.

**57. Note.** The novel Margaret reads aloud in VII (the drowned brother, the estate) is never named, and the scene is better for it. Leave it.

## 4. Questions a reader is left with

- What became of the thirty days? Fault (finding 4).
- Where did the office's nine hundred pounds come from, and who could stop the office? Fault (finding 5).
- What exactly did Guardian buy: a table, a second computation, or a checked table? Fault, or a deliberate ambiguity that should be named (finding 8).
- Who is Thomas Neale and where did the venture find a checker of his quality in 1851? Mostly virtue; his competence is shown rather than explained. One clause would do no harm.
- Where is the calculating room? A works in Lambeth, a room in the City? Neutral; but the anonymity of the place fits the anonymity of the other three customers, and both together make the second half feel underpopulated.
- What happened to Halden after March 1855, and to Margaret? He appears in XII only as "Halden's question." Virtue in principle (the record outlives him), but one sentence in XII about what became of him would cost nothing and would matter to readers who have followed his household.
- Did Wills find a place? Virtue; the reference is the answer.
- What did Babbage publish "separately, under his own authority" in 1851, and did anyone read it? Virtue; the book is right not to follow him there.
- Was the unfunded successor ever built? Virtue; the title of X is the answer.
- Why did Henry open the packet in 1900? Fault, small (note 50).
- Who put the qualification between the two tables before 1900? Neutral; the image suggests Charles did it, which is the right thing for the reader to suspect.
- What is "the Book of Conditions"? Note 43.

## 5. Reading experience

**I. The Returned Table.** Absorbed at once by the packet and the transposition; the paragraph on the third course ("felt least like a decision") is the best piece of moral accounting in the book. Confused, by design, at the shelf and the last line; on first read I could not say what "parts of the same result" meant.

**II. Thirty Days.** Held by the sparring and by "a map drawn by another person of one's own house." Lost the thread once at "build a metaphor," and missed a year for the whole chapter. The handshake is a strong close.

**III. The Estimator.** Strong: the blank sheet over the drawing, the night of the reversal, "six empty columns." The middle retells the discovery; attention slackened for a page and returned at the exclusions.

**IV. What Can Be Bought.** The Davies dialogue is the crispest in the book ("Before or after I pay?"). Attention dropped in the Whitworth paragraph and the two-column letter, both summary.

**V. The Finite Compact.** The deputy line and "your memory" hold the chapter; the change-clause argument is abstract and I read the capital paragraph twice to check the sum. Babbage holding the pen is the right last image.

**VI. Parts That Would Not Become a Machine.** The most absorbed I was: bodies, benches, the wage book, Friday. Nothing to skim.

**VII. The Call.** The crisis is exact and the Margaret scene is the warmest thing in the book; the novel with the drowned brother is a small gift. Not a moment of confusion.

**VIII. The Sealed Cases.** The set piece works; the false start at the sixth case, "Let him hear the card," Davies's "Read it again," and the three empty strokes at the end are all earned. The one snag was "Neale signed both preparation checks."

**IX. Four Deposits.** Attention dropped in the capacity arithmetic and recovered at the checking strip and the interrupted lesson ("The cards first, Wills."). The signing of the four acceptances is very good. I did the multiplication myself.

**X. The Unfunded Successor.** Most moved here: William and the water, the pencil duel, "It does not read Guardian's source sheet," and the office not knowing who could alter the schedule. Briefly confused by "He did not consent or refuse."

**XI. The Seller's Conditions.** Strong throughout; the reference scene is the book's quiet climax. Confused twice, at "the third rescue" and at who asked for the order to be put in.

**XII. The Complete Record.** Quiet and, in the two headings, earned. The drawing exchange was opaque; "successful papers" stopped me; the 1900 coda is a shade arbitrary but the tape around three sheets is the right last gesture.
