{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"# Blind read (C): answers

I read the whole file (Sections I to VIII, then the questions). Everything below rests on the text alone. Where the text does not settle something I say "unknown" or "ambiguous".

## Q1. Ideas the text seems to convey (most important first)

**1. A claim or promise is only as good as the conditions it is deliberately bounded by, and those conditions have to be written down and then kept.**
The book shrinks an unpriceable grand design into "one finite obligation": "Six registers. Six decimal digits. Thirty card steps... No claim that the object was the Analytical Engine." Everything else goes into a separate "thin book" that "cannot draw one shilling from the apparatus I have priced."
Carried by: II (Lovelace: "Sign the method by which an arrangement is proposed, tried, and refused without carrying the undertaking down with it"; the thirty days); III ("I can't price a thing without an edge"); IV (the second column of what "the undertaking must do": "the reason anyone may believe the machinery"; without it, "a very beautiful clock that nobody is obliged to consult"); V ("This apparatus... is not the Analytical Engine"); VI (Farrow re-machines the accepted interface instead of swapping in Babbage's design: "It isn't this machine yet"); VIII ("The test began with everyone forbidden to improve it"; the signed sentence is limited to twelve sealed cases "under the recorded conditions"; "Do not put them above these signatures"). Section I is the counter-example: a delivery that could "borrow two days from its own conditions", and "We took one witnessed trial and sold four tables upon it."

**2. Trust depends on divided, independent authority: someone other than the doer must be able to check and to say no, and one signature standing in for two hollows out the assurance.**
"They founded the undertaking by deciding who could stop it." "If the same person holds all five, the paper is theatre."
Carried by: II ("You have omitted the man who can say no"); III (who may alter a configuration, hold money, judge manufacture, accept the result, and what follows a failed test); V (the sixteen-page compact splitting architecture, claim, price, manufacture and acceptance among different people, with money released in four stages); VIII (Neale reads every value against Davies's copy; Davies keeps the answer sheet covered until the machine's value is read; "Babbage held nothing that permitted him to alter the apparatus that morning"); and in I, the option Halden took: "let one signature stand temporarily for two and preserve both appearances."

**3. The machine is faithful but cannot judge what it is given. Responsibility sits in preparation, checking and release, and in the institution around the machine, not only in one careless clerk.**
"The Engine carried, as it was built to carry, precisely what it was given." Babbage says blaming the mechanism would "confuse obedience to an operation with judgment upon its premise." Halden answers "Of course it is a human failure" and then moves to "the constitution of the office." "For every hour of its operation, people spent several hours deciding what it should be given, and more deciding whether its answer could leave the room."
Carried by: I; VI (two assemblies each pass their gauges but bind when joined: "The drawings do not tell me which interface owns it"); VIII (the first test morning was "most of it spent by people").

**4. Keeping conditions costs particular people real money and security, and that cost is what tempts the holder of the power to stop to waive them.**
"The mechanism's resistance entered Farrow's life first as Friday." In I: wages due, a returnable 180 pounds, the Lothbury delay. In VII: "six letters and no money"; stopping is "choosing which men would carry the consequence of strangers' fear"; "Every private consequence pressed towards continuation", yet Halden pays the earned wages, stops, and loses his own fee. The text sets his holding the line in 1847 beside his waiver in 1854 and does not explain the change.

**5. Real authority, labor and credit often go unrecognized, and the book keeps a place for what is deferred or uncredited.**
Lovelace's signature governs the test and its claim, "not the venture's money"; she works "inside a household whose legal powers were not hers"; she strikes the deputy clause herself ("Chosen by whom?"); "People will say more. I have had more said about me all my life." Margaret's stationer's accounts: "knowledge without a public title was still knowledge that purchased coal." The successor register lets refused improvements survive ("A change refused here would survive there"; "Enter both"; "It was the first time he called the successor register hers").

## Q2. The apparatus's part in the table that came back wrong

The text presents the apparatus as faithful and not at fault, and also as something that could not have prevented the error.

- It did not cause it. The sealed configuration register was "Unbroken" and the mechanism was "still the mechanism in the room". The run trace "showed no jam, correction, or repeated card. The second run agreed with the first." Babbage: "The recurrence is exact... The first value supplied for forty-seven, and nowhere after it. Every transfer that follows is true. No wheel introduced this." The first divergence is in the preparation copy: Guardian supplied 3,742, the office's copy read 3,472, in the preparer Samuel Wills's hand.
- Its actual part was that of a conduit. It "treated it with perfect fidelity", carrying one transposed starting value through the recurrence into a table whose values "remained orderly and plausible", each differing "by an amount small enough to survive an impatient glance and large enough to alter a later reserve." It had no way to judge or reject a wrong premise: "An absurd answer accused itself. A reasonable wrong answer recruited the reader." Repeating the run only reproduced the result (compare Babbage in VIII: the second run "tests only repetition").
- Its trace and sealed register helped. They let the fault be located in the input ("observe where"), by a quarter past one. Lovelace's list in IV had required the apparatus to "expose a trace".
- The text does not let the exoneration end the matter. "Halden knew that relief. He had felt it himself on finding the seal unbroken. Now Babbage was looking only at the trace." Halden insists "That desk is in this office", and the narration says the machine is the visible "marvel" while "the clerks were furniture. The accounts said otherwise."

## Q3. How the office's commitments related to the people who did its checking

The commitments outran the checking capacity, and checking was the element that gave way.

- "We sold four dates with hands for two." The dates promised to Guardian and to the Lothbury office depended on one independent checker: "Mr Neale had the Lothbury packet". Two commitments claimed the same hands, and the date won over the independent comparison.
- Checking was the easiest thing to bend because it was invisible. The option Halden took "moved no visible object and required no difficult letter. Only a line in the margin had changed." The alternatives (asking Davies for an extension, moving Neale) each meant admitting an oversold or broken promise.
- The people at the bottom absorbed it. With no independent checker, Wills substituted a self-check ("I read it back to myself"; "That is not a comparison"). He arrives "pale", holding his ruler and pencil aligned, and faces the questioning although the release had been authorized above him. Whether Neale was consulted about the waiver, or objected, is unknown.
- Contrast with the office's own earlier principles. Division of labor was supposed to tell "whose hours go on the bill, and whose word stops the wages". In the 1851 test the checkers were central (Neale "signed the preparation check for each run"). In routine work they are what the visitor's eye skips. Meanwhile Guardian never relied on the office's checking: Davies kept a hand calculation "as a check on every table he bought".

## Q4. The margin note in the delivery ledger

- Presentation. It is an italic, terse, signed entry, "Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date. E. H.", in Halden's own hand, in "the margin reserved for an exception". That is a legitimate place, which gives the waiver an official look. The ledger should have carried two marks and carries one. The wording is impersonal ("Delivery permitted") apart from the initials, and what it preserves is "date", not accuracy. It also answers by implication the question Wills would not answer ("Who instructed you to release the cards?").
- How it came to be written. Not by lapse: "He had not forgotten the morning." Wages were due Friday; Guardian's date fell that day and missing it made its 180 pounds returnable; the Lothbury delay would also have cost money, and Neale was on that packet. Halden "had seen the other choices": ask Davies for an extension and admit the date was oversold; take Neale off Lothbury and break that promise; or let one signature stand for two. He chose the one that "had felt least like a decision", telling himself "a single delivery could borrow two days from its own conditions and repay them on Monday." The repayment never came: "Monday had filled itself before it arrived." (Ambiguous whether he knew when writing it that Monday was already full.)
- How it is accounted for. It is treated as a debt that was never repaid. The only accounting in the text is Halden's own. He finds the note after Wills stays silent, says plainly to Babbage "I waived Neale's comparison", and begins the reply to Davies with "There was no second signature." Babbage reads it and holds to "a human failure", calling the office's constitution "a second inquiry". The text does not say whether the waiver itself, or the wages and date pressure behind it, is disclosed to Davies, or what the office will change about exceptions.

## Q5. Who could stop or refuse the undertaking, and what stopping costs

Who:
- The compact deliberately spreads vetoes. Farrow's works are "entitled to reject a drawing that supplied no inspectable condition." Guardian has "the right to accept or refuse the test result" (and may reject before final payment; in I it orders the office to "suspend the related work"). Lovelace's signature is required for the operational examples, comparison method and public claim, and she strikes the deputy clause, so "the test waits" for her. Halden controls price, schedule, staged release of money and, at the test, "the stopping rule" (he calls the stop at the sixth case). Subscribers can stop it by not paying (VII). Babbage holds architecture only, and at the test "nothing that permitted him to alter the apparatus"; he could withdraw ("he did not withdraw").
- The designer does not decide what counts as a correction: "Then we have written sixteen pages to arrive at your memory." Every change is entered in the register first.
- The design responds to earlier refusals that ended everything ("no one had offered him a refusal that did not also end the undertaking"). It tries to make refusal survivable: the thirty days with a written refusal, Halden's fee "for the possibility of refusal" ("The last line may be: build nothing"), and the successor register.

What stopping costs:
- Wages and livelihood, borne by those least able. Farrow's twelve men; earned wages had to be paid first; Halden's managing fee ("He lost his own fee with the works'"); Margaret's night work and a child's room; his 100 pounds "beyond recovery unless the test was reached".
- Time and goodwill. "Babbage did not forgive the lost months, but he did not withdraw." The re-machining cost seventy pounds and eleven weeks. The stop at case six voided a morning and forced a full restart.
- Personal cost for the holder of an irreplaceable veto: Lovelace attends the test while ill ("She resented the necessity and relied upon it").
- Stopping was survivable in 1847: "By spring, two delayed subscriptions arrived... Manufacture resumed with the same accepted configuration. The delay remained in the account."
- In I the costs of stopping (the 180 pounds, the Lothbury delay, a difficult letter) are what Halden avoided, and the cost of not stopping (a returned packet, suspended work, a missing second signature) arrives larger.

## Q6. The value of the apparatus and its test, given what happens afterwards

- The apparatus proves reliable. Three years after the test its register seal is intact, it has "the same limits", the recurrence is "exact", and its trace let the fault be found within hours. The test's public sentence (twelve sealed cases, two complete runs, "under the recorded conditions") is not contradicted by the failure.
- But the test's warrant was narrow and conditional, and the office stretched it. The 1854 run lacked the independent comparison that was part of the recorded conditions. "We took one witnessed trial and sold four tables upon it." The test packet and "Lady Lovelace's qualification on capacity" are "parts of the same result", which suggests the result cannot be separated from its qualifications. What the qualification says is not given.
- The more durable value appears to lie in the method the test embodied: sealed inputs, independent comparison, a trace, stop rules, a claim limited to what was shown. Those are what caught the error in 1854 (Guardian's hand check, the trace) and what had lapsed in the office. The machine is only as trustworthy as the practice around it. Guardian remains a customer but still hand-checks "every table", so the test bought bounded, verified trust, not general trust.
- Its worth for the grand design is deliberately left open: "It may nevertheless disclose something true of it." "That is the question." The text shows no Engine being built. The apparatus is unspectacular ("no printer to dramatize the answer"; nine watchers while "half London" went to the Exhibition), yet its success produced real joy and relief in those who built it.

## Q7. What the text leaves unresolved

Most clearly deliberate:
1. Whether the small apparatus discloses anything true of the Analytical Engine (Babbage: "It may nevertheless disclose something true of it"; Lovelace: "That is the question"). Babbage's "general consequence" is kept outside the signed claim, and the Engine's fate is never shown.
2. Which design was better: "The accepted correction had worked. His own improvement might still have been better. The machine offered no judgment on the route not taken." Both are "entered" and neither is judged.
3. How the 1854 frame resolves. Section I ends with the reply to Davies begun, and the text never returns to 1854. Unknown: whether Davies accepts the account, what clause eleven requires, what becomes of the office, Wills, Neale and Halden, and whether the other three tables sold are wrong. The disagreement between Babbage (a human failure; the office's constitution "may be a second inquiry") and Halden ("one witnessed trial... four tables") is left standing: "For a moment neither man spoke."
4. Why the man who stopped in 1847 waived in 1854. The text gives that morning's pressures but not what had changed in between.

Less clearly deliberate, simply unstated:
- Wills's answer to "Who instructed you to release the cards?" (he "said nothing"), and whether he saw or relied on the margin note.
- What Lovelace's "qualification on capacity" says, and whether she is alive in 1854 (she appears only as a paper on a shelf).
- What clause eleven says.
- How much Margaret shaped Halden's decision (he draws a line under the current balance and the novel reading resumes; the link is implied, not stated).
- The title "The Book of Conditions" is never glossed; which book is meant (successor register, thin book, configuration register, ledger) is ambiguous.

{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"# Blind read (P): answers

Read in full (lines 1 to 1838 of the one file). Answers come from the text alone; where the text does not settle something I say so.

## Q1. Ideas the text is trying to convey (most important first)

**1. A machine's exactness does not make an output right. What makes a table believable is the whole arrangement around the machine (preparation, independent comparison, stated limits, a stopping rule), and a customer buys the table, not the mechanism.**
Babbage separates "obedience to an operation" from "judgment upon its premise". The book grants that the mechanism was exact and then refuses to let that settle anything.
- Ch. I: "No wheel introduced this. The Engine carried, as it was built to carry, precisely what it was given." Also: "For every hour of its operation, people spent several hours deciding what it should be given, and more deciding whether its answer could leave the room."
- Ch. IV: Lovelace's second column, the things "the undertaking must do", "the reason anyone may believe the machinery"; "a very beautiful clock that nobody is obliged to consult".
- Ch. VIII: "The apparatus itself turned for less than an hour."
- Ch. XI and XII: Davies, "I do not doubt your mechanism ... Guardian did not purchase it"; Charles, "The distinction was true ... But they bought the table."
- The Ockham scene makes the same point in miniature ("Our surprise would not be its intention"; "It does not read Guardian's sheet").

**2. Small, locally reasonable exceptions made under money and date pressure wear the safeguards away. Promises get sold beyond real capacity, and the people at the bottleneck absorb it.**
- The margin note in ch. I and ch. X: "borrow two days from its own conditions and repay them on Monday"; "Only a line in the margin had changed"; "Monday had filled itself before it arrived."
- Ch. IX: four deposits against eighty checker-hours ("We sold four dates with hands for two"; "Four deposits are not four deliveries"; the letters' corners "covered the marked line"; "No one altered the figure").
- Ch. X: 1853 to 1854, "No single day announced failure; each exception was carried forward until one could leave the room."
- Friday wages recur as the pressure point (Farrow's "Friday", Margaret's "Is this sum in the bank on Friday?").
- The unseen labour that pays: "the clerks were furniture"; Margaret's work called "help with his books".

**3. A claim should be no larger than its evidence, and a check counts only if it is independent of what it checks.**
- Ch. VIII: the signed sentence ("under the recorded conditions") and Lovelace's "Do not put them above these signatures" against Babbage's "general consequence".
- Ch. III and V: the thin book of exclusions; "This apparatus is not the Analytical Engine."
- Ch. IX: Lovelace's qualification, "not the rate at which customer work could be prepared and independently checked".
- Ch. I: "We took one witnessed trial and sold four tables upon it"; Wills's "I read the copy back to myself" / "That is not a comparison."
- Ch. X: "both checking paths inherited the same earlier value."
- Ch. XI: Halden's refusal of a circular in which "Every sentence could be defended" yet the whole would invite subscribers to fund obligations the account could not meet.

**4. Trust comes from dividing authority and deciding in advance who may refuse or stop. It holds only if the refusers are real, funded and replaceable, and here they were not.**
- Ch. II: "You have omitted the man who can say no."
- Ch. V: "They founded the undertaking by deciding who could stop it"; "deputy, if required" struck through by Lovelace herself ("Chosen by whom?").
- Ch. IX: "And who may refuse the manager?" answered "The account"; Lovelace's "Before the first return arrives, name Mr Neale's deputy."
- Ch. X: "It depends upon my continuing to insist that he is single"; her succession table with "authority to refuse" as a heading, "No row was complete"; "Nobody could say who now held her signature."

**5. Owning an error fully, and keeping the whole record with proof and failure together, is the honest end of such an undertaking even when it costs the work. The bounded result is complete "of that object", not of the grand design.**
- Ch. XI: "pressure of business" struck through and both authorizations "copied ... in full"; Wills's "Only the other part as well"; "I authorized delivery before the independent comparison was complete"; "That preserves the account by surrendering the work." / "It does."
- Ch. XII: the packet "assembled as if for a dispute whose parties might all be dead"; the inventory line "configuration, proof, qualification, error, correction, and closure, complete" with "Of that object. Not of the Engine."; Henry tying the tape around "all three".

## Q2. The apparatus's part in the wrong table

It is presented as the faithful conveyor of the error, not its source.
- The configuration register's seal was "Unbroken". The run trace "showed no jam, correction, or repeated card. The second run agreed with the first."
- Babbage places the fault at "The first value supplied for forty-seven, and nowhere after it. Every transfer that follows is true."
- The bad value was a hand transposition at the preparation desk: Guardian supplied 3,742, the preparation copy read 3,472, and Wills had only "read the copy back to myself", so there was no independent comparison.
- Davies later "accepted the trace and rejected the table."

The text does not treat the apparatus as irrelevant, though:
- Its fidelity is what made the error dangerous. The values stayed "orderly and plausible", and "A reasonable wrong answer recruited the reader." The machine cannot detect a bad premise ("It does not read Guardian's sheet"). Agreement between two runs "tests only repetition" (Babbage, ch. VIII), so an exact trace cannot vouch for the table.
- The bounded design keeps a human hand at both ends ("Manual entry and transcription ... No automatic printing"). Halden's answer to Babbage's printer is "The figure went in by hand. A printer would have printed it."
- Clearing the mechanism is shown as a comfortable relief that can become a dodge: "Halden knew that relief ... Now Babbage was looking only at the trace." Halden will not "answer cancellation with a paragraph about the Engine."
- Babbage fears the machine will take the blame anyway: "They will say the Engine made a wrong table."

So it was executor, not author, of the error. Its exactness clears the mechanism and does not clear the office.

## Q3. How the office's commitments related to the people who did its checking

The commitments were larger than the independent-checking capacity beneath them, and the checkers absorbed the difference.
- Checking was the scarce resource: "independent checking, not preparation, set the boundary". Neale was a borrowed part-timer ("His employer spared him ten hours a week, a hundred and thirty in a quarter on paper"). Halden entered "eighty independent checker-hours" as what he could promise, and "At forty hours per verified packet, the office could deliver two." Four were accepted.
- The commitments were sized by money and dates rather than by checking hours. Deposits "keep Wills paid" and "carry the rent". Babbage: "We are using four obligations to purchase more hours." Training a second checker "consumed the same scarce hours it was meant to increase" (Neale: "If I spend them teaching Wills, I cannot enter them again here as his independent check"). By the fourth acceptance Halden "checked the customer's name, the deposit, and the delivery date", not capacity.
- Neale's craft was not in the plan. His knowledge of illegible originals and fatigue "did not appear in the apparatus's operation count."
- Lovelace's conditions were not met: "Accept no fifth. / Pay for Mr Wills's instruction in hours of its own. / Before the first return arrives, name Mr Neale's deputy." The replies gave her no date ("Neither paper gave her a day"), and Babbage recommended that the office wait.
- Later the dated promises drove the checker. "Neale moved to whichever promised date was nearest"; he "worked, as he had all year, to the nearest promised date, and a delivered table had none." So a promised after-the-fact check had no place in his schedule.
- The checking was the flexible part when promises collided ("I waived Neale's comparison"; "one signature stand temporarily for two"). Neale's time was pledged without his involvement: "You promised my Monday, sir." / "I did."
- The checkers carry the cost. They read aloud until Neale's voice "had roughened", and their names sit on the record. Wills asks that Halden's part be written down too.

## Q4. The ledger margin note

Presentation:
- It is given verbatim, in italics, signed "E. H.", twice: first after the failure (ch. I) as "a short authorization in Halden's own hand" in "the margin reserved for an exception", then at the moment of writing (ch. X, 7 April 1854).
- It is a considered, self-authored choice, not an accident or a subordinate's slip. Halden "had told himself that a single delivery could borrow two days from its own conditions and repay them on Monday."
- The pressures are money and dates: wages due Friday, Guardian's £180 "returnable" if the date was missed, Lothbury's table also due with Neale on it, envelopes filled in a box. In ch. X Lovelace's qualification is on the shelf beside the test packet as he writes.
- He saw the alternatives: ask Davies for an extension and admit the date could not be kept, pull Neale off Lothbury and break that promise, or "let one signature stand temporarily for two". He took the third because it "had felt least like a decision because it moved no visible object and required no difficult letter."
- The note is also an unkept promise, a loan against Monday. Monday was taken by the third office's query and the fourth return. Halden "had meant to tell him" (Neale) "once the query was answered". The line "carried its single mark forward from week to week, as the year's exceptions had", until the packet returned "tied with the office's own green tape". This closes the loop with the book's first sentence.

How it is accounted for:
- Halden owns it at once ("Of course it is a human failure ... I waived Neale's comparison"). His reply to Guardian opens with "there was no second signature" and encloses the ledger page.
- Neale confronts him ("You promised my Monday, sir." / "I did.").
- In the closure resolution the ledger names "the February 1852 four-job authorization and the April 1854 delivery exception". Under "cause of exception" Halden writes "pressure of business", strikes it, and copies "both of his authorizations in full".
- At Wills's prompting he writes into the reference: "I authorized delivery before the independent comparison was complete."
- It is filed with the rest of the packet in ch. XII.
- The cause is spread over a chain: the four-for-two acceptance, the unheeded qualification, Lovelace's death, the scheduling that let delivered tables drop off Neale's list. It is not given as one motive. The debt was in effect repaid at high cost through the refund, correction and closure.

Unsettled: whether Neale was told before the return. The text implies not ("had meant to tell him"; he read the margin and was told by Wills afterward).

## Q5. Who could stop or refuse, and what stopping costs

Formally the compact distributes it:
- Babbage owns the architecture.
- Lovelace's signature is needed for "operational examples, comparison method, and language of any resulting claim". "The test waits" if she cannot attend.
- Halden holds price, schedule, supplier obligation, accepted changes, and "the stopping rule" (he "called the stop" when a register failed to clear).
- Farrow's works may "reject a drawing that supplied no inspectable condition".
- Guardian keeps "the right to accept or refuse the test result".
- Subscription money is released only after four stages.
- The very role is the point of ch. II ("the man who can say no") and of Halden's estimate ("The last line may be: build nothing").

Where refusal actually came from, or failed to:
- Outsiders refused first: the Treasury, Davies ("Guardian purchases calculations"), Whitworth's review ("The proposed date was fiction").
- In 1847 the unpaid calls effectively stopped the work. Halden then followed Lovelace's "pay, stop, publish nothing" rather than Babbage's plan to circulate the improvement notice. Margaret, who has no title, twice makes him look at what is owed first (the Friday sum; "what leaves this house").
- The gap is the manager: "And who may refuse the manager?" is answered "The account". Halden alone signed acceptances. One line in the margin overrode the second comparison.
- After Lovelace's death, and with her request to "accept no work beyond Neale's demonstrated reach" answered by deferral, no one held that refusal.
- In the end Guardian cancelled ("invoked both clauses": the error passed a promised check, or no check occurred), the account ran dry, and Halden closed the office himself.

Costs, which fall first and hardest on those paid by the week:
- "The mechanism's resistance entered Farrow's life first as Friday."
- In 1847 stopping meant Halden lost "his own fee", his £100 was "beyond recovery unless the test was reached", and Margaret took night work.
- Babbage "did not forgive the lost months".
- The re-machined drive cost "seventy pounds and eleven weeks". The voided test run meant losing the completed cases.
- Closure cost the refund, the office, dismantled apparatus, and Wills and Neale paid only "through the closure month". Babbage calls it "preserves the account by surrendering the work", and Halden agrees ("It does").
- The text also shows the cost of not stopping: an exception compounded until it came back as a cancelled contract.
- It also says stopping was cheap only where designed for: "no one had offered him a refusal that did not also end the undertaking" until the successor register.

## Q6. The value of the apparatus and its test, given what follows

- The test was real and narrow. The signed sentence claims only that the frozen apparatus "executed the declared card sequences upon twelve sealed recurrence cases and had reproduced the independently calculated values on two complete runs under the recorded conditions". Its credibility came from conditions (sealed cases held by different people, a ban on improving, a stopping rule, a voided and restarted run, a second full run), not from the machine alone.
- After the failure the test still stands. The traces are "exact", and Davies "accepted the trace". Charles concedes "The distinction was true."
- Its value does not transfer to the office's service. Lovelace's qualification says it established "one frozen operation under prospective comparison", not the rate at which customer work could be prepared and checked. Halden: "We took one witnessed trial and sold four tables upon it." Ch. I says the test packet and the qualification were "parts of the same result", so the limits are part of what the test showed. Nor does the text let it prove the wider design; Lovelace: "Add those consequences to your own paper."
- The success fed the failure. "The first inquiry arrived before the apparatus was covered", and by December there were four, which led to the overcommitment.
- It cannot adjudicate design alternatives ("The machine offered no judgment on the route not taken").
- After the office closes, the apparatus is "dismantled into stored assemblies". What survives is the record: proof, qualification, error, correction and closure filed together, "complete. Of that object. Not of the Engine." Its value is as an honest, bounded demonstration and as evidence of what such a demonstration does and does not license. Whether it "disclose[s] something true" of the larger Engine is left open (see Q7).

## Q7. What the text leaves unresolved

Signposted as open:
- Whether the bounded apparatus tells us anything about the general Analytical Engine: "It may nevertheless disclose something true of it." / "That is the question." Charles ends still separating "that object" from "the Engine".
- Whether Babbage's redesign would have beaten the accepted repair: "His own improvement might still have been better."
- Whether a machine that compares its own operations exercises "judgment". Babbage's "at what exact line would you deny it the word?" gets Lovelace's view (purpose "would still have entered from us") but no concession or resolution.
- Lovelace's succession question, left "unclosed, so the unanswered place remained visible", with "No row was complete".
- Whether she was right to strike out the deputy clause. She says "I would not have let you". William does not confirm she was right; "He asked whether the water was still cool."
- Whether Henry understands. "I understand." / "Do you?" / "No matter. Keep the sentence." What he decides in 1900, beyond re-tying the tape around "all three", is not stated.

Left to inference:
- How blame divides among Wills, Halden, Neale, Babbage, the compact and the pressures. The text strikes out the euphemism but gives no verdict.
- Whether Neale's Monday check would have caught the error, or whether asking Davies for an extension would have saved the office.
- What became of the other customers' tables and whether the year's other exceptions did harm; only Lothbury's is said to have had "both signatures".
- Whether "Accept no fifth" was kept (implicitly yes) and whether Neale's deputy was ever named (implicitly no).
- What becomes of the Engine and drawings after 1900.

Unclear rather than clearly deliberate: Charles's "Not there" when the table is set beside the office accounts (I read it as his resisting either filing); Halden reading "inventor" twice in a salutation (a hint of vanity in accepting the fourth deposit, planted but not developed).

{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"Blind read of readback-control.md. I read only that file, and every answer below rests on its text alone.

Q1. UNKNOWN. The text never says whether Neale knew the Guardian copy had gone out without his comparison. What it does give:
- Wills says "Mr Neale had the Lothbury packet," and the narration says "Neale had been checking the Lothbury office's table."
- Halden's waiver is recorded only as a ledger margin note, "Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date."
- The narration says that course "moved no visible object and required no difficult letter. Only a line in the margin had changed."
This hints that nobody was formally told. But no line says Neale was told, was not told, or reacted. Neale is never shown in person in chapter I, and Halden's "I waived Neale's comparison" is said to Babbage after the return, not to Neale before it. So I cannot say he knew or did not know.

Q2. ONLY PARTLY ANSWERED. The text's own reason is that Halden "had told himself that a single delivery could borrow two days from its own conditions and repay them on Monday," but "Monday had filled itself before it arrived." All it records afterwards is "There was no second signature."
- It does not say what filled Monday, whether anyone tried later, or how long passed between delivery and the packet's return. The question's "weeks" is not in the text, which gives only "two days" and "Monday."
- The nearest underlying cause is Halden's summary "We sold four dates with hands for two." Chapter IX supports it: "At forty hours per verified packet, the office could deliver two." But the text never states that this is why the Monday comparison did not happen; that link is my inference.

Q3. Who ordered it: HALDEN. The delivery ledger's exception margin holds "a short authorization in Halden's own hand," "Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date. E. H.," and he says "I waived Neale's comparison." One caveat: that note authorizes "Delivery." The text never shows him ordering the cards' release itself. Asked "Who instructed you to release the cards?", Wills gave no answer: "The clerk said nothing."
Whom he told: NO ONE IS NAMED. The only telling recorded is that "Halden had told himself" it could be repaid on Monday. He passed over "He could have asked Davies for an extension," and the course he took "required no difficult letter." Whether he told Wills, Neale, Guardian or Babbage at the time is unknown.

Q4. UNKNOWN. The question's premise does not match the text. After the table returns, Babbage says nothing about why he built his engines, and Halden answers no such remark.
- Babbage's after-return lines concern where the error lies:
  - "The Engine carried, as it was built to carry, precisely what it was given." This describes how it was built to behave, not why it was built.
  - "It remains a human failure."
  - "To charge the mechanism with the table is to confuse obedience to an operation with judgment upon its premise."
- Halden's replies there are "Of course it is a human failure" and "We took one witnessed trial and sold four tables upon it." Neither answers a statement of purpose.
- The nearest remark on purpose is Babbage's in chapter IX: "A machine exists precisely to free us from the pace of human repetition. I have argued that for twenty years." It is spoken in the February 1852 scene, before the table returns. Chapter I already has the 1851 test packet and Lovelace's qualification on Halden's shelf and the four dates sold. It is also about machines in general.
- In that scene Lovelace replies ("It has freed the operation... It has not freed us from deciding what operation we asked for"). Halden only cuts in on "A second apparatus—" with "Isn't in any contract or any account."

Q5. Does he believe the machine erred? NO. He says "No wheel introduced this," "It remains a human failure," and "it is not a failure of the calculating mechanism."
What he fears: UNKNOWN. The text never states a fear of his.
- The closest are things he resists: charging "the mechanism with the table," and moving "from one supplied value to the constitution of the office," which he calls "a second inquiry."
- "I had not expected to meet it here" reads as surprise or dismay, not fear.
- The narration credits the mechanism's exoneration with relief ("Halden knew that relief"), not fear.
Calling any of this a fear would be my inference.

{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"Blind read of readback-passage.md (the only file I opened). Answers from the text alone.

Q1. Probably no, but the text never says so outright, so this is an inference and not a settled fact.
Rests on: Halden gave the release order to Wills, not to Neale: "Mr Neale will compare the copy on Monday." Neale was then at his desk on the Lothbury figures. The text says Halden "could walk twenty feet" but does not say he did. After the Monday query, Halden "had meant to tell him about Guardian's copy". That implies he had not yet told him, and no later telling is reported. Neale's first reaction in the text comes on the day the packet returned. He "read the margin of the delivery ledger" and said "You promised my Monday, sir", which reads like discovery.
Not settled: nothing rules out Wills (who saw "the single mark" and "the margin") or someone else telling Neale in the meantime. Also, Neale's "my Monday" refers to a Monday that is not in the ledger margin as quoted ("Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date."). How he knew of it is unexplained.

Q2. The text gives a chain of causes rather than one cause. The time and the notice never reached Neale.
- On Monday, the day Halden named for the comparison, the third office's signed return arrived with a query, and "Neale's hours went to the query."
- Halden "had meant to tell him about Guardian's copy once the query was answered". The text never reports that he did and never says why not (unknown).
- On Tuesday the fourth return arrived. Neale "worked, as he had all year, to the nearest promised date, and a delivered table had none". So the already-delivered Guardian table never came to the front of his work.
- Nothing forced the exception to close: the Guardian line "carried its single mark forward from week to week, as the year's exceptions had".
Background, implied and not stated as the cause: checking rested on "a single man" with limited hours ("I have eighty hours, sir"; "Four packets at forty hours make a hundred and sixty"). The proposed fixes for capacity were put off ("He recommended that the office wait").

Q3. Halden ordered it. He wrote in the ledger margin, "Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date." signed "E. H.", and said aloud to Wills, "Release them." So at the time the only person he told was Wills, plus the written ledger entry.
As far as the text shows, he did not tell Neale (he only "had meant to" later). He did not tell Guardian: the course he chose "required no difficult letter", and asking Davies for an extension is listed as a road not taken. He did not tell Babbage, who first reads the authorization after the return ("Babbage read the authorization without sitting down").

Q4. Babbage says: "I began the first engine because tables computed and copied by hand were wrong." He says he gave it a printer "so that no hand need copy a figure between the machine and the page", and that Halden "struck the printer from your first report."
Halden answers: "The figure went in by hand. A printer would have printed it." My gloss, inferred from the exchange: the bad figure entered by hand before the machine, and a printer that only removes hand-copying after the machine would have printed the wrong figure faithfully. Halden then adds that he will not "answer cancellation with a paragraph about the Engine."
Note: the text has Babbage speaking of "the first engine" (and a printer). It does not give a wider account of why he built engines in the plural.

Q5. No. Babbage holds that the machine did not err and that the fault is human. In Chapter I he says "The Engine carried, as it was built to carry, precisely what it was given", that "It remains a human failure", and that the office's constitution "is not a failure of the calculating mechanism". After the recomputation, "The correction had required no alteration to the mechanism. Babbage wanted the response to say so."
What he fears is what people will say, not a fault in the machine. "They will say the Engine made a wrong table." A trace "will not govern what people say." Members of both Houses have twice asked "whether the machine gives right answers when it is given wrong figures", and now "They will think this table has answered them."
Not settled: the text does not spell out what consequence he dreads beyond this public and parliamentary misattribution. Anything more (loss of support, funding) would be a guess.

These are supported pressures, not a single proven psychological cause.

{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"Independent informed content review recommends retaining all six values after clarifying their scope. Current rendered Chapter IX.scene.03 and Chapter X.scene.01–02 distinguish continuing informal supervised lessons from deferred protected paid release and outside instruction. The old aggregate chapter nodes are nonrendered historical text. E17 preserves that supervised practice consumes checking time and does not establish qualification or additional independent hours. The new March interruption is one mechanism, not proof that every lesson was displaced, Wills could never qualify, or a funded program would guarantee success. The reviewed material included E06, E17–E21, relevant life boundaries and U04/U05/U08/U10/U12/U15. Framing and deciding are correctly conditional on their corresponding HOW shares on the same carrier. All six compositions sum to one. The reader knows the 1854 failure from Chapter I, but Lovelace’s 1852 assessment must rest on then-known capacity, commitments, illness and replies, not future knowledge. This was an informed review with model context and a follow-up discussion of scope, not a blind text-only test.

Retain impartial .62, personal .29, remainder .09. The request attends chiefly to demonstrated competence, paid time and authority to refuse; personal attachment remains explicit in the refused deputy, William and bodily limits. Impartial means conditions whose force does not change solely with who is involved, not moral purity. The new funding distinction removes neither side.

Retain the existing emotion composition, with scope clarified. Fear .25, sadness .22, anticipation .17 and trust .14 plausibly characterize threatened succession, illness, renewed requests and collaboration. Joy .01 is the least directly supported numerical choice, but no defensible replacement follows: the brief laughter and recovered speed are real, while this Cut is an authored succession-focused attention composition, not an emotion intensity score, duration measurement or constant state throughout August. Do not treat its exact share as proven by the prose.

Retain abstract .36, concrete .55, remainder .09. Reserved hours, outside instruction, £120, the missing date, incomplete table and source sheet support concrete emphasis. Internal comparison versus independent evidence and authority versus enduring function retain abstract framing. Specifying paid release strengthens existing concrete evidence without requiring a new number.

Retain deciding .46, framing .45, remainder .09. She both reorganizes the problem into competence/time/refusal authority and presses the men to act within demonstrated reach. Near-balanced framing and deciding remains an authored interpretation; the .01 difference is not an extracted measurement.

Retain threatened .76, assured .16, remainder .08. Supervised lessons establish possibility, not independent capacity or a funded date. Missing reserved hours sustain predominantly threatened fulfillment; Neale, current teaching and collaboration support some assurance. This is not the probability of the 1854 failure and is distinct from the fear share.

{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"A1: Neale (guess) - clipped clerk's answer about the strip; A2 then addresses "Mr Neale", so he is probably the previous speaker
A2: Wills (guess) - deferential "Mr Neale", a junior correcting a senior; a Babbage or Halden reading is possible
A3: Babbage (guess) - Engine vocabulary (difference, first card) and wants the explanation ahead of the refund, the worry A5 spells out
A4: Halden (guess) - flat "the trace is enough" position that A6 builds on ("the clerk has his line in the trace"); could be Wills or Neale
A5: Babbage (sure) - his own anecdote about being asked by both Houses whether wrong figures give right answers; grievance ending in a sting
A6: Halden (sure) - "What did Guardian purchase?", "Mine is in the ledger", refuses to spin the refund; short blunt sentences and a contraction
B1: Babbage (guess) - analogy plus grievance; the "we/purchase/obligations" register could be Halden
B2: Lovelace (guess) - two-word challenge to the claim that hours can be bought; could equally be Halden
B3: Halden (guess) - plain payroll fact answering "From whom?"; could be Babbage
B4: Lovelace (guess) - raises the customer requirement as an objection; could be Halden, less likely Neale
B5: Halden (guess) - practical concession, and "stage" echoes his later "stagger"; could be Babbage
B6: Lovelace (guess) - precise clarifier ("I know. I mean..."); could be Halden
B7: Babbage (sure) - "I have argued that for twenty years", tides simile
B8: Lovelace (likely) - measured ironic distinction; "leave you both to it" sounds like the third party
B9: Babbage (likely) - proposes another machine; interrupted mid-sentence
B10: Halden (likely) - "contract" and "account" language, blunt interruption
B11: Halden (likely) - deposits, rent, "accept no fifth"
B12: Babbage (guess) - "Mr Halden" in the third person rules Halden out; could be Lovelace
B13: Halden (likely) - "We began at opposite ends"; "Mr Babbage" in the third person rules Babbage out
B14: Lovelace (guess) - tests the "four" arithmetic; could be Halden or Babbage
B15: Neale (likely) - terse conditional answer using the "hours in the account" frame
B16: Halden (guess) - hours-and-accounts question put to the man Neale calls "sir"; could be Babbage
B17: Neale (sure) - "I have eighty hours, sir"
Easiest: Babbage lecturing or nursing a grievance, Neale's first-person hours with "sir", Halden's ledger and contract talk. Hardest: short plain lines; Halden against Lovelace on questions and clarifications, Babbage against Halden on B1, B3, B5, B12; Neale against Wills in A1, A2, A4 close to a coin flip. Lovelace clearly identifiable only in B8.

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"revision","text":"Modeling Lovelace's speech over time showed a line the text had not caught up with: at the trial in May 1851 her illness shortens her speech to the condition and the command, yet before the first run she argued in full, polished sentences. Revised in VIII: 'After we record the disagreement,' she said, and waited for her breath. 'Alter the source first, and the answer has chosen its own question.' and, to Babbage's 'A misplaced source figure is not a trial of the Engine': 'Then it is a trial of us.' The other eleven speech episodes already match the passages that render them."}
nodes.title: The trial argument follows Lovelace's modeled voice

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"revision","text":"Seventeen passages changed after the voice records and model revision 19. Babbage's lines lengthen into qualification and sardonic asides and carry his documented grievances (the Treasury's economy with words, Clement keeping the tools, the members of both Houses and their wrong figures). Lovelace negotiates in conditions and turns figurative about the Engine (a function of the other two; the loom that weaves flowers; 'I have been said more about all my life'). Halden speaks plainly, in sums and contractions ('I can't price a thing without an edge'). Five narrator closers that only restated a scene are cut. Lines both readers singled out are kept as they were: 'Let him hear the card', 'Judgment is often the name...', 'sixteen pages to arrive at your memory', Davies's 'Before or after I pay?', and the Ockham and Chapter XII exchanges. 12,715 words."}

Bodily limits narrow space while model insight remains active; a correct insight remains unfunded. William protects rest without confiscating papers. Ada can recognize a shared-source flaw without foreseeing the later transposition. Her death is elsewhere and is not itself the cause of the delivery error. Do not resolve the unfunded function by treating internal comparison as independent source judgment. Earlier informal lessons are now reader knowledge. The additional commitment is protected paid release and outside instruction; the missing date and deferral refer specifically to that arrangement. The chapter now ends on the Friday of 7 April 1854: both dates fall due, Halden writes the exception and orders the cards released, and the Monday that was to repay it is taken by the next returns. The qualification lies on the shelf unanswered. After Lovelace's death nobody holds her claim signature. Guardian's and Lothbury's are the two small packets, which is why both dates could fall on the first Friday. The Monday falls in the first fortnight of the war. Nobody told Neale of Guardian's Monday; working to the nearest promised date, he never reached a delivered table. Revision 28: the reader now learns at the Friday that the two dates are the first the office has ever promised, so its name is at stake beside its deposit. {"id": "story.fact.book.office-capital.20260929", "chapter": 9, "claim": "The office is constituted in January 1852 with £900 (£650 from Babbage, £150 of the Halden household's savings, the £100 construction reserve) and promises two signatures beneath each table.", "event_id": "event.book.07r2.E16a", "path": "/description", "evidence": {"node_id": "document.book.07r2.chapter.09.scene.01", "quote": "The calculation office was constituted in January 1852, in the solicitor's room
where the compact had been signed. Babbage put in six hundred and fifty pounds.
Halden put in a hundred and fifty, most of what his household had saved since
the first venture, and the hundred pounds left unspent from the construction
account made nine hundred. The apparatus came to the office in its frozen
configuration. The stopping clauses were copied from the compact, and every
customer was to receive two signatures beneath each table: the preparer's and
an independent checker's."}, "reader_first_known": {"nodeId": "document.book.07r2.chapter.09.scene.01", "boundary": "end"}, "epistemic_status": "authored_fiction", "assertion_scope": "Only this separate fact, not every fact in the native Event, becomes disclosed here."}

{"id": "story.fact.book.restart.20260927", "chapter": 8, "claim": "A first attempt fails to clear, is stopped, and the complete run starts over.", "event_id": "event.book.07r2.E14a", "path": "/description", "evidence": {"node_id": "document.book.07r2.chapter.08.scene.01", "quote": "At the sixth, one register failed to clear completely. Halden called the stop
before anyone could decide that the remaining digit was harmless. The card was
marked and the incomplete run was voided. Davies had already leaned towards the
glass. Irritation crossed his face before he told one clerk to note the card and
the other to leave the locked case shut. Under observation the register was
reset, the inputs were restored, and the full twelve-case sequence began again
from its first declared card. The interruption entered the trace; it was not
smuggled into either accepted run. Babbage objected to losing the completed
cases and then, seeing Davies watch him, objected to nothing further."}, "reader_first_known": {"nodeId": "document.book.07r2.chapter.08.scene.01", "boundary": "end"}, "epistemic_status": "authored_fiction", "assertion_scope": "Only this separate fact, not every fact in the native Event, becomes disclosed here.", "reviewedGraphHash": "558c9b648e0f70ace8eb1a67a36a7b03860838fa7f3e0e509b40b5d84b546a16", "reviewedModelHash": "6f190085425f479b0f1ba6753f6a02419942fdf527dff4f1b9de24e46a169e4c"}

{"schema":"meaning-model-story-author-record/v1","kind":"assessment","text":"Telling process for the idea 'The exception that felt like no decision': where the reader meets it, where the story tests it, where it lands.","data":{"schema":"meaning-model-document-process/v1","documentId":"document.book.07r2","label":"Idea: The exception that felt like no decision","question":"Where does the reader meet the idea 'The exception that felt like no decision', where is it tested, and where does it land?","summary":"The failure is not a dramatic wrong but an honest, temporary exception that moves no visible object and is carried forward by routine until it becomes permanent. Accountability is naming one's own authorization in full, not the pressure that explained it. The phases follow its strategy through the chapters: an authored reading of where the text carries the idea, not a measure of what readers take from it; the controlled read-back tests that.","states":[{"label":"Met: a line in the margin","spanId":"document.span.book.chapter.01.20260927","description":"Halden finds his own hand in the margin and remembers why the third course felt like no decision.","evidence":[{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.01.scene.03","excerpt":"The third course had felt least like a decision because it moved
no visible object and required no difficult letter."},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.01.scene.03","excerpt":"Monday had filled itself before it arrived."}],"basisUnits":[{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.01.scene.01","contentHash":"fa2e10c492a812d94a2bb947bbb9a6a2d52676dcb6a009bfad6f1381fcbbe84d"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.01.scene.02","contentHash":"899879bb75fc4c0003dbe5cb21e1003a403118044058ccebcab45fb7149873a7"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.01.scene.03","contentHash":"aee70a72b4a41c56a8c4557f3d68c1a9db002a0808adaf3633e0ca607da6f61b"}]},{"label":"Tested: the fourth acceptance","spanId":"document.span.book.chapter.09.20260927","description":"The same shape at the office's founding: a salutation read twice, and by the fourth acceptance the capacity sheet no longer looked at.","evidence":[{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.09.scene.02","excerpt":"One letter had called him inventor."},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.09.scene.02","excerpt":"By the fourth he no longer looked at the capacity sheet."},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.09.scene.03","excerpt":"He did not cancel it."}],"basisUnits":[{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.09.scene.01","contentHash":"1c16bc2a6864e34496efd940bbbb48111df224848f78ab978aa7f257428eaa43"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.09.scene.02","contentHash":"9045f65f7c79819b3de1a53a3bfe86264d4f944e0d0dc054f473e6bcafd02653"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.09.scene.03","contentHash":"0396fbd77d4776542ba34632752e6aae545a47203e1d947117fb3a9867c0f2d0"}]},{"label":"Tested: carried forward","spanId":"document.span.book.chapter.10.20260927","description":"Through 1853 no day announces failure; on the Friday Halden writes the exception, and on the Monday he means to tell Neale.","evidence":[{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.10.scene.04","excerpt":"No single
day announced failure; each exception was carried forward until one could leave
the room."},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.10.scene.04","excerpt":"Halden had meant to tell him about Guardian's copy once the query was
answered."}],"basisUnits":[{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.10.scene.01","contentHash":"add206e7273b5098ed34372437efa8a304dc9336536fdc7f0701f059e097fd6a"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.10.scene.02","contentHash":"db495628837cc68158fdecb9f5b20eb8d45649ecb775412b6e0519f03dde3bfe"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.10.scene.03","contentHash":"24cf9b64a556115940cb34ea999d6ca933092fa9bbf4789df774f5f0cea4993c"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.10.scene.04","contentHash":"3e81da5da67788fb05c93d67123b3e249bd2e37a3bdf2eb0e6ad9234982b9be9"}]},{"label":"Lands: both authorizations in full","spanId":"document.span.book.chapter.11.20260927","description":"He strikes 'pressure of business' and copies his authorizations; at Wills's asking the reference names the order as well as the copying.","evidence":[{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.11.scene.02","excerpt":"He read

answer recruited the reader."},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.01.scene.03","excerpt":"Monday had filled itself before it arrived."}],"basisUnits":[{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.01.scene.01","contentHash":"fa2e10c492a812d94a2bb947bbb9a6a2d52676dcb6a009bfad6f1381fcbbe84d"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.01.scene.02","contentHash":"899879bb75fc4c0003dbe5cb21e1003a403118044058ccebcab45fb7149873a7"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.01.scene.03","contentHash":"58d473f6fb0b7b2ca21b9dedbd93b82976499d6d9e23c3723f7efb5351d46524"}]},{"label":"Ironic and interior, then quiet","spanId":"document.span.book.chapter.02.20260927","description":"Close to Babbage's indignation and Lovelace's history; after the voice pass it leaves Babbage's laughter unexplained and lets the principals carry the wit.","evidence":[{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.02","excerpt":"with

A reading of how the telling changes the stakes of refusal: the opening makes an absent check an acknowledged failure; the earlier bargain makes refusal possible; stopping then costs money and standing; anticipated capacity weakens the constraint; a worker finally asks that the superior’s choice travel with his own error. This is dramatic pressure expressed through changing alternatives and agency, not a measure of a reader’s arousal or a verdict that every pause is right. Nora’s unsettled_account and bodily_tempo invite attention to who must carry a correct condition. The phases are authored interpretations, grounded in exact excerpts. nodes.text:
## U01 — Why a third principal exists

Targets: E02--E06; Edward Halden's life.

Babbage and Lovelace can continue a negotiation but cannot, between them,
supply independent manufacture, commercial staging, and liability. The third
principal therefore carries the narrow integration function that makes the
divergence causal. He is fictional because assigning all of that function to a
known historical figure would distort the evidence. He does not absorb the
manufacturer, customer, financier, or successor roles.

nodes.text:
## U02 — Why the machine is small

Targets: the Bounded Card Apparatus; E03, E06, E14.

A completed general Analytical Engine by 1851 would require far more
counterfactual industrial change than the story needs. A six-register,
addition-and-subtraction, card-directed apparatus gives the founders something
real to finish and test while preserving the distinction between the bounded
artifact and Babbage's architecture. If later technical opening shows even this
configuration to be implausible, reduce its registers or card sequence rather
than enlarging the industrial world to rescue it.
nodes.title: U02 — Why the machine is small

nodes.text:
## U03 — Why success is the central shock

Targets: E14--E18.

Another mechanical failure would merely confirm every existing caution. A
bounded success changes the principals' wants and interpretations in different
directions and creates the temptation the conditions were designed to resist.
It therefore produces both stronger causality and a better story: their method
works, then they misstate what its success licenses.

## U04 — Why the office fails outside the mechanism

Targets: E17--E27.

The tested arithmetic should remain true. The office fails because recurring
calculation is a human-machine process containing preparation, checking,
delivery, correction, and money. The known two-job checking capacity, the
four-job commitment, the specific transposition, and the omitted duplicate
check make the failure traceable without making the apparatus magically break
at the required dramatic moment.

## U05 — Why Lovelace's death is not the cause of the error

Targets: E19--E24.

Her illness and death expose a succession failure already visible in the 1852
capacity review. The surviving principals choose not to fund a second checker
before she dies. Death removes her active pressure; it does not enter a wrong
number or force Halden's later delivery decision. This preserves agency and
avoids using a woman's death as a mechanical plot device.

## U06 — Why the ending is documentary

Targets: E27--E30.

The counterfactual earns one bounded proof, not an industrial revolution. The
complete packet is a meaningful surviving object because it contains success
and failure under the same identity. Babbage's late growth is the decision not
to curate away the parts that limit his preferred interpretation.

## U07 — Revision from the first candidate round

Targets: the whole 07r2 construction.

The earlier candidate passes showed that a plausible macro outcome was not enough:
continued negotiation lacked a person capable of converting it into priced,
staged obligations. This version retains the useful bounded-proof and
overcommitment pattern, adds the missing commercial founder, and narrows the
long-run outcome. Discarded casts, signature objects, prose, and numerical
worlds are not part of this construction.

## U08 — Pragmatic revision rule

Targets: all later openings.

When a finer event is uncertain but does not change the parent account, keep it
coarse or put it in the remainder. When a local route is weak, repair that
route. When the children reveal that the parent could not have happened, or
that the only coherent realization is dramatically inert, revise the parent
and propagate the change. Do not restart a whole world to avoid making an
ordinary authorial choice.

## U09 — Why this world is accepted

Targets: the complete macro, E01--E30, and the twelve-passage route.

Progressive opening found local defects—the access route to Halden, the formal
authority behind the 1852 contracts, and the exact 1854 delivery choice—but no
failure of the parent history. Farrow now supplies the access route, Halden
alone binds the customers after Babbage urges expansion, and the omitted check
has its own Direction Cut. The ledgers close, the prospective test remains
valid, and each principal's late action grows out of an earlier pattern. The
world is therefore accepted at its declared resolution. Unopened workshop,
subscriber, and customer detail stays remainder rather than delaying the book.

## U10 — Why assurance and threat are separated from fear

Targets: the principal period profiles; selected-scene WHAT and FEELS Cuts;
passages I--XII.

The five core wants identify what is receiving motivational attention. They do
not by themselves say whether the person expects those wanted endpoints to be
secured. The added outlook Cut therefore divides one comparable unit between
assured fulfillment, threatened fulfillment, and unresolved expectation; its
threat child may then be opened across the five wanted regions. Fear remains a
separate emotional appraisal because the same represented threat can instead
organize anger, sadness, bargaining, or action. This distinction guided a
small rendering revision: Babbage classifies mechanisms under threat,
Lovelace converts uncertainty into explicit conditions, and Halden moves from
bounded accounting through promotional accounting to self-audit. No world
event or causal dependency changed.

## U11 — Why the emotional-depth pass adds residue rather than shocks

Targets: E09--E11, E14, E18--E28; passages II, V, VII--XII.

The accepted world already contains the required long perturbations: earlier
institutional rupture makes finite dependence threatening to Babbage; bounded
success destabilizes both him and Halden; Lovelace's foreseeable absence tests
whether authority has a carrier; and the returned table forces a slow change in
what counts as the work's complete record. Adding another catastrophe would
weaken that causality. The revision instead repeats existing objects with
changed use—drawings cover ledgers, deposit letters cover the capacity line,
handwriting widens, checking tools wear, and proof and failure remain under one
tape. Explanatory prose was removed where those residues could show adaptation.

## U12 — Why character refinements change the model before the rendering

Targets: E04, E06, E09, E14, E17, E20, and E26; passages II--XII.

Lovelace's fallibility and the secondary people's lives need consequences beyond
their assigned jobs. The smallest correction does not add a new shock. It opens consequences
already latent in accepted Events. In the finite compact Lovelace declines an
unspecified deputy because substitution could dissolve the rare authority she
has won; in 1852 she recognizes that this protection also made her a single
carrier, which sharpens rather than magically supplies her succession argument.
Davies's curiosity makes evidential restraint a choice, Farrow protects his
foreman's finding despite delayed payment, and Neale tries to teach Wills
without counting supervised practice as independent capacity, then shares
responsibility for the correction. These refinements were entered in the life
and Event descriptions before their passages were revised. They do not alter
the macro outcome or any existing Cut composition. The remaining changes remove
balanced, thesis-bearing speech and replace it with handling, interruption, and
profession-specific language; those are rendering changes rather than new
world facts.

nodes.text:
## U13 — Why invention joy is deepened

Targets: E03, E10, E14, E16, and E18; the finite-invention and
recognition-to-overreach change arcs; passages III, VI, VIII--X.

The rendering moves too quickly from making to governance.
The repair therefore opens experiences already causal in the accepted world.
Halden's reversal from pricing a machine part to pricing an answerable claim is
treated as a cognitive invention; the corrected assembly's first free motion is
allowed to reward several kinds of expertise; and the successful trial is
experienced as shared joy before commercial attention arrives.

The pleasure is not an ornamental scene. E14 changes beliefs about feasibility,
standing, and the value of each participant's work. E16 reinforces those
beliefs. In E18 Babbage and Halden then mistake two judgments moved by the same
success and response for independent confirmation. This was already the
recognition-to-overreach arc; the revision makes its positive shock perceptible.
That common-cause account belongs to the constructor's model and is not given to
Lovelace as an explicit diagnosis in the rendered scene. She can demonstrate
the capacity error without possessing the whole explanation of either man.
Accordingly, only the three immediate post-trial FEELS Cuts change. Their joy
shares rise and their anticipatory shares fall because the named moment is now
fixed after the second complete run and before the first inquiry. WHAT, HOW,
fulfillment outlook, threat, and Direction Cuts remain unchanged.

The same macro history and failure remain. The revision develops four literary
functions—cognitive discovery, pleasure in matter,
shared recognition, and intellectual intimacy under bodily cost—through the
current model's existing Events, relationships, Cuts, and change arcs.

## U14 — Why Lovelace discusses mechanical judgment

Targets: E20 and E20a; E23--E26 and E28; passage X; the valid-computational-claim
concept model.

Lovelace's published 1843 Notes already distinguish the Engine's ability to
follow supplied analytical relations from any power to originate those
relations, while also proposing that suitably represented relations outside
ordinary number—including harmony—could be subjected to operation. Passage X
does not quote the Notes or attribute modern terminology to her. It develops
those documented positions inside the counterfactual self-comparison design.

The exchange changes a record: a common-source fault causes Babbage to narrow
mechanical verification to comparison of internal operations. Lovelace states
only the distinction between an unforeseen consequence and intention.
Guardian's source sheet, followed by the returned table, supplies the adverse
case.

nodes.text:
## U15 — Why voice and sensory detail are consequences of the model

Targets: principal life trajectories; E03, E06, E10, E14, E18, E20--E21, and E26;
passages I--XI.

The voice pass adds no Event, Cut, causal dependency, or outcome. Sentence
movement and diction are derived from the person's existing organization:
Babbage expands from the local question toward architecture, Lovelace translates
between representations and grows terser as bodily capacity declines, and
Halden names hours, money, workers, dates, and deliverables. Secondary voices
use the narrower evidence their work makes available. These are rendering
constraints recorded in `PERSON-MODELS.md`, not new personality coordinates.

Sensory detail is likewise rendered from Things already participating in an
Event and from their changing state: coupled assemblies transmit load, heat,
and vibration; the trial exposes cards, register faces, the slowing shaft, and
the sealed comparison case; the succession episode exposes drawings, breath,
packets, and the cold apparatus. A city or room remains a Place Thing; presence
and any consequential weather, traffic, work, or crowd condition are Events in
its lifecycle. A separate place Event is opened only if that condition changes
access, timing, choice, or consequence. This keeps atmosphere available without
letting an unmodeled detail become a hidden cause.

The final bounded prose pass opens the already recorded deputy refusal and
its later recognition, without adding a successor or changing the plot.
Lovelace hesitates before striking the provision; in illness she asks William
about the signature and admits she would have refused his substitution.
Recognition does not settle her attachment to the authority she secured.
Several narrator explanations are removed where the action already supplies
their meaning, and a few exchanges lose their immediate polished rebuttals.
E06, E20, the person description, and the route retain those same choices.
The Cut weights, accounting, dates, capacity, outcomes, and ending are
unchanged. A fresh retrospective import is required to bind the revised
descriptions and manuscript to their new source identities.

nodes.text:
## U16 - Connect preparation to the final checking window

Targets: E09, E17--E18, E22--E24; passages VI, IX, and X.

A fresh complete-manuscript reading identified a missing link: at forty hours
per packet, four checks appear finishable long before the 1854 delivery unless
the reader knows why the final inputs are not yet available. The world model
already placed all four checks in one delivery quarter. This pass opens that
commitment: methods and specimen work precede customer returns closed at the
end of 1853; final figures arrive in early 1854 for April--June delivery.
Earlier checking cannot certify those new values. This is an authored source
dependency, not a fifth customer, new historical evidence, or new work invented
to consume every intervening hour.

Halden's error remains a gamble on future capacity followed by a refusal to
fund it. The existing 80-hour capacity, 40-hour final check, four contracts,
cash accounts, and decision Cuts are unchanged. The model descriptions and
loadable scaffold request are updated before the prose. The scene then shows
old checking marks being set aside instead of adding a speech about scheduling.

The same reading caught two consecutive Babbage speeches that looked like
alternating speakers in VI. His claim that the failure justifies the larger
redesign is joined into one attributed speech. No character position changes.
The witnessed test, emotional palette, death, closure, and custody ending are
preserved. This pass does not claim a fresh Rust import.

nodes.text:
## U17 - Retrospective Rust import and the final-source cutoff

Targets: E17--E24; passages IX--X; the concept component Cut and person scaffolds.

The construction review distinguished a coherent authored artifact from a
complete native execution record. This repair imports the existing descriptions,
person processes, Cuts, and manuscript into a new database. It records the
source digests and new compilation and retrieval results; it does not recover
earlier editing order. The concept allocation gains an explicit zero remainder
and component addresses. All thirteen declared person profiles now request
their nine concurrent processes. Slow outlook remains authored: unselected
scenes are not invented to manufacture a temporal-mixture proof.

Checking the source schedule exposed a remaining causal weakness in U16's
refinement. Returns available during the first quarter could consume that
quarter's checking hours before April--June. The revised authored arrangement
is that customers reconcile the year-end returns during the first quarter,
then release the final signed checking copies from 1 April 1854. Guardian's
copy arrives on that date; other April arrivals remain coarse. Work on earlier
specimens or provisional figures cannot replace comparison against these final
copies. E22's window extends through April, and the model, route, and two
affected passages carry the same constraint.

This supersedes U16's source-availability assumption, not its preserved account
of the earlier revision. The four jobs, forty hours per final check, eighty
protected quarter-hours, omission on 7 April, refund, closure, and ending do
not change. Nor do the psychological weights. The alteration is a local repair
to the causal explanation, not new historical evidence or a rerolled world.

nodes.title: An accurate account can fail to answer another person

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"The ending already names a bounded object: configuration, proof, qualification, error, correction and closure. Nora’s new compositional question is whether faithful custody can leave the people more various than this account of their undertaking. Her own later relapse into planning Kit’s life prevents an easy claim that recognition permanently cures a habit. Preserve Babbage’s impatient last question and Henry’s separate life; do not add a concluding thesis. This is a new interpretation linked to the received ending, not recovered intent."}
nodes.title: Complete of an object, not complete of a person

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Nora’s shoulder adaptation and earlier care fatigue supply sensitivity to changing reach, waiting and ordinary dependence. In IX and XI, Neale and Wills’ checking actions acquire different meanings through their own modeled learning. Future voice review must inspect those processes and actual lines separately."}
nodes.title: Bodily limits alter rhythm without settling meaning

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Nora’s tendency to make family time absorb her jobs makes Chapter VII’s interrupted account especially salient. This remains an open authorial inquiry, not new world canon."}

The older current-balance note still stands; its question about the later failure remains open."}

Are the important characters' voices and actions credible and recognizable through their own underlying processes, including meaningful changes by situation? Assess the author separately and give an individual finding for each relevant principal character. If author modeling was omitted, record that limit rather than inventing an author profile. For characters who act without speaking, examine behavior and viewpoint where available rather than inventing dialogue.\nEach finding must distinguish intended voice from observed effects, cite exact draft passages and identify the relevant author-model dispositions or character-process evidence through graph node IDs or model paths. Explain recognizability, useful distinction or similarity, and variation by situation; record weaknesses or uncertainty honestly. Give the smallest useful repair, or explain why to keep what works. Examine attention, narrative distance, rhythm, imagery, dialogue, action and omission where useful; do not replace reading with a checklist, enforced imitation or a quota for every trait. Distinguish purposeful narrator contrast or shared character language from an unintended flattening of voices. A voice is assessed against the chosen model and text, not claimed to be a real person's objectively true voice. A reader's interpretation of a narrator or character is not evidence of the real author's private beliefs or biography.\nStore the assessment inside the graph using life_story_author_record with kind assessment, producing an actual externalized_reflection Understanding Node, not metadata or an exported review alone. In data preserve the reviewed graphHash, sourceSnapshotHash and modelHash, the selected author model ID and record hash when supplied, and per-subject findings with their prose citations and model evidence node IDs or paths. Use the exact identities and hashes available in the review task or graph; retrieve missing evidence rather than fabricate it, and identify unavailable evidence as a limit.
