Explain adequate boundaries, missing evidence or deliberate exclusions; do not invent scores, change or detail just to fill a checklist.

Explore the model recursively throughout the work: opening a process, relationship or meaning can reveal new questions and distinctions, and following them can change the account that first prompted the exploration. Curiosity, surprise, play and discoveries in provisional prose are valid reasons to open the model even when no gap is known. Return to connected regions as understanding changes; the supplied checks do not bound what can be investigated.
Automatically review model depth before preparing scenes for commitment and after consequential changes to lives, mechanisms, institutions, causal transitions, outcomes, or disclosure plans. Exploratory candidates, drafts and questions can be saved before this review and while it has unresolved findings; use what they reveal to guide further modeling. Use life_story_model_depth_review with the current story graph, overall-life dossier, a stored outline/plan as focusNodeId, and the relevant contextNodeIds. Read the actual model bound to this graph; model depth cannot be judged from a synopsis or node count alone.
Supply modelEvidenceRefs for the actual lives, circumstances, constraints and choices the focus depends on, also when a life dossier is present. The packet includes these records and model records anchored by the selected graph nodes. It follows only those explicit references, not every possible explanatory connection: inspect the records, follow relevant dependencies through life_meaning_query or life_model_inspect, and add missing context before concluding. Read every relevant omitted record through the supplied routes; a model summary, dossier, or lens interpretation cannot substitute for its underlying evidence.
For an existing work whose lives and causes already live in native model records, explicitly set lifeTrendsNodeId:null and supply modelEvidenceRefs rather than inventing a dossier or duplicating the model into fixed phases. Inspect the returned records and open further evidence through life_meaning_query or life_model_inspect as needed. Judge whether those records explain the chosen focus, and report unknown history or inadequate coverage honestly; references are not proof of a complete life model. This mode supports existing-work review and explicit revision. It does not satisfy the separate life-dossier gate for committing a new scene.
Ask: Is this model developed enough to explain the consequential choices and outcomes in the planned story? Identify the important explanatory dependencies, then inspect them where relevant: whole-life trends and flaws that affect choices; concepts and what their distinctions mean; physical quantities, capacities and bottlenecks; institutions, incentives and constraints; causal Events, alternatives, anticipation and adaptation; author processes for intentional withholding and later resolution. Choose subjects from this story. These are prompts for attention, not a mandatory taxonomy, fixed list of life processes, decomposition quota, or demand for a shock in every scene.
Include the processes underlying consequential character speech and behavior. Inspect actual model and graph evidence for how relevant experience, learned habits, motives, attention, understanding and expectations produce a choice of words, silence or action in the present relationship and situation. Where emotions, status, anticipation, surprise or adaptation change that response, inspect the causal connection and its limits. A voice adjective, catchphrase or assertion that two characters differ does not explain their conduct. Numerical tendencies need defined meanings and links to the modeled response; a score alone cannot establish it. Do not require a universal voice taxonomy or forced differences: shared language, restraint and situation-dependent variation can be well explained. Keep authorial selection, narrator presentation and the character's own processes distinct, with each speaker's knowledge bounded by the story. When reviewing an existing draft, use its passages to identify the consequential speech and actions requiring explanation; literary recognizability and effectiveness still require a separate actual-prose review and are advisory.
For each reviewed subject, give a concise sufficient, needs_opening, or unclear finding with evidence from actual model records and selected graph nodes. Where the work claims a consequential causal connection, inspect how the relevant circumstances and history bear on what the person knows, wants or can do and on the action and its consequences. Explore plausible alternatives when they reveal a useful distinction; this is one avenue of inquiry, not a required scene pattern or a simulated counterfactual. Identify an unsupported claimed connection as a gap rather than repeating the intended plot. Separate the character's condition and understanding from an author's or reader's interpretation. Explain why the existing abstraction is enough for this focus, or specify a useful refinement/evidence needed. A sufficient finding is a local judgment and leaves the model open to fresh questions. A name, generic process label, numerical score or plot assertion alone is not an explanation. Numerical categories must have meaningful comparisons and units. Preserve intentionally unknown causes, competing accounts, quiet scenes, ambiguity and distinctive choices; do not manufacture certainty to pass a review. Judge whether the scene respects what is established and what remains open, not whether all mysteries have been resolved. Do not demand extra detail or a flaw on every page. Separate a necessary explanatory repair from an optional artistic preference; this is not a literary grade.
Record coverage and findings with life_story_model_depth_record using the exact taskHash. Cite model evidence as {kind: "model", ref: "process:<id>"} (or event:, cut:, concept:, abstract_cut:, event_relation:, referent:, binding:, realization:, law:, claim:), optionally with a JSON Pointer path inside that record, or as a full JSON Pointer path; the server resolves refs against the bound model. Findings become an Understanding Node with links to their graph and model evidence. Save gaps honestly rather than marking them sufficient to pass. Repair only the relevant model parts through existing tools, preserve unaffected character/history, then repeat the depth review on the changed basis and re-review affected prose. A new or consequentially changed story plan must be stored and reviewed; do not continue from an external plan. Reuse a sufficient review only while its focus, source, dossier and relevant context remain unchanged and cover the intended scene. Incidental draft or note additions do not require repeating it.
When rebinding a narrative graph to a successor model, use life_narrative_revise to retain earlier depth-assessment nodes as historical records but remove their predecessor-model anchor edges from that successor only. Native model anchors must resolve against the graph's current source. Never retarget an old finding's path to new model values. The immutable predecessor graph and each assessment's reviewedGraphHash/modelHash preserve its exact evidence. Then record a fresh assessment with new anchors; historical assessments cannot authorize scenes against the changed source. Review other affected anchors explicitly under the existing graph revision contract.
The calling LLM supplies the judgment. The server verifies references, recorded coverage, source identity and freshness, not explanatory truth, completeness, hidden reasoning, or literary merit. Use an independent reviewer when available; otherwise identify self-review. Model-definition reads are administrative and not scope-filtered. They describe static structure and initial values, not current values in a frozen world/candidate snapshot; inspect appropriate bound evidence for runtime claims and mark unavailable evidence unclear.

Develop or reuse a model of the author's voice during exploration and before preparing new scenes for commitment, within the agreed brief and human involvement, derived from the author's life in its own life model (life_story_world_record, stage author_reader). Exploratory drafts can reveal new aspects of that voice and life; follow those questions back into the model without requiring a settled account before trying a passage. Store it with life_story_author_record, kind author_model, using data with schema meaning-model-story-author-model/v1. Its modeledAuthorId is the person/persona being modeled; the tool's authorId identifies the recorder. Keep the model author-only and separate from story-world character life trends. For an existing project, reuse its chosen model; an explicit request to omit author modeling or a bounded review/edit remains valid. Do not silently invent a model of the real user in an autonomous story run: create a clearly fictional author persona when authorial choices have been delegated and no real author model was supplied, recording that choice.
Model causes of style: supplied preferences or relevant experience, observations from actual writing samples, tentative interpretations, or invented persona history lead to outlook and habitual attention, which lead to concrete writing choices. In real_author mode use supplied material and distinguish interpretation from what the author actually said; a narrator's statements are not evidence of the author's biography or beliefs. Do not fabricate private experiences. Fictional author material must be labeled invented. The life itself belongs in the author's life model; this record holds the voice that life produces. Numerical dimensions can describe chosen comparisons and tendencies with explicit meanings, units, bounds and values; they are authored models, not universal personality scores. Existing numerical life exploration can inform a fictional author's development when useful; keep its samples and conclusions in the graph.
For new writing, explicitly locate the author at the time of composition: their life stage and current circumstances, relevant earlier life and writing history (including influences, experiments and habits changed or retained), and their reasons for writing this particular work now. Store supported or invented context as labeled basis entries and link its relevant effects through dispositions; no new record type is needed. Only experience available at that composition point may shape this version of the author. Use known real-author information; leave unavailable life history or motives explicitly unknown in the record summary, without inventing evidence or demanding private biography. For a delegated fictional persona, choose and record these elements as invented. Reasons can be multiple, conflicting, uncertain or evolving: curiosity, pleasure, craft, a commission, earning a living, remembrance or questioning a conviction are all possible. An exploratory work need not have a settled thesis. Keep reasons for undertaking the work separate from a chapter's purpose, narrator or character motives, and the effect actually achieved for a reader. The connections may shape subject, form, voice, emphasis or omission without requiring autobiographical exposition or a message in every scene. Revisit them when useful during review; preserve the earlier record and explicitly revise changed motives rather than retrofitting an intention to declare the draft successful.
The data object requires schema, modeledAuthorId, mode (real_author or fictional_author), label, basis and dispositions; dimensions is optional. Each basis entry has id, kind (author_statement, writing_sample, interpretation or invented), description, and optional sourceNodeId/excerpt. Writing samples require a stored source node and exact excerpt. Each disposition has id, names basisIds and explains outlookOrHabit, writingConsequences (an array), usefulContexts, risksOrCounterweights and optional dimensionIds. Optional dimensions have id, meaning, comparisonQuestion, unit, minimum, maximum and value. For example, work negotiating between institutions may prompt attention to who can interrupt or name a problem, expressed through asymmetrical dialogue; its counterweight is allowing uncalculated affection and encounters outside institutions. Keep the experience, interpretation and proposed literary effect distinct rather than assigning stock adjectives or equating a background with one inevitable style.
Carry the exact stored authorModelNodeId into scene preparation. In scene.authorApplication select relevant dispositionIds and describe intendedEffect, restraint and narratorRelation. Vary attention, distance, syntax, rhythm, image sources, treatment of dialogue, explanation and omission where the model gives a reason; these are examples, not required dimensions or sentence quotas. A contrasting narrator, an unusual register or deliberately leaving a disposition inactive can be appropriate. Do not force every disposition into every scene or make all characters sound like the author. The author, recorder, narrator and focal character are separate identities; author knowledge or beliefs do not grant character knowledge, narrator authority or fictional truth. No private author background should appear in prose merely because it shaped a choice.
Ground character speech and behavior in the characters' own modeled processes, not in the author model alone. Where consequential, connect what a character notices, wants, expects, understands and has learned to how they speak, withhold, act and respond to others. Consider relationship and status, emotional state, anticipation, surprise and adaptation as relevant causes rather than a required list of traits. The same person can speak differently in safety, negotiation or grief while retaining a recognizable history. Give these connections evidence in the existing model and graph; an adjective-only voice label, accent or catchphrase is not a substitute. Do not invent universal voice axes, force contrast between every pair of characters, or give a speaker knowledge unavailable to them. Shared language and deliberate resemblance can be meaningful.
Automatically review the actual prose after a draft and after a substantive revision. Ask explicitly: Does this work express the modeled author's voice at this point in their life, and where does the text support or undermine that reading? Are the important characters' voices and actions credible and recognizable through their own underlying processes, including meaningful changes by situation? Assess the author separately and give an individual finding for each relevant principal character. If author modeling was omitted, record that limit rather than inventing an author profile. For characters who act without speaking, examine behavior and viewpoint where available rather than inventing dialogue.
Each finding must distinguish intended voice from observed effects, cite exact draft passages and identify the relevant author-model dispositions or character-process evidence through graph node IDs or model paths. Explain recognizability, useful distinction or similarity, and variation by situation; record weaknesses or uncertainty honestly. Give the smallest useful repair, or explain why to keep what works. Examine attention, narrative distance, rhythm, imagery, dialogue, action and omission where useful; do not replace reading with a checklist, enforced imitation or a quota for every trait. Distinguish purposeful narrator contrast or shared character language from an unintended flattening of voices. A voice is assessed against the chosen model and text, not claimed to be a real person's objectively true voice. A reader's interpretation of a narrator or character is not evidence of the real author's private beliefs or biography.
Store the assessment inside the graph using life_story_author_record with kind assessment, producing an actual externalized_reflection Understanding Node, not metadata or an exported review alone. Link about the exact reviewed draft/passage nodes and shaped_by the selected author model when present; link relevant graph process evidence as appropriate. In data preserve the reviewed graphHash, sourceSnapshotHash and modelHash, the selected author model ID and record hash when supplied, and per-subject findings with their prose citations and model evidence node IDs or paths. Use the exact identities and hashes available in the review task or graph; retrieve missing evidence rather than fabricate it, and identify unavailable evidence as a limit. These findings externalize the evidence and conclusions needed for revision, not hidden reasoning. Save them before treating voice review as complete. Use the optional authorModelNodeId in life_story_purpose_review so its advice uses the exact graph model rather than a caller summary. Literary effectiveness remains advisory, not a style score or hard gate.
When a voice is weak, distinguish a prose realization problem from an inadequately explained character process or author interpretation. A later deepening pass can strengthen an existing causal connection or its expression while preserving successful scenes and variation; more detail, difference or intensity is not automatically better. Reassess changed passages after revision and preserve earlier findings as historical evidence rather than rewriting them to match the new draft.
Record changed author models as new author_model records linked supersedes, then prepare and review affected prose against the chosen revision. Style-only changes need not invalidate an otherwise unchanged causal depth review; changes to story causes or disclosure do. The server validates structure, sources and provenance, not whether the model captures a person or produces distinctive writing.","responseGuidance":"Briefly identify the purpose(s) and whether each is author-stated or inferred; give a qualitative judgment (fulfilled, partly_fulfilled, not_fulfilled, or unclear) with textual evidence. Consider character and reader anticipation, change, and adaptation where relevant. Include individual evidenced author/character voice findings under the voice-review instructions and save them as Understanding Nodes. Add at most one revision suggestion, only if useful, as the overall editorial recommendation; voice findings may identify subject-specific repairs or reasons to keep the prose. New aspects answer the changed questions: threads that echo by realizing one concept, what the opening promises, the spacing of turns, time and room narrowing on the Friday, voices under strain, a changed understanding in a costly choice, silences explained, and the cuts between scenes, left open.","data":{"schema":"meaning-model-story-world/v1","stage":"aspects","openingNodeId":"world.book.opening.compression.r26.20260929","aspects":[{"id":"flaws.halden-recognition","kind":"flaws","aspect":"Halden's flaw: after the trial his judgment of capacity bends toward being recognized as an inventor of organization; he accepts four deposits against a ledger showing two (E18) and writes the Friday exception himself (E24).","how":"Modeled as a process over his life (the recognition process): invisible usefulness (1817-1843), the invention it made possible, visibility after the trial, the salutation and the fourth article, the Friday, and the account that replaces recognition; who sees it (Lovelace, Margaret) and the habit he does not see in himself. Chapters I, III, IX, X and XI read against it; the Friday's cost now includes Neale's Monday promised without him.","status":"modeled","records":["process:profile.edward-halden.person.edward_halden.is.recognition","event:event.book.flaw.halden.manager","event:event.book.flaw.halden.friday","event:event.book.flaw.halden.account","event:event.book.wants.halden"]},{"id":"flaws.babbage-sole-judge","kind":"flaws","aspect":"Babbage's flaw: preserving the architecture is entangled with preserving himself as its sole adequate judge; after the trial he reads visible use as vindication of the whole Engine, and after the return he first places the error outside the Engine.","how":"Modeled as the control process: what taught it (Clement, the Treasury), where it takes over (whenever a signature binds him), strength and harm, its cost, and its slow change into complete custody; Chapter XI now shows the defence reaching for the printer his engines were built to have.","status":"modeled","records":["process:profile.charles-babbage.person.charles_babbage.is.control","event:event.book.flaw.babbage.taught","event:event.book.flaw.babbage.defence","event:event.book.flaw.babbage.custody","event:event.book.wants.babbage"]},{"id":"flaws.lovelace-sole-signature","kind":"flaws","aspect":"Lovelace protects her sole signature over the claim by striking the deputy line (E06) and only at Ockham recognizes that she, like Neale, has been made a sole carrier (E20).","how":"Modeled as the sole-authority process: taught by being received as somebody's relation, the struck deputy line, the claim kept on her lap, the recognition at Ockham and the signature nobody holds at her death. Prose already renders it; kept.","status":"modeled","records":["process:profile.ada-lovelace.person.ada_lovelace.is.sole-authority","event:event.book.flaw.lovelace.deputy","event:event.book.flaw.lovelace.recognition","event:event.book.wants.lovelace"]},{"id":"wants.principals","kind":"wants","aspect":"What each principal wants and how it moves: Babbage autonomy and competence, Lovelace understanding, Halden competence and then belonging; Halden's belonging rises from 0.08 (September 1843) to 0.23 (February 1852) and falls to 0.10 after the return.","how":"Deepest wants, the learned wants that serve them, their proxies and conflicts are now described per principal (event.book.wants.*); the WHAT Cuts stay as they were.","status":"modeled","records":["cut:cut.book.07r2.what.halden-september-1843-estimate","cut:cut.book.07r2.what.halden-february-1852-expansion","cut:cut.book.07r2.what.halden-may-1854-returned-table","event:event.book.wants.halden","event:event.book.wants.babbage","event:event.book.wants.lovelace"]},{"id":"fear-love.decisions","kind":"fear-love","aspect":"Whether each consequential act comes from fear or from love: Babbage's refusal to sign into permanence (from Clement), Lovelace's struck deputy line, Halden's Friday order (the returnable deposit, the wages, his household's savings in the office), Neale putting his name under Wills's work, Charles's complete custody.","how":"Read qualitatively for five acts (lens.book.fear-love.decisions): which are fear, which care, which both, and what else stands beside them. Babbage's distinction stays true; it is not the whole truth.","how":"Written down as one of the five ideas with its strategy (met, tested, lands) in the author record and a plan note; grounded in the concept it rests on and the Events that realize it; followed through the chapters as a telling process; whether it reaches a reader is tested by the controlled read-back.","status":"modeled","records":["concept:valid_computational_claim","concept:common_source_dependence","idea.book.exact-machine-wrong-table.20260929","story.process.book.idea.exact-machine-wrong-table.20260929"]},{"id":"theme.hands-not-deposits","kind":"theme","aspect":"Hands, not deposits: Capacity is particular people's hours. Nora's life, voice, reasons, figuring-out and buttons are unchanged.","data":{"schema":"meaning-model-story-world/v1","stage":"author_reader","author":{"personId":"referent.profile.nora.person.nora","name":"Nora Vale","mode":"invented","lifeModelHash":"9d7be364f47f4369388aaffc8725e6913eb508b8bbb420925c8683844e0c8f84","authorModelNodeId":"author-model.nora-vale.20260927","livesIn":"separate_world","writing":"Chosen on 27 September 2026 to develop future revisions of an already existing historical counterfactual; she has no in-world access to its nineteenth-century people. Her fabricated displays, family rota and later physical limits give her reasons to see hidden labor and to distrust her pleasure in a clean account. Its joy in making also challenges her tendency to explain away unproductive pleasure.","teach":"Five ideas, each with its strategy: where the reader meets it, where the story tests it, where it lands. Nora holds them as questions she wants a reader to feel, not a thesis. (1) The machine was exact; the table was wrong: a result is right only when the whole route to it is answerable. Met in I (the exact trace; 'We gave it'). Tested in IV (the second column), VIII ('a trial of us'), IX ('It has freed the operation'), X (two checking paths inherit one value). Lands in XI ('A printer would have printed it') and XII ('But they bought the table'; a heading that takes both). (2) Hands, not deposits: capacity is particular people's hours, a promise sold beyond them is paid by the one who checks, and one indispensable person cannot be multiplied by money. Met in I ('four dates with hands for two'). Tested in V (Lovelace strikes her own deputy line), IX (eighty hours; four acceptances; teaching eats the hours it should add), X ('a single man'; nobody holds her signature). Lands in XI ('You promised my Monday, sir.' 'I did.'; the correction read by two). (3) The exception that felt like no decision: failure is an honest temporary exception carried forward by routine; accountability is naming one's own authorization in full. Met in I (the margin in his own hand). Tested in IX (by the fourth acceptance he no longer looks at the capacity sheet), X (each exception carried forward; 'had meant to tell him'). Lands in XI ('pressure of business' struck; both authorizations copied; the reference names the order). (4) Someone must be able to say no: an undertaking is trustworthy only as far as someone named can stop it, and refusal is weakest where proposer and refuser are one. Met in II ('the man who can say no'), III ('build nothing'), V ('who could stop it'). Tested in VII (stop before the next stage, at his own fee), VIII (the sixth case), IX ('The account'), X (no row complete). Lands in XI (dissolution as a completed stage; 'It does.'). (5) What was made stays made: a bounded achievement keeps its truth and pleasure when the larger promise fails, if its edge is stated. Met in III (six empty columns). Tested in VI (the handle turned once more), VIII (joy close to relief; three strokes), X (their old speed). Lands in XII ('Of that object. Not of the Engine'; the tape around all three). Left open, not taught: whether a complete record can leave a person unexhausted, when accuracy is care and when self-defence, and what matters outside the account (Margaret's novel, William's water); nor does the book prove that refusing a promise is always right.","figuringOut":"Can a record remain complete about a bounded undertaking while leaving a person unexhausted by it? {"schema":"meaning-model-story-author-record/v1","kind":"world","text":"The opening again after the ideas pass: the same accepted history in the compression's successive accounts, the sentence and paragraph first and then the page (compression.book.r26.20260929). It keeps the claims of world.book.opening.retrospective.20260929 and its era; no history changes. Sentence: In an 1850s where a working fragment of Babbage's Analytical Engine is built under Ada Lovelace's conditions, the estimator who made it answerable sells four tables with hands for two and waives one check himself to keep a date, so that when the wrong table comes back every sentence of the machine's defence is true and the failure is still his.","data":{"schema":"meaning-model-story-world/v1","stage":"opening","candidatesNodeId":null,"accounts":["In an 1850s where a working fragment of Babbage's Analytical Engine is built under Ada Lovelace's conditions, the estimator who made it answerable sells four tables with hands for two and waives one check himself to keep a date, so that when the wrong table comes back every sentence of the machine's defence is true and the failure is still his. Babbage will not let his Engine be governed; Lovelace will not let it be believed without conditions; Edward Halden, an estimator paid twenty-five pounds to say whether it can be priced at all, finds an edge: six registers, thirty card steps, no printer, no claim to be the Engine, and a register for everything left out. Guardian Assurance buys only a comparison it can check by hand. Through a panic, a binding drive and seven years the fragment is built, and in 1851 it reproduces twelve sealed cases twice; the signed sentence says no more than that. Its success buys a calculation office. In 1852 Halden accepts four deposits against checking hours for two, over Lovelace's written qualification; she dies that November with her own deputy line struck through and Thomas Neale still the office's only independent checker. On a Friday in April 1854, with the wages due, Halden lets Guardian's table go out on one signature, and a clerk's transposed figure goes with it. The machine was exact; the ledger says who let the table leave. Halden closes the office rather than raise money on a defence in which every sentence is true, and in 1871 Babbage's son files the wrong table, the corrected one and Lovelace's qualification together: complete of that object, not of the Engine.","I. May 1854. Guardian Assurance returns a table computed by the office's apparatus, cut open along its far edge as evidence. The configuration's seal is unbroken and the run trace exact, and Babbage is relieved. Halden finds the error before the first card: the clerk Samuel Wills transposed 3,742 as 3,472 and read his copy back to himself, and in the delivery ledger's margin, in Halden's own hand, the second comparison was deferred to keep the date. 'Of course it is a human failure.' There was no second signature.

II and III. 1843. After the Treasury's refusal Lovelace proposes a constitution for the Engine; Babbage refuses to be governed but grants thirty days to find the man who can say no. Halden, from instrument and railway supply, is paid twenty-five pounds for four lists whose last line may be 'build nothing'. Pricing the answer instead of the drawing, he finds a bounded apparatus: six registers, thirty steps, no branch, no printer, no claim to be the Engine, and a successor register for every excluded improvement.

IV and V. Davies at Guardian will buy only a comparison he can check by hand; Whitworth's review turns the date into fiction; Lovelace divides the work into what the apparatus must do and what the undertaking must do, the second being the reason anyone may believe the first. The compact is founded by deciding who can stop it: architecture Babbage's, claims Lovelace's, price and schedule Halden's, money released in four stages. Lovelace strikes the deputy line beneath her own name. Halden puts in nearly half his savings.

VI and VII. Two assemblies that each pass their gauges bind when joined; Halden refuses Babbage's better redesign as a change and has the drive re-machined; the handle turns, and Babbage calls the successor register hers. In the 1847 panic the calls fail; on Lovelace's letter, and against every private pressure, Halden pays what was earned and stops before the next stage, losing his fee. At home Margaret asks whether the wages are in the bank on Friday, and then reads him a novel.

VIII. 1851. The sealed test: twelve cases, two complete runs, a stop when a register fails to clear, agreement. The signed sentence claims nothing more. Babbage's joy is close to relief; the empty reader lifts three times while nobody watches.

IX and X. 1852. Four offices want tables; the checking hours allow two. Babbage argues that machines free us from the pace of repetition, Lovelace that they do not free us from deciding what we asked, Neale that his eighty hours cannot be spent twice. Halden, called inventor in one letter, accepts all four. Lovelace qualifies the decision in writing: no fifth, pay for Wills's training, name Neale's deputy. The training is deferred; she sees that she, like Neale, is a sole carrier, and dies in November with no one holding her signature. Through 1853 exceptions are carried forward. On Friday 7 April 1854 Halden writes the margin himself; the Monday fills with another office's query.

XI. Davies accepts the trace and rejects the table; cancellation follows. 'You promised my Monday, sir.' 'I did.' The table is recomputed with Wills reading and Neale following. Babbage wants the reply to lead with the machine's exactness and new money raised on it; every sentence could be defended. Halden writes the closure instead, strikes 'pressure of business', copies both authorizations, and at Wills's asking adds to his reference that he authorized delivery before the comparison. The office closes in March 1855.

XII. 1871. Henry Babbage inventories his father's papers and finds the returned table filed with the successes. Charles adds a heading: the bounded apparatus and office, complete, of that object and not of the Engine. In 1900 Henry ties the faded tape around the wrong table, the corrected one, and Lovelace's qualification between them."],"closedQuestions":["Who: Babbage, Lovelace and the invented estimator Edward Halden are the principals; Davies, Farrow, Neale, Wills, Margaret Halden, William King-Noel and Henry Prevost Babbage are the secondary lives.","What is built: one six-register card-directed apparatus answering twelve actuarial recurrence cases, never the general Analytical Engine.","Construction money reconciles at £3,000 staged: Babbage £1,500, Guardian £400, Halden £100, outside subscribers £1,000 held by the trust.","Office money reconciles at £900 of capital (Babbage £650, the Halden household £150, the £100 construction reserve) and four deposits of £180.","Capacity reconciles: eighty protected checker-hours a quarter at forty per final packet; four final packets need a hundred and sixty.","When: divergence after 14 August 1843; the trial in May 1851; Lovelace dies on 27 November 1852; the Friday is 7 April 1854; the return on 3 May 1854; closure on 31 March 1855; custody in October 1871; the packet opened in 1900.","Where: Babbage's Dorset Street rooms, Ockham, Farrow's Lambeth works, Guardian's consultation room, the calculation office in London, Great Cumberland Place in Marylebone.","The failure is human and institutional: the apparatus propagates the supplied value correctly; the error is a transposition (3,742 entered as 3,472) delivered after a single check Halden authorized.","Nothing beyond the packet's survival in 1900 is asserted: no adoption, no office lineage, no completed Engine."],"revisions":[],"era":{"kind":"alternate","documentaryCutoff":"14 August 1843","knowledgeLimit":"My training ends in mid-2026; the era (1843 to 1900) is long documented. Facts added on this branch were checked against sources and recorded as reports: Guardian's Lombard Street address, Clement keeping the tools in 1833, Babbage's wrong-figures questions in his Passages (1864), the Great Exhibition's dates, the declaration of war in March 1854.","livingPeople":"No living people. The real people are historical (Babbage, Lovelace, Davies, Whitworth, Clement, Somerville, William King-Noel, Henry Prevost Babbage) and act counterfactually only after the cutoff; Guardian Assurance is a historical organization in a bounded customer role. It records what earlier openings settled; no history changes.","data":{"schema":"meaning-model-story-world/v1","stage":"opening","candidatesNodeId":null,"accounts":["In August 1843, when Lovelace offers to conduct the business of the Analytical Engine on conditions, Babbage does not refuse: he gives the negotiation thirty days. Within them an estimator, Edward Halden, is paid £25 to find one finite obligation, and he finds it by reversing the question: not which part of the Engine can be built, but which exact claim a physical object can answer. A six-register card-directed apparatus is composed, reviewed by Whitworth's works and bought by Griffith Davies for Guardian Assurance as a comparison against twelve actuarial cases; a compact divides authority, and Lovelace strikes out the deputy for her own claim signature. Farrow's works builds it through a binding failure and the credit pressure of 1847, and in May 1851 it passes a sealed trial twice. Success brings inquiries, a calculation office with £900 of capital, and four deposits accepted against a ledger that shows independent checking for two. Lovelace files a qualification, asks that Neale's deputy be named, and dies in November 1852 with nobody named. On Friday 7 April 1854, with Neale on another packet, Halden releases Guardian's cards after one check; the table comes back in May with a transposed figure; the office discloses, corrects, refunds and closes in March 1855. Babbage keeps the whole record, the error beside the proof, and in 1871 passes it complete to his son Henry, who opens it again in 1900.","In August 1843 the government has withdrawn, Clement has kept the tools for ten years, and Lovelace's letter asks Babbage to let her conduct the Engine's business on conditions. He gives the negotiation thirty days. Farrow forwards the packet to Halden, a Lambeth estimator who has made other men's designs deliverable all his working life; Babbage pays him £25 from his own purse, four days inside the term, for four weeks that may end in a refusal. Every attempt to price a severed part of the Engine fails because every part depends on machinery elsewhere, so Halden asks which claim an object can answer, and the three compose a six-register apparatus that answers twelve of Guardian's recurrence cases while the general architecture is deferred, not destroyed. Davies buys rejectable calculations, not an opinion of the Engine; Whitworth's works finds the interfaces gaugeable and several tolerances unsupported. In April 1844 the compact gives architecture, evidence, contracts, manufacture, acceptance and cash to separate hands, and Lovelace makes her signature the sole authority over what may be claimed, striking the deputy line herself.

£3,000 is staged by configuration, component, assembly and test. Farrow's assemblies meet their drawings and bind under the shared drive in July 1846; the works re-machines the interface, and in 1847 a wider contraction delays the next call while earned wages are paid. The configuration is frozen with its inputs, exclusions and stopping rule before the result is known, and in May 1851, in the Exhibition's first month, the apparatus agrees with the sealed independent answers on two complete runs. The joy of it moves Babbage toward the whole architecture and Halden toward a profession of organization. In 1852 the calculation office opens with £900, Babbage's £650 and £150 of the Halden household's savings among it, and Halden accepts four deposits over Lovelace's objection although the ledger shows eighty protected checking hours a quarter, forty to a packet, all of them the ten hours a week Neale's employer spares. Lovelace's qualification asks for no fifth, for Wills's instruction in paid hours, and for Neale's deputy to be named; she dies on 27 November 1852 and nobody holds her signature. On Friday 7 April 1854 both small packets fall due, and Halden writes the exception himself: Guardian's deck, transposed by Wills at the first value for age forty-seven, goes out after one check. Davies returns it on 3 May; Halden records his own authorization, the office refunds £180, corrects in four days of paired checking and closes on 31 March 1855. Babbage keeps the returned table beside the proof, and in October 1871 the complete packet passes to Henry, who opens it in 1900 to decide what passes after him.","August 1843 to April 1844. The negotiation continues because Babbage chooses a bounded interval over refusal; Lovelace expected refusal. Halden's four weeks turn an unpriceable Engine into one answerable claim: he supplies the priced boundary, Lovelace an operation that can be tested, Babbage the finite register arrangement, until three descriptions refer to one object. Davies, who has read Lovelace's Notes, keeps his curiosity apart from the payment condition. Whitworth's report and Guardian's memorandum reach Lovelace at Ockham. The compact records every present change and sends improvements to one successor register, Halden's thin book; Lovelace's struck deputy line protects her authority and leaves its succession open.

May 1844 to December 1851. Capital is released by stage; manufacture begins under the frozen register while Babbage keeps designing successors outside it. The binding under the shared drive is a material shock without a culprit; Farrow backs his foreman's refusal to invent a defective part though payment waits, and when the joined assemblies turn freely the foreman, the estimator and the inventor recognize the same recovery through heat, load and motion. Through the credit pressure Margaret asks Edward to let her finish her own line before he spreads the venture ledger across it. The trial restarts once when a register fails to clear, then passes twice; Babbage briefly stops explaining; three unnecessary empty strokes are allowed. The publication claims only what the frozen apparatus did, and four inquiries follow.

1852 to 1900. The office's articles copy the compact's stopping clauses, promise two signatures beneath every table and give acceptance of customer work to the manager; Lovelace asks who may refuse the manager, and Halden answers 'The account'. Customers close their accounts at the end of 1853 and release final returns from 1 April, so the four final checks meet in one quarter against capacity for two. A March lesson for Wills is displaced by preparation; at Ockham in August 1852 Lovelace finds that Babbage's two checking paths inherit one value and asks for a funded successor; Halden postpones it. After her death the Friday arrives with the wage envelopes on Halden's desk, Guardian's returnable deposit among what paid them, and the third direction on the shelf unanswered. The return makes the failure public to the offices involved; Babbage first says the Engine did not err, and Halden asks what Guardian purchased. Wills asks that Halden's order stand beside his own error in his reference. The office closes with its obligations met. Babbage's interpretation changes slowly until the human system is part of what the record means, and his last inventory has two headings: the bounded undertaking's complete record, and the unfinished Engine."],"closedQuestions":["Who: Babbage, Lovelace and the invented estimator Edward Halden are the principals; Davies, Farrow, Neale, Wills, Margaret Halden, William King-Noel and Henry Prevost Babbage are the secondary lives.","What is built: one six-register card-directed apparatus answering twelve actuarial recurrence cases, never the general Analytical Engine.","Construction money reconciles at £3,000 staged: Babbage £1,500, Guardian £400, Halden £100, outside subscribers £1,000 held by the trust.","Office money reconciles at £900 of capital (Babbage £650, the Halden household £150, the £100 construction reserve) and four deposits of £180.","Capacity reconciles: eighty protected checker-hours a quarter at forty per final packet; four final packets need a hundred and sixty.","When: divergence after 14 August 1843; the trial in May 1851; Lovelace dies on 27 November 1852; the Friday is 7 April 1854; the return on 3 May 1854; closure on 31 March 1855; custody in October 1871; the packet opened in 1900.","Where: Babbage's Dorset Street rooms, Ockham, Farrow's Lambeth works, Guardian's consultation room, the calculation office in London, Great Cumberland Place in Marylebone.","The failure is human and institutional: the apparatus propagates the supplied value correctly; the error is a transposition (3,742 entered as 3,472) delivered after a single check Halden authorized.","Nothing beyond the packet's survival in 1900 is asserted: no adoption, no office lineage, no completed Engine."],"revisions":[{"claim":"The thirty-day term is set in 1843 and never closed.","revisedTo":"The commission closes the term with its missing man found: Halden reads the packet on the twenty-fifth day and is paid four days inside it.","reason":"Blind read 1 on the branch (E02, model revision 14)."},{"claim":"The office appears in 1852 without its founding.","revisedTo":"E16a constitutes it in January 1852 with £900, two promised signatures beneath each table and the fourth article.","reason":"Blind read 1 on the branch (model revision 14)."},{"claim":"The Friday's pressure is summarized.","revisedTo":"E24 opens the Friday in scene: both small packets due, the wage envelopes, the qualification's third direction unanswered, Halden's own exception.","reason":"Blind read 1 on the branch (model revision 14)."}],"era":{"kind":"alternate","documentaryCutoff":"14 August 1843","knowledgeLimit":"My training ends in mid-2026; The prose supports this distinction but gives no exact resolution day.","data":{"operations":[{"kind":"replace_text","nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.09.scene.02","expectedText":"In Halden's new office that February, Babbage held that the estimate described
the office they had, while the deposits described the office they might create.

“We are not dividing eighty hours among four fixed objects, as though hours
were loaves,” he said. “We are using four obligations to purchase more hours.
The railways built themselves on exactly that principle, and nobody asks them
to apologize.”

“From whom?” Lovelace asked.

The office was two rooms adjoining the calculating room. Through the wall came
the intermittent motion of the apparatus. On the table lay four letters and the
capacity sheet. Lovelace had marked one line twice: independent checking, not
preparation, set the boundary.

Halden laid the letters around the capacity sheet. Their corners covered the
marked line.

Halden had advertised for another checker. Two men answered; neither could yet
challenge a prepared set of cards without Neale's supervision, and training
consumed the same scarce hours it was meant to increase.

“The deposits keep Wills paid while Neale trains him,” Halden said.

“The customers require checked tables before Wills can sign one,” Lovelace
said.

“Then we stage the work.”

“I know.” She reached for the capacity sheet. “I mean the final comparison.
When would Neale do it?”

Halden did not answer the question. One letter had called him inventor. He had
corrected the word in his reply, but not before reading the salutation twice.
Now he looked at the four deposits covering the line.

Babbage stood at the apparatus-room door. “The objection assumes that the
present method of checking is fixed for ever, like the tides. A machine exists
precisely to free us from the pace of human repetition. I have argued that for
twenty years, and I did not expect to argue it in this room.”

“It has freed the operation,” Lovelace said. “It has not freed us from deciding
what operation we asked for. If it had, I should go home and leave you both to
it.”

“A second apparatus—”

Halden interrupted him. “Isn't in any contract or any account.”

Halden looked again at the four deposits.

“Four deposits are not four deliveries,” he said. “They pay Wills, retain
Neale, and carry the rent while we stagger preparation. We begin training now
and accept no fifth.”

“Mr Halden has priced every hour by which this office came into being,” Babbage
said. “He does not mistake a receipt for capacity.”

“And Mr Babbage knows which repeated hours the mechanism can remove,” Halden
said. “We began at opposite ends and arrived at four.”

Halden drew the letters inward until their edges made a square. One corner
remained over the line Lovelace had marked.

Lovelace asked Neale to join them. He stood awkwardly at the end of the table
while Halden described the schedule.

“Four packets at forty hours make a hundred and sixty,” she said. “Can you
check them independently by the final dates?”

“Not if all four require the hours in the account.”

“Could they require less?” Babbage said.

Neale began to answer, stopped, and put the blank strip beneath the total.
“Some will. Some will not. I have eighty hours, sir. If I spend them teaching
Wills, I cannot enter them again here as his independent check.”

No one altered the figure.

Lovelace asked that her objection be entered with the capacity sheet. Babbage
would support the four. Neither could sign a customer's acceptance for Halden.

Halden held the office pen. He dated the first acceptance and laid it aside for
the second. By the fourth he no longer looked at the capacity sheet. He checked
the customer's name, the deposit, and the delivery date. All three were
correct. He initialled it and laid down the pen.","text":"In Halden's new office that February, Babbage held that the estimate described

correct. He initialled it and laid down the pen."},{"kind":"replace_text","nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.11.scene.02","expectedText":"Halden opened the office account.

There had been nine hundred pounds in contributed capital and seven hundred and
twenty in customer deposits. Wages, rent, heat, cards, maintenance, and delivery
had consumed most of it. Guardian's refund, the correction, reprinting, closure,
and storage consumed the rest. Even if another customer agreed to wait, the
office could not support the staff required to complete and independently check
the remaining work without new capital.

“Then raise new capital on the investigation,” Babbage said.

“On what statement?”

“That the calculating mechanism executed every operation supplied to it;
preparation and checking failed outside it.”

“And the office?”

“Those functions can be constituted anew under stricter conditions.”

Halden imagined the circular. A correct machine, a corrected human process,
subscriptions sought for renewed operation under improved safeguards. Every
sentence could be defended. Together they would invite a new subscriber to
finance obligations the present account could not meet.

Margaret had sorted the figures the night before into sums already owed, money
still in hand, and money a new circular only hoped to attract. When Halden
began to call the third column a rescue, she had put one finger beneath the first.

“Before you send any circular,” she had said, “show me what leaves this
house before the first new subscription comes in.”

She had found his capacity sheet among the office papers, the line marked twice.
“You showed me the articles in January, when you asked for the savings,” she
had said. “Not this.”

He had not.

New money might preserve Halden's standing and keep Wills and Neale employed.
He looked again at the sums already owed.

He wrote the closure resolution.

The remaining customer obligations would be completed only where existing
funds and independent checking sufficed; otherwise they would be cancelled
before another stage became due. Guardian would receive its refund and corrected
table. Wills and Neale would be paid through the closure month. The apparatus
would be dismantled into stored assemblies. The complete ledger would name the
February 1852 four-job authorization and the April 1854 delivery exception.
Under *cause of exception*, Halden first wrote *pressure of business*. He read
the words, struck them through, and copied both of his authorizations in full.","text":"Halden opened the office account.

twenty in customer deposits. Wages, rent, heat, cards, maintenance, and delivery
had consumed most of it. Guardian's refund, the correction, reprinting, closure,
and storage consumed the rest. Even if another customer agreed to wait, the
office could not support the staff required to complete and independently check
the remaining work without new capital.

“Then raise new capital on the investigation,” Babbage said.

“On what statement?”

“That the calculating mechanism executed every operation supplied to it;
preparation and checking failed outside it.”

upsertNodes.text:
In Halden's new office that February, Babbage held that the estimate described
the office they had, while the deposits described the office they might create.

“We are not dividing eighty hours among four fixed objects, as though hours
were loaves,” he said. “We are using four obligations to purchase more hours.
The railways built themselves on exactly that principle, and nobody asks them
to apologize.”

“From whom?” Lovelace asked.

The office was two rooms adjoining the calculating room. Through the wall came
the intermittent motion of the apparatus. On the table lay four letters and the
capacity sheet. Lovelace had marked one line twice: independent checking, not
preparation, set the boundary.

Halden laid the letters around the capacity sheet. Their corners covered the
marked line.

Halden had advertised for another checker. Two men answered; neither could yet
challenge a prepared set of cards without Neale's supervision, and training
consumed the same scarce hours it was meant to increase.

“The deposits keep Wills paid while Neale trains him,” Halden said.

“The customers require checked tables before Wills can sign one,” Lovelace
said.

“Then we stage the work.”

“I know.” She reached for the capacity sheet. “I mean the final comparison.
When would Neale do it?”

Halden did not answer the question. One letter had called him inventor. He had
corrected the word in his reply, but not before reading the salutation twice.
Now he looked at the four deposits covering the line.

Babbage stood at the apparatus-room door. “The objection assumes that the
present method of checking is fixed for ever, like the tides. A machine exists
precisely to free us from the pace of human repetition. I have argued that for
twenty years, and I did not expect to argue it in this room.”

“It has freed the operation,” Lovelace said. “It has not freed us from deciding
what operation we asked for. If it had, I should go home and leave you both to
it.”

“A second apparatus—”

Halden interrupted him. “Isn't in any contract or any account.”

Halden looked again at the four deposits.

“Four deposits are not four deliveries,” he said. “They pay Wills, retain
Neale, and carry the rent while we stagger preparation. We begin training now
and accept no fifth.”

“Mr Halden has priced every hour by which this office came into being,” Babbage
said. “He does not mistake a receipt for capacity.”

Halden looked up. He was unused to hearing his caution praised by this man.
Before he could think what to say, he had drawn the first letter nearer.

“And Mr Babbage knows which repeated hours the mechanism can remove,” Halden
said. “We began at opposite ends and arrived at four.”

Babbage came back from the doorway and drew out a chair.

Halden drew the letters inward until their edges made a square. One corner
remained over the line Lovelace had marked.

Lovelace asked Neale to join them. He stood awkwardly at the end of the table
while Halden described the schedule.

“Four packets at forty hours make a hundred and sixty,” she said. “Can you
check them independently by the final dates?”

“Not if all four require the hours in the account.”

“Could they require less?” Babbage said.

Neale began to answer, stopped, and put the blank strip beneath the total.
“Some will. Some will not. I have eighty hours, sir. If I spend them teaching
Wills, I cannot enter them again here as his independent check.”

No one altered the figure.

Lovelace asked that her objection be entered with the capacity sheet. Babbage
would support the four. Neither could sign a customer's acceptance for Halden.

Halden held the office pen. He dated the first acceptance and laid it aside for
the second. By the fourth he no longer looked at the capacity sheet. He checked
the customer's name, the deposit, and the delivery date. All three were
correct. He initialled it and laid down the pen.

Halden opened the office account.

There had been nine hundred pounds in contributed capital and seven hundred and
twenty in customer deposits. Wages, rent, heat, cards, maintenance, and delivery
had consumed most of it. Guardian's refund, the correction, reprinting, closure,
and storage consumed the rest. Even if another customer agreed to wait, the
office could not support the staff required to complete and independently check
the remaining work without new capital.

“Then raise new capital on the investigation,” Babbage said.

“On what statement?”

“That the calculating mechanism executed every operation supplied to it;
preparation and checking failed outside it.”

“And the office?”

“Those functions can be constituted anew under stricter conditions.”

Halden imagined the circular. A correct machine, a corrected human process,
subscriptions sought for renewed operation under improved safeguards. Every
sentence could be defended. Together they would invite a new subscriber to
finance obligations the present account could not meet.

The night before, Margaret had laid the figures out at the kitchen table:
sums already owed, money still in hand, and money a new circular only hoped to
attract. When Halden began to call the third column a rescue, she put one finger
beneath the first.

“Before you send any circular,” she said, “show me what leaves this house
before the first new subscription comes in.”

She found his capacity sheet among the office papers, the line marked twice.
“You showed me the articles in January, when you asked for the savings,” she
said. “Not this.”

Halden reached for the sheet. She kept her hand on it.

“I meant to get another checker.”

Margaret looked at him. “You asked me about the money.”

“Yes.”

She placed the capacity sheet beside the household book. He waited for her to
move it back to the office pile. She went on with the sums already owed.

After a while he drew his chair closer and read the payments to her, one at a
time. She entered them in the first column. Neither of them had yet touched the
money a new circular hoped to attract.

New money might preserve Halden's standing and keep Wills and Neale employed.
Back at the office, he looked again at the sums already owed.

He wrote the closure resolution.

The remaining customer obligations would be completed only where existing
funds and independent checking sufficed; otherwise they would be cancelled
before another stage became due. Guardian would receive its refund and corrected
table. Wills and Neale would be paid through the closure month. The apparatus
would be dismantled into stored assemblies. The complete ledger would name the
February 1852 four-job authorization and the April 1854 delivery exception.
Under *cause of exception*, Halden first wrote *pressure of business*. He read
the words, struck them through, and copied both of his authorizations in full.

with it. Wills laid Guardian's beside the specimen sheets. Much of the card
order could be kept. Neale put the old checking sheets aside; their ticks

its first line beneath his strip. Lothbury's and Guardian's were the two small
packets, a week of Neale's hours apiece; the two large ones would need the rest
of the quarter and more.

On Friday the seventh both dates fell due, the first the office had ever had
to keep.

his copy to Halden's desk. There was one mark in the checking column, his own.

“Mr Neale?” Halden asked.

“The Lothbury comparison, sir. He hopes to finish it by four.”

figures. He had perhaps six of his week's hours left. Halden could walk twenty
feet and put the Guardian copy on top of the Lothbury sheets, and one of the
two offices would receive its table late.

The wage envelopes lay filled in their box on the corner of the desk.
Guardian's deposit had paid for some of them; if the date passed, the deposit
became returnable. On the shelf above, beside the test packet, lay Lady
Lovelace's qualification.

marked delivered. He wrote in the margin reserved for an exception.

*Second comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date.*

{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"Decision: REVISE, retaining the episode and making the acting subjects explicit.

Scope: I previously read the complete 13,156-word completed baseline of The Book of Conditions. For this review I read the entire exact candidateText and baselineText for document.book.07r2.chapter.10.scene.04, the complete Chapter X purposeReview earlier, and the experiment metadata. The provisional reading copy is exactly equal to the stored MCP request's candidateText. I am an informed independent editor, not a blind reader. I did not re-read a newly assembled whole manuscript, inspect the bound native model, accept proposed model facts or change canon.

The episode earns a distinct development versus March1852. In March Halden sends Wills back to production before his lesson can be completed. Here Wills's learning has made him useful to a colleague: he distinguishes a reusable arrangement from old figures, shows a row, gives the colleague the ruler and asks him to do the next. The colleague continues alone. Wills has gained a practical capability without becoming an independent checker. The unfinished comparison therefore coexists with real improvement. This makes the opening claim that the work looked like growth more complex rather than merely repeating it.

The colleague's continuation is the clearest evidence of useful help. The technical account is sufficient for this limited literary focus: a reusable form, provisional figures and a subsequent row establish the task without an additional machinery explanation. I cannot independently validate the procedural details as native-model facts. Neale remains at work and later closes his book, so the draft does not imply his paid time was spent waiting idly. The unfinished specimen remains visibly separate from the provisional work. No final signed customer data is brought into1853; the unchanged1April1854 arrival remains intelligible.

Wills's short instructions are credible extensions of the earlier learner who could say that a figure was unreadable. The nod, smile and stool movement allow a small pleasure in being useful without naming a secret motive or claiming permanent confidence. Neale's 'Your copy next time' fits his practical, restrained speech and makes deferral ordinary without assigning him either indifference or prophetic knowledge. The other preparer has enough action to be a participant rather than a mute illustration.

Required local repairs:
1. In 'another preparer called Wills over to a card form he had used before', identify whose earlier use is intended. If it is Wills's, change only 'he had used before' to 'Wills had used before'. As written, the pronoun can point to the other preparer and weaken the intended evidence of Wills's familiarity.
2. The concern about 'He had been trying to describe it' is justified. After 'Wills nodded', the following 'He' strongly points to Wills; the next 'he moved his pencil' then also seems to point to Wills, although the useful advance presumably belongs to the colleague. It also asserts a prior attempt to describe the arrangement that the exchange has not made clear. The smallest robust repair is to remove that explanatory clause and name the man who advances: 'The man set out the row and held it beside the form. Wills nodded. The man moved his pencil to the following row without asking. Wills smiled and drew his stool nearer.' This proposed wording is editorial advice only, not an accepted draft or fact.

I do not recommend adding an explicit moral, a quantified loss of hours, another error, a new forewarning of the Guardian transposition or an explanation of why Wills smiles. The following April sequence carries the consequential failure. The new episode supplies a stage in Wills's development, not a claim that helping this colleague caused the later error.

The closing 'The card form could be used again' lightly restates what the colleague's continuation already shows, but it also preserves the useful method/source distinction. I do not consider its removal necessary; judge it with the clarified paragraph before making a further cut. Broad revision remains unwarranted by this reading. With the two subject clarifications, my recommendation would be to keep this candidate for the next actual-model/prose review. Its effect on an independent reader remains untested.

Guardian's and Lothbury's are the two small packets, each about a week of Neale's hours; the two large packets fall later in the quarter. That is why the two dates could be set for the first Friday, and why they could not both be kept.

Each small packet needs about twenty hours in total: ten of method checks with specimen figures before its signed return and ten of final comparison after it. Each large packet needs about sixty: twenty before its return and forty after. Current specialized depth review is locally sufficient on the accepted source; its result is not a literary verdict.","data":{"modelHash":"59ade7958b42ab41f3dbe5832ed233d6543cd0c18c75a0aa1bd79d6e56c611db","depthReviewNodeId":"depth.book.064dev.successor","operations":[{"kind":"replace_text","nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.09.scene.01","expectedText":"## IX. Four Deposits

The first inquiry arrived before the apparatus was covered. A messenger
brought a letter from an office that had heard the first day's rumour and wished
to know the price of a calculation. Halden turned the unopened letter over in
his hand. It was the first request he had received for something that had not
existed when he began to price it.

In July the signed sentence was published without the larger conclusions
Babbage had proposed for it. He published those interpretations separately,
under his own authority. By December the first inquiry had become four.

The calculation office was constituted in January 1852, in the solicitor's room
where the compact had been signed. Babbage put in six hundred and fifty pounds.
Halden put in a hundred and fifty, most of what his household had saved since
the first venture, and the hundred pounds left unspent from the construction
account made nine hundred. The apparatus came to the office in its frozen
configuration. The stopping clauses were copied from the compact, and every
customer was to receive two signatures beneath each table: the preparer's and
an independent checker's.

Lovelace read the articles at Ockham and returned them with a question
pencilled beside the fourth, which gave the acceptance of customer work to the
manager.

*And who may refuse the manager?*

Halden wrote beneath it, *The account*, and sent the page back. She signed the
article that governed published claims and left the fourth without her name.

By February 1852, Halden's capacity sheet allowed eighty independent
checker-hours in a quarter.

Thomas Neale would not leave an assurance post that carried a pension for an
office a month old. His employer spared him ten hours a week, a hundred and
thirty in a quarter on paper. But late sources, corrected preparations,
customer questions, and ordinary absence consumed the difference. Halden
therefore entered eighty independent checker-hours as the quantity he was
willing to promise. At an average of forty hours per verified packet, the office could
deliver two.

The proposed tables were due between April and June 1854. Customers would close
their accounts at the end of 1853, reconcile them through March, and release
signed returns no earlier than 1 April. Before then, methods and card sequences
could be prepared with specimen or provisional figures. Halden had spread that
work over two years. Neale's final comparison could not begin with figures that
had not arrived.

Four offices wished to place deposits.

Neale had no theory of the general Engine. His knowledge was narrower and, at
that moment, more decisive. He knew how often a neat source concealed an
illegible original, how a correction at the third line required a second reading
of the thirtieth, and how fatigue made familiar figures more dangerous than
strange ones. None of that appeared in the apparatus's operation count.

He had cut Wills a checking strip from a rejected card, the twin of his own.
When the younger man tried to compare a whole column at once, Neale covered
everything below the current line and made him begin again. “A strange figure
stops you,” he said, moving the strip down. “Watch the one you expect.”

Wills read the next line and reached for his pencil. Neale kept the strip where
it was.

“From the source.”

“I was.”

“You were looking here.” He touched the prepared copy.

Wills put the pencil down. At the corresponding place on the specimen sheet the
ink had thickened. He knew what the figure ought to be: the other copy gave it
plainly. He bent closer to the source, then straightened.

“I can't read that one.”

Neale drew the sheet towards the light. For a moment Wills wished he had given
the figure after all; Neale was taking longer over it than he had.

“Nor can I,” Neale said. “Leave it open.”

“Shall I ask for the original?”

“Yes.”

Wills marked the place before moving the strip. The rest of the line remained
unmarked. He had spent the lesson trying to give Neale no reason to stop him;
now he had a question he would have to carry back to the preparation desk.
Neale moved his own chair aside so the younger man could get out.","text":"## IX. Four Deposits

## IX. Four Deposits

The first inquiry arrived before the apparatus was covered. A messenger
brought a letter from an office that had heard the first day's rumour and wished
to know the price of a calculation. Halden turned the unopened letter over in
his hand. It was the first request he had received for something that had not
existed when he began to price it.

In July the signed sentence was published without the larger conclusions
Babbage had proposed for it. He published those interpretations separately,
under his own authority. By December the first inquiry had become four.

The calculation office was constituted in January 1852, in the solicitor's room
where the compact had been signed. Babbage put in six hundred and fifty pounds.
Halden put in a hundred and fifty, most of what his household had saved since
the first venture, and the hundred pounds left unspent from the construction
account made nine hundred. The apparatus came to the office in its frozen
configuration. The stopping clauses were copied from the compact, and every
customer was to receive two signatures beneath each table: the preparer's and
an independent checker's.

Lovelace read the articles at Ockham and returned them with a question
pencilled beside the fourth, which gave the acceptance of customer work to the
manager.

*And who may refuse the manager?*

Halden wrote beneath it, *The account*, and sent the page back. She signed the
article that governed published claims and left the fourth without her name.

By February 1852, Halden's capacity sheet allowed eighty independent
checker-hours in a quarter.

Thomas Neale would not leave an assurance post that carried a pension for an
office a month old. His employer spared him ten hours a week, a hundred and
thirty in a quarter on paper. But late sources, corrected preparations,
customer questions, and ordinary absence consumed the difference. Halden
therefore entered eighty independent checker-hours as the quantity he was
willing to promise. His planning average of forty checker-hours per packet covered the whole
work, including its earlier stages. Two jobs were the limit he was willing
to promise in the delivery quarter.

The proposed tables were due between April and June 1854. Customers would close
their accounts at the end of 1853, reconcile them through March, and release
signed returns no earlier than 1 April. Before then, methods and card sequences
could be prepared with specimen or provisional figures. Halden had spread that
work over two years. Neale's final comparison could not begin with figures that
had not arrived.

Four offices wished to place deposits.

Neale had no theory of the general Engine. His knowledge was narrower and, at
that moment, more decisive. He knew how often a neat source concealed an
illegible original, how a correction at the third line required a second reading

In Halden's new office that February, Babbage held that the estimate described
the office they had, while the deposits described the office they might create.

“We are not dividing eighty hours among four fixed objects, as though hours
were loaves,” he said. “We are using four obligations to purchase more hours.
The railways built themselves on exactly that principle, and nobody asks them
to apologize.”

“From whom?” Lovelace asked.

The office was two rooms adjoining the calculating room. Through the wall came
the intermittent motion of the apparatus. On the table lay four letters and the
capacity sheet. Lovelace had marked one line twice: independent checking, not
preparation, set the boundary.

Halden laid the letters around the capacity sheet. Their corners covered the
marked line.

Halden had advertised for another checker. Two men answered; neither could yet
challenge a prepared set of cards without Neale's supervision, and training
consumed the same scarce hours it was meant to increase.

“The deposits keep Wills paid while Neale trains him,” Halden said.

“The customers require checked tables before Wills can sign one,” Lovelace
said.

“Then we stage the work.”

“I know.” She reached for the capacity sheet. “I mean the final comparison.
When would Neale do it?”

Halden did not answer the question. One letter had called him inventor. He had
corrected the word in his reply, but not before reading the salutation twice.
Now he looked at the four deposits covering the line.

Babbage stood at the apparatus-room door. “The objection assumes that the
present method of checking is fixed for ever, like the tides. A machine exists
precisely to free us from the pace of human repetition. I have argued that for
twenty years, and I did not expect to argue it in this room.”

“It has freed the operation,” Lovelace said. “It has not freed us from deciding
what operation we asked for. If it had, I should go home and leave you both to
it.”

“A second apparatus—”

Halden interrupted him. “Isn't in any contract or any account.”

Halden looked again at the four deposits.

“Four deposits are not four deliveries,” he said. “They pay Wills, retain
Neale, and carry the rent while we stagger preparation. We begin training now
and accept no fifth.”

“Mr Halden has priced every hour by which this office came into being,” Babbage
said. “He does not mistake a receipt for capacity.”

Halden looked up. He was unused to hearing his caution praised by this man.
Before he could think what to say, he had drawn the first letter nearer.

“And Mr Babbage knows which repeated hours the mechanism can remove,” Halden
said. “We began at opposite ends and arrived at four.”

Babbage came back from the doorway and drew out a chair.

Halden drew the letters inward until their edges made a square. One corner
remained over the line Lovelace had marked.

Lovelace asked Neale to join them. He stood awkwardly at the end of the table
while Halden described the schedule.

“Four packets at forty hours make a hundred and sixty over the whole work,”
she said. “Can you check them independently by the final dates?”

“Not if all four require the hours in the account.”

“Could they require less?” Babbage said.

Neale began to answer, stopped, and put the blank strip beneath the total.
“Some will. Some will not. I have eighty hours, sir. If I spend them teaching
Wills, I cannot enter them again here as his independent check.”

No one altered the figure. Some work could be done before the returns, but
the sheet did not show that the final comparisons would fit within the
quarter’s eighty hours.

Lovelace asked that her objection be entered with the capacity sheet. Babbage
would support the four. Neither could sign a customer's acceptance for Halden.

Halden held the office pen. He dated the first acceptance and laid it aside for
the second. By the fourth he no longer looked at the capacity sheet. He checked
the customer's name, the deposit, and the delivery date. All three were
correct. He initialled it and laid down the pen.
